ACH.name: Backing to Retake Constantinople
ACH.desc: Although the has since been destroyed by the, recent crusader state campaigns in Greece have encouraged sponsorship to restore the empire.
mods: Can Create Latin Reconquest casus belli

ACH.name: Titular Rulers of the Latin Empire
ACH.desc: Although we have since lost control of Constantinople, the seat of power for the, our claim to it still remains as strong as ever.
mods: Can Create Latin Reconquest casus belli

ACH.name: A System of Forts
ACH.desc: Our coastal defenses are unmatched, utilizing Italian Trace Italienne design to repel enemy naval raids and incursions into our sovereign territory. We have transformed the old Crusader castles into modern artillery forts, capable of withstanding months of siege while projecting power over the Ionian and Aegean seas. No invader shall take the Morea by sea so long as our stone sentinels stand watch over the rocky capes and fertile valleys.

ACH.name: Achaean Enlightenment
ACH.desc: As scholars flee the crumbling peripheries of the East, many find refuge in our courts, leading to a unique synthesis of Latin philosophy and Greek classical knowledge. Under the enlightened patronage of the Princes, we have established academies where the works of the great sages of both East and West are studied side-by-side, sparking a cultural rebirth. This intellectual flowering attracts the best minds of Europe, ensuring our state remains at the cutting edge of administrative and scientific progress.

ACH.name: Assizes of Romania
ACH.desc: The feudal laws of the Frankish East are the most refined in the Catholic world, having been codified to manage a complex web of Greek serfs and French lords. These Assizes provide a clear legal framework for land disputes, inheritance, and military obligations, ensuring that even in times of war, the social order remains unbreakable. Rigorous adherence to these laws prevents the internal fractures that destroyed the first Crusader states, providing a rock-solid foundation for governance.

ACH.name: Knights of the Peloponnese
ACH.desc: Our nobility has spent centuries in constant border skirmishes against our enemies, creating a unique tradition of highly mobile cavalry. These knights have discarded the cumbersome barding of their French ancestors in favor of lighter armor and tactics adapted for the steep, treacherous Greek mountains. This allows our forces to outmaneuver traditional heavy cavalry and strike at the enemy's flanks with devastating speed and precision.

ACH.name: Morean Silk
ACH.desc: The Peloponnese remains the heart of European silk production, a legacy of the Byzantine era that the Frankish Princes have expanded through state-sponsored mulberry groves. By controlling strategic ports, we can undercut the high prices of Persian and Chinese imports, making Achaea the primary supplier for the garment makers of Florence and Lyon. This monopoly provides a steady stream of Soft Gold that funds our mercenaries and the fortification of our mountain passes.

ACH.name: Villehardouin's Valor
ACH.desc: Geoffrey of Villehardouin, marshal of Champagne and eyewitness chronicler of the Fourth Crusade, composed one of the earliest vernacular histories in Old French, immortalizing the deeds of his companions and the astonishing capture of Constantinople in vivid, heroic prose that circulated widely among the nobility of Western Europe. His chronicle served not only as a record but as propaganda and inspiration, rallying fresh knights and pilgrims to reinforce the beleaguered Latin states, while fostering a shared sense of chivalric brotherhood among the scattered Frankish lords who continued to view themselves as crusaders holding God's frontier against schismatic and infidel alike long after the original host had dispersed. It is time to recover that spirit for the challenges of our army.

ALB.name: Angevin Legitimacy
ALB.desc: Our latest crowned heads can be traced directly to the lineage of the Capetian House of Anjou, specifically established by Charles I of Naples to serve as his gateway into the Byzantine heartlands. This connection grants us a unique Western prestige among the fragmented Balkan lords, allowing us to claim a seat at the table of the great Catholic monarchs of Europe. By upholding the honors and heraldry of the Lily, we distinguish our sovereignty from that of mere tribal chieftains.

ALB.name: Diplomacy of the Two Shores
ALB.desc: Our position allows us to act as the essential bridge between the Italian city-states and the rugged Balkan interior. Our diplomats are trained to navigate both the Venetian Senate and tribal councils, making our mediation indispensable for trade and war.

ALB.name: Eastern and Western Heritage
ALB.desc: Our urban centers continue to operate under both the sophisticated principles of Byzantine Law and the modern bureaucracies of the West. This legal continuity provides a stable framework for contracts, property rights, and inheritance that attracts foreign merchants and scholars to our courts. A predictable legal system is the foundation of our growing administrative strength.

ALB.name: Enlightened Albanian Absolutism
ALB.desc: Following the European trend, our monarchs have centralized power, stripping the old clans of their feudal privileges in favor of a modern state. This move has allowed us to implement universal taxation and a national judicial system, turning the kingdom into a streamlined machine of war.

ALB.name: The Albanian Merchant Class
ALB.desc: The merchants of our coast have become the primary carriers of trade between the Balkans and the West. By utilizing the Greek language for commerce and Albanian for loyalty, they dominate the markets from Venice to Constantinople. These merchant marines are the lifeblood of our modernizing economy.

ALB.name: The Arbëreshë Diaspora
ALB.desc: Over time, a good number of our people have emigrated abroad and formed Arbëreshë communities. These 'Albanians across the sea' maintain our language and traditions while gaining influence in their new homes. They serve as permanent diplomatic envoys there, constantly lobbying for support for the homeland.

ALB.name: The Arbërian Principality
ALB.desc: As the power of our foes wanes, our great houses have united to ensure the survival of our nation. By making the most of our position between the Catholic West and the Orthodox East, we have become masters of maritime diplomacy and coastal trade. This strategic autonomy allows us to navigate the rivalries of neighbors to our own benefit.

ALB.name: The Catholic Bulwark
ALB.desc: Positioned as the easternmost outpost of the Roman Church, we have become the primary shield against both Orthodox schismatics and Turkish heathens. Our sacred duty brings an inner peace that infuses the entire realm and turns our struggle into a crusade for our soul.

ALB.name: The Champion of Christ
ALB.desc: Despite our communities being divided by faith, our nation is devoted to Christ, earning us the title of Athleta Christi. Our relentless faith has drawn the eyes of the Papacy and the Patriarchs, securing us financial subsidies and military volunteers. We fight not just for our land, but for the very survival of the 'Word of Christ'.
mods: Damage Done versus Heathens in Battle

ALB.name: The Expansion of the Regnum
ALB.desc: We will not rest until the borders of the ancient Kingdom are restored to their greatest extent and beyond, reclaiming our place as masters of the Balkans. This centralizing mission allows us to integrate newly conquered territories with little resistance as we restore 'rightful' rule.

ALB.name: The National Arsenal
ALB.desc: As the primary port for Western intervention, we have modernized the shipyards of Durrës to maintain a permanent fleet of galleys. This infrastructure allows us to project power across the Adriatic, ensuring that the sea lanes between Naples and Albania remain open for reinforcements and trade. Our control of the harbor makes us the undisputed masters of the western Balkan coastline.

ALB.name: The Spirit of the Rilindja
ALB.desc: Our 'National Rebirth' or Rilindja has ignited a fire in the hearts of Albanians everywhere, from the mountains of the north to the diaspora in Italy and Egypt. This cultural and political movement has unified all Albanians under the common banner of 'Albanianism'. We are a nation reborn, ready to take our place among the sovereign states of Europe.

ANR.name: Co-Principality Structure
ANR.desc: The land of Andorra is governed under a unique constitutional arrangement: the joint sovereignty of two co-princes, the Bishop of Urgell and the Count of Foix, whose competing claims have paradoxically produced a stable equilibrium. Neither sovereign can act without the consent of the other, and this mutual check has preserved Andorra from absorption by either neighbor. We have formalized this co-principality structure as the constitutional foundation of our realm, accepting the limitations it places on unilateral action in exchange for the diplomatic shelter it provides.

ANR.name: Consell de la Terra
ANR.desc: The Consell de la Terra is the assembly representing the six parishes of Andorra, established to oversee the affairs of the land and protect the ancient rights of its communities against the encroachments of either co-prince.

ANR.name: Quartons
ANR.desc: The six parishes of Andorra govern themselves through elected councils called quartons, which administer local affairs and send representatives to the Consell de la Terra. This ancient system of communal self-rule limits the direct reach of the co-princes into the daily life of our communities.

ANR.name: Síndic General
ANR.desc: The Síndic General is the elected representative of the Andorran community, charged with defending the collective interests of the parishes before both co-princes and serving as the head of our communal administration.

ANR.name: Pareatges
ANR.desc: The co-principality's founding charter divides sovereignty between two lords, defining the legal basis of Andorran governance and the obligations each suzerain holds to the land and its people.

ANR.name: Charter Entrenched
ANR.desc: The co-principality's constitutional framework is further entrenched, with legal structures deepened and local governance given firmer roots — the suzerains' reach is limited, but the realm's internal order grows stronger for it.

ANR.name: Charter Upheld
ANR.desc: The Pareatges are honored in full, with both suzerains recognized and their respective rights respected — a careful balance that preserves Andorran autonomy and keeps the realm's external relationships stable.

ANR.name: Manual Digest
ANR.desc: A systematic manual compiled by the co-principality's jurists codifies Andorran customary law, providing clear precedent for the valleys' courts and reinforcing the realm's enduring legal traditions.

ANR.name: La Questia
ANR.desc: Our annual tribute to the co-princes, the Questia, is paid in alternating years to the Bishop of Urgell and the Count of Foix, a sum that has remained nominally fixed for centuries while our valley economies have grown substantially. The modest scale of the sum, combined with the deflation of its real value over time, allows our parish councils to fund themselves through local revenue. This favorable fiscal settlement frees court spending for public works and the ceremonial obligations of statecraft rather than on tribute paid to outside powers.

ANR.name: Neutralitat Pirinenca
ANR.desc: Our policy of Neutralitat Pirinenca (Pyrenean neutrality) keeps Andorra clear of the great wars that consume our larger neighbors, our valleys serving instead as a refuge for political exiles, smugglers, dynastic claimants in transit, and the occasional troubadour whose sudden popularity has rendered his home kingdom's tax gatherers uncomfortably attentive. Both co-princes find the arrangement convenient enough that they spare us from any formal alignment with their wider conflicts. This neutral reputation makes our envoys welcome at conferences from which combatant states are excluded and gives our small army the time to prepare defensive positions no aggressor cares to assault.

ANR.name: Pau dels Dos Coprínceps
ANR.desc: The Pau dels Dos Coprínceps (the perpetual peace agreed between the Bishop of Urgell and the Count of Foix in the paréage of 1278) establishes Andorra as a dual sovereignty in which neither prince may act in our valleys without the consent of the other. Our diplomats learn from the start that every external relationship must be balanced against the watchful eye of a second prince, breeding habits of careful drafting and patient negotiation rare in courts that answer to a single sovereign. This dual-headed sovereignty teaches our envoys to extract more from foreign courts than the size of our delegation alone could ever justify.

ANR.name: Sis Parròquies
ANR.desc: The Sis Parròquies (Canillo, Encamp, Ordino, La Massana, Andorra la Vella, and Sant Julià de Lòria) each send representatives to the Consell de la Terra to deliberate on taxation, public works, and the customary law that governs our valleys. Decisions taken in council bind every parish equally, and the parishes in turn administer their own commons, irrigation, and dispute resolution without sending matters to the co-princes for routine governance. This parish level self-government keeps the costs of administering our Crown remarkably low and gives every household a direct voice in the policies they live under.

ANR.name: Síndic Procurador General
ANR.desc: Our Síndic Procurador General presides over the Consell de la Terra and acts as the executive face of Andorra before the two co-princes, negotiating on behalf of the parishes without ever surrendering the council's ultimate sovereignty over their own affairs. The síndic is chosen by consensus among the parish representatives, typically a respected churchman or notable, and serves as a permanent buffer between local interests and external pressure. This neutral mediator role keeps both clergy and nobility committed to the council's decisions and limits the factionalism that more partisan executives produce.

ANR.name: Via dels Passos
ANR.desc: The high passes connecting our valleys to French Ariège and Catalan Urgell (the Port d'Envalira, the Coll de la Botella, and the Port de Cabús) are maintained year-round by parish corvée labor that clears rockfalls, marks the snow stakes, and stocks the refuge huts that allow military and commercial traffic through. Centuries of mountain road building have produced a corps of parish engineers who can move men and supplies across alpine terrain in conditions that defeat lowland armies. This command of the high passes lets our small forces concentrate against intruders faster than any flatland army can reposition.

ANR.name: Mediate between the Co-Princes
ANR.desc: We engage in delicate diplomatic correspondence between the two co-princes of Andorra — the Bishop of Urgell and the Count of Foix — whose competing claims must be continuously balanced. Skillful mediation boosts our diplomatic standing, earns prestige, and keeps the principality's fragile governance stable.

ANT.name: Arianiti's Defiance
ANT.desc: Following the heroic example of our leaders, our house is known as the first to rise and the last to surrender against our foes. This legacy of unyielding resistance has forged our people into a nation of warriors who see struggle as a sacred duty rather than a burden.

ANT.name: Born in the Highlands
ANT.desc: Our ancestral home in the highlands of our nation is a natural citadel of jagged peaks and narrow ravines that is nearly impossible for a conventional army to navigate. We have further fortified every strategic pass and mountain peak, ensuring that any enemy invader must pay a staggering price in blood for every inch of our territory they attempt to occupy.

ANT.name: Patronage of the Faith
ANT.desc: By providing significant land grants and funds to our monasteries, we maintain the spiritual loyalty of the nobility and the peasantry. These sacred sites serve as the cultural heart of our principality, where our victories are celebrated.

ANT.name: The Eternal Resistance
ANT.desc: We have sworn an eternal oath that so long as we breathe, the heart of the rebellion will continue to beat. Our troops are drilled with a fanatical devotion to our ruling house, ensuring they maintain discipline even in the face of overwhelming imperial numbers.

ANT.name: The Iron Mines of the Interior
ANT.desc: The rugged mountains of central Albania under our control are rich in high-quality iron ore essential for the tools of war. We have established state-sponsored smelters to provide our clans with a constant supply of superior steel blades and armor plates, ensuring we are never dependent on foreign imports to equip our growing armies.

ANT.name: The Professional Highland Grenadiers
ANT.desc: We have evolved our traditional skirmishers into elite mountain grenadier units, specialized in heavy assault and siege warfare. These troops combine their ancestral mountain agility with the devastating firepower of modern explosives, making them the terror of any fortress garrison.

AQU.name: Alpine Defense
AQU.desc: Our territory sits at the junction of the Julian Alps and the Karst plateau, a landscape that provides natural defensive advantages to those who know how to use it and proves lethal to armies that do not. We invest in the fortification of the key passes and valley approaches, training our garrison forces to hold terrain rather than meet the enemy in open ground, and establishing a network of signal stations that ensures no advance can reach us without warning. This system of Difesa Alpina makes our territory one of the most costly to invade in the region, converting the rugged landscape into an ally that inflicts losses on any hostile force before our own soldiers need to engage.

AQU.name: Friulian Soldiery
AQU.desc: The Friulian countryside has always been a frontier, and the men raised on its farmsteads and in its market towns carry a soldier's habits from youth, accustomed to bearing arms, experienced in the local terrain, and under no illusions about what happens to those who cannot defend themselves on a border that hostile powers have crossed many times. We formalize this martial tradition by organizing, equipping, and training the Milizia Friulana on a professional footing, giving these experienced men the discipline and the leadership that converts their individual hardiness into a reliable military force. Our armies gain a core of steady infantry who fight for their own soil and hold their ground with a tenacity that mercenaries rarely show.

AQU.name: The Amber Road
AQU.desc: Long before the Roman legions formalized it, the route that carried Baltic amber from the northern seas down to the Adriatic ran through our territory, making Aquileia one of the great entrepôts of the ancient world and establishing trade habits that outlasted the empire which later paved the road. We revive and invest in this corridor, improving the roads and staging posts that connect our city to the Alpine passes and the trading networks beyond them, ensuring that our merchants can reach markets to the north with greater efficiency than any rival route. This control over the Amber Road multiplies our diplomatic reach and makes our trading lanes the preferred route for goods moving between the Adriatic and central Europe.

AQU.name: The Enlightened Patriarchate
AQU.desc: The memory of Aquileia as a crossroads between west and east, between the Roman and the Slavic worlds, and between the Latin and the Germanic, has given our institutions an instinctive openness to ideas from outside that more homogeneous states can struggle to achieve. We build on this tradition by welcoming the scholars and administrators produced by the Enlightenment into our governing institutions, reforming our laws by the same principles of reason and evidence that the patriarchate once applied to canon law in a different era. This spirit of the Patriarcato illuminato earns our state a reputation as a place where ideas are taken seriously and institutions are genuinely open to improvement, drawing scholars and skilled administrators whose presence accelerates every reform we attempt.

AQU.name: The Patriarchal Legacy
AQU.desc: For centuries, the patriarchs of Aquileia administered a territory that stretched from the Adriatic coast to the Alpine passes, managing ecclesiastical law, civil disputes, and diplomatic relations with secular powers simultaneously, an administrative experience that accumulated in our institutions long after the patriarchate's temporal power was absorbed by Venice. We draw on this heritage to rationalize and improve our own machinery of government, applying the procedural knowledge of an institution that once governed a far larger and more complex territory to the more manageable scale of our current state. This Patriarchal Legacy of administrative sophistication makes our cabinet more effective and our legislation more coherent, giving us a strength in government that belies the modest size of our domain.

AQU.name: The Patriarchate of Aquileia
AQU.desc: Aquileia was once the fourth city of the Roman Empire and later the seat of a patriarchate that claimed authority over the whole of northeastern Italy and the eastern Alps, a tradition of ecclesiastical prestige that lingered in our institutions long after the political power that created it had passed. We draw on this heritage to build institutions of learning that reflect the city's ancient role as a center of transmission between the Latin west and the Slavic and Germanic east. This tradition of the Patriarchate of Aquileia as a crossroads of cultures and books gives our state an unusual depth of literacy and a tolerance rooted in centuries of managing Christians of different rites under a single ecclesiastical roof.

ARA.name: Crown of Aragon
ARA.desc: The Crown of Aragon is a composite realm formed by several kingdoms and a principality, each with their own institutions and laws. As a trade and seafaring-oriented confederation, it represents extraordinary naval power, primed to dominate the Mediterranean with its fleets.

ARA.name: Formalized Oath of Loyalty
ARA.desc: The monarchy is bound by a formalized agreement that requires the rights and freedoms of the estates to be recognized and upheld before an oath of loyalty can be sworn.

ARA.name: General Privilege of Aragon
ARA.desc: The General Privilege is a list of deals and laws that compels the monarch to guarantee traditional nobiliary rights and to ask for the parliament's permission before declaring war.

ARA.name: Justicia de Aragón
ARA.desc: Justicia de Aragón is a powerful legal and judicial office in the, established to uphold regional laws, mediate disputes, and protect the rights of subjects against royal overreach.

ARA.name: Consulate of the Sea
ARA.desc: The Consulate of the Sea is a new quasi-judicial body that will administer maritime and commercial law.
mods: Unlocks the Fondaco rights relation type

ARA.name: Basílica del Pilar
ARA.desc: At Zaragoza rises the great baroque Basílica del Pilar, raised over the pillar where tradition holds the Virgin appeared to Saint James, drawing pilgrims from across the Spains. The crown endows its chapter, processes beneath its towers on the great feasts, and wraps its legitimacy in the most venerable Marian devotion of the peninsula. This sacral prestige binds clergy and commons to the dynasty and sanctifies the kingdom's rule as no mere law could.

ARA.name: Cariñena Vineyards
ARA.desc: The stony terraces of Cariñena and Campo de Borja, baked by the dry interior sun and swept by the cierzo wind, yield a dark, powerful wine prized far beyond the kingdom. Monastic cellars and town guilds expand the plantings across the Ebro depression, and the vintage travels by river and mule to the courts and garrisons of the crown. This robust viticulture turns thin upland soil into one of the inland kingdom's most valuable and durable exports.

ARA.name: Conquest of the Ebro
ARA.desc: The descent from the Pyrenean valleys onto the plain of the Ebro crowns generations of frontier war: Huesca falls in 1096, and Alfonso el Batallador storms Zaragoza in 1118 to make it the seat of the kingdom. Our light frontier foot soldiers, hardened in the long march south and skilled in the reduction of walled Moorish towns, turns each captured stronghold into a base for the next advance. Our soldiery are built for taking fortresses, not for the sea.

ARA.name: Dinero Jaqués
ARA.desc: Minted at Jaca since the first kings of Aragon, the dinero jaqués becomes the trusted coin of the kingdom, its silver content guarded by the Cortes against every royal temptation to debase it. A sound currency lets the crown borrow cheaply, the merchants reckon honestly, and the treasury may collect its revenues without the friction of clipped and doubtful coin. This monetary stability underwrites the kingdom's finances more reliably than any single tax.

ARA.name: Diputación del General
ARA.desc: Our kingdom's standing executive, the Diputación del General, emerges from the Cortes of Monzón as a permanent commission that administers the general subsidio, defends the realm's fueros between Cortes sessions, and represents the four estates in continuous dialogue with the Crown. We will channel the kingdom's tax revenue through the Diputación's accounting offices, fund public works through its commissions, and lodge the noble houses' grievances in its standing chamber. Because the Diputación never adjourns, our realm keeps its parliamentary memory and its accounts in order, while the Crown's other realms must start afresh each session.

ARA.name: Zaragoza Industry
ARA.desc: Zaragoza and the towns of the Ebro corridor fill with sugar refineries, flour mills, foundries, and rail workshops as the inland kingdom enters the industrial age. The Imperial Canal's water, the new lines linking the city to the Cantabrian coast and the Mediterranean, and a steady migration off the land feed a growing manufacturing economy. This industrial awakening lifts the once-agrarian heartland into a producing region rivaling the old coastal centers.
mods: Monthly Prosperity in towns and cities

ARA.name: Unite The Dynasty
ARA.desc: With the Sicilian Vespers securing the throne for our dynasty, our influence in Italy has grown. Despite this, Sicily still maintains its sovereignty, distancing itself from our dynastic politics. Rather than allowing this opportunity to pass us by, perhaps we can contact our relatives there, establishing a stronger dynastic union and potentially kickstarting our ambitions in Italy.

ARG.name: Backing to Retake Constantinople
ARG.desc: Although the has since been destroyed by the, recent crusader state campaigns in Greece have encouraged sponsorship to restore the empire.
mods: Can Create Latin Reconquest casus belli

ARG.name: Dominance of the Catalan Company
ARG.desc: Since the seizure of the, the Catalan Company has projected considerable military influence over Greece.

ARG.name: Argive Maritime Insurance
ARG.desc: Capitalizing on our position as a safe harbor, the merchant houses of Nauplia have developed a sophisticated system of maritime insurance and risk sharing for Aegean trade. By guaranteeing the safety of Latin cargoes against piracy and storms, we have turned our port into the financial safe haven of the Peloponnese. This early form of financial capitalism draws capital away from the larger Italian republics and concentrates it in our own local banks.

ARG.name: The Artillery School of Argos
ARG.desc: Recognizing that the future of warfare is determined by the cannon, we have turned our high-altitude forts into laboratories for ballistics and gunnery. Our officers are trained to calculate firing arcs from extreme heights, allowing our batteries to hit enemy ships with pinpoint accuracy. The Argos School of Gunnery is respected across Europe for its mathematical precision and tactical innovation.

ARG.name: The Curia of the Two Benches
ARG.desc: In a daring move toward social stability, the Lordship has reformed the high court of Nauplia into the Curia of the Two Benches. This judicial body requires that every civil case involving land or inheritance be heard by a panel consisting of one Frankish judge and one Greek Demogeron (Elder). By institutionalizing this 'Shared Justice', we have effectively ended the centuries-old legal friction between the Latin and Orthodox populations. This governance model has created a unique 'Argive Identity' that is fiercely loyal to the Lordship, protecting the state from the revolutionary fervors sweeping through the rest of Europe.

ARG.name: The Gibraltar of the Levant
ARG.desc: The Palamidi fortress, perched high above the Gulf of Argos, has been expanded into a complex system of seven interlocking forts that command the entire Argolid. By controlling this 'Gibraltar', we dictate the movement of any fleet attempting to supply an army in the Morea, effectively making the lordship unconquerable by land or sea. This strategic dominance allows us to play the role of kingmaker between our neighbors.

ARG.name: The Heraldry of the Brienne
ARG.desc: As the House of Brienne maintains claims to Jerusalem and Cyprus, Argos has become a center for 'Chivalric Genealogy'. Knights from across the West come here to prove their lineage or seek titles in the 'crusader fringe'. A constant stream of high-born adventurers keeps our local levies supplied with talented officers.

ARG.name: The Peloponnesian Diplomatic Hub
ARG.desc: Because Argos is the most neutral and secure port in the Peloponnese, it has become the preferred meeting ground for the ambassadors of the Latin states. We have established a permanent 'Diplomatic Quarter' where treaties are negotiated and alliances are forged between the Frankish lords and the Great Powers. As a mediator between the great powers, we are too useful to be swallowed by our larger neighbors.

ARM.name: Highland Fortresses
ARM.desc: Our fortresses are a brilliant emblem of our resilience and fortitude, built to endure not only the difficult local climate, but also any foreign invader foolish enough to mount an attack into our unforgiving territory.

ATH.name: Backing to Retake Constantinople
ATH.desc: Although the has since been destroyed by the, recent crusader state campaigns in Greece have encouraged sponsorship to restore the empire.
mods: Can Create Latin Reconquest casus belli

ATH.name: Dominance of the Catalan Company
ATH.desc: Since the seizure of the, the Catalan Company has projected considerable military influence over Greece.

ATH.name: The Athenian Bureaucracy
ATH.desc: As our rulers transitioned toward absolute rule, they replaced the fractious feudal lords with a meritocratic civil service drawn from the urban bourgeoisie. This centralized administration ensures that taxes are collected efficiently and the ruler's law is enforced uniformly from Marathon to Megara. By breaking the power of the old baronial families, our nation has become a streamlined, modern state capable of rapid mobilization.

ATH.name: The Attican Gunpowder Mills
ATH.desc: Our artillery is now the finest in the world, benefiting from the metallurgical secrets of the world's renowned master smiths and the chemical innovations of our local alchemists. The 'Thunder of Athens' is heard across the Balkans, as our cannons are prized for their range and reliability.

ATH.name: The Catalan Company
ATH.desc: After being hired and then betrayed by the Byzantine emperor, the ferocious Catalan Grand Company turned against their former paymasters and, in 1311, annihilated the Frankish duke Walter V of Brienne at the Battle of the Cephissus, seizing control of the Duchy of Athens and establishing a period of Catalan rule. These battle-hardened Almogàvers introduced a more ruthless mercenary ethos to Greek affairs, fortifying key strongholds, extracting tribute from the countryside, and maintaining their grip through a combination of terror and disciplined infantry tactics until internal strife and Aragonese intervention eventually shifted power back toward a more conventional feudal regime.

ATH.name: The Parthenon Dukes
ATH.desc: Otto de la Roche, first Duke of Athens, established his court amid the ruins of the Acropolis, converting the ancient Parthenon into a Catholic cathedral dedicated to Our Lady while ruling over a duchy that stretched from Attica to Boeotia. Under his successors, the duchy became a surprising center of cultural exchange where Frankish knights patronized Greek scribes, Italian merchants traded in Piraeus, and scholars debated philosophy in sight of marble temples. All this produced a distinctive aristocratic society that prized both the martial virtues of chivalry and an appreciation for the Hellenic past that had so long been ignored by Western conquerors. We must reinstate this court to its past glory.

ATH.name: The Piraeus Arsenal
ATH.desc: Modeled after the Venetian Arsenal but utilizing modern assembly line techniques, our new dockyards at Piraeus can produce a fully equipped war galley in a matter of weeks. This industrialization of naval warfare allows the small Duchy to punch far above its weight class, maintaining a professional navy that dominates the Saronic Gulf. The Piraeus is no longer a ruin, but the most modern naval base in the Eastern Mediterranean.

ATH.name: Thebes' Textiles
ATH.desc: The workshops of Thebes, already renowned in Byzantine times for their silk weaving, have flourished anew under Frankish rule as the dukes of Athens encourage Italian merchants to invest in looms, dyeworks, and export networks that carry Theban samites and velvets to markets from Bruges to Alexandria. This revival of luxury textile production, combined with the fertile plains of Boeotia that supply raw materials, generate substantial wealth that funds castle building, knightly retinues, and the lavish lifestyle of the Athenian court, ensuring that the duchy remains one of the richest and most economically sophisticated territories of the entire Frankokratia.

BAM.name: Fürspang Society
BAM.desc: The Gesellschaft mit dem Fürspang is an order of knights formed to defend their interests and provide assistance to those who sponsor them. Providing them with extensive funds will grant us significantly more political prowess within our region and within the Holy Roman Empire.

BAM.name: Fürspang Society
BAM.desc: The Gesellschaft mit dem Fürspang is an order of knights formed to defend their interests and provide assistance to those who sponsor them. Providing them with extensive funds will grant us significantly more political prowess within our region and within the Holy Roman Empire.

BDE.name: Society with the Donkey
BDE.desc: Founded to protect knightly interests within the Empire, the Gesellschaft mit dem Esel has entrenched itself in the lands surrounding Heidelberg. Their expertise in governance, as well as their ability to sponsor tourneys, will improve our cultural standing.

BDE.name: Society with the Donkey
BDE.desc: Founded to protect knightly interests within the Empire, the Gesellschaft mit dem Esel has entrenched itself in the lands surrounding Heidelberg. Their expertise in governance, as well as their ability to sponsor tourneys, will improve our cultural standing.

BLG.name: Galvanism
BLG.desc: The University of Bologna remains at the cutting edge of the Enlightenment. The discovery of animal electricity in a Bolognese laboratory has laid the groundwork for modern bio-electricity and physics. This spirit of inquiry will turn the city into a hub for early industrial and scientific pioneers, bridging the gap between ancient scholasticism and the modern laboratory.

BLG.name: L'Académia di Incaminè
BLG.desc: As the wild energy of the Renaissance cools, education is shifting toward organized Academies. These are state-sponsored institutions for scientists, writers, and painters, whose aim is to reform art education by moving away from Mannerism toward naturalism and life drawing. These reforms will allow the state to direct artistic and scientific production toward national prestige, leading to the birth of the 'Bolognese School' of painting, which will dominate European tastes for decades.

BLG.name: La Grâsa
BLG.desc: Through the fertile bounty of the Po Valley and the mastery of the Bolognese guilds, our capital will earn a reputation for unparalleled opulence and a second nickname: La Grâsa (or La Grassa, the Fat One, in standard Italian). By investing in the Quadrilatero markets and the production of refined meats and pastas, we will ensure that every traveler leaves with a full stomach and a lighter purse.

BLG.name: La Råssa
BLG.desc: La Råssa (the Red, or La Rossa in standard Italian), as Bologna is also known, celebrates the crimson soul of our skyline; the ancient terracotta brickwork and the defensive sea of red rooftops seen from the Asinelli Tower inspire awe in our subjects and defiance against our foes. Red is becoming so associated with our city that we must start creating laws to make sure that anything not currently in our preferred palette is rebuilt in red terracotta as soon as possible.

BLG.name: The Bolognese School of Music
BLG.desc: Bologna will become the center of development for the concerto and the professionalization of the orchestra. By abandoning the unpredictable modal traditions of the past, we will establish the rigid architectural laws of modern major-minor tonality. This synthesis will transform the violin from a folk instrument into the primary voice of the Baroque era, standardizing the Trio Sonata and the Concerto Grosso. This apparent simplicity will soon become the benchmark of prestige, spreading from Italian cathedrals to the most distant European courts. It will also represent the final transition from the experimental Renaissance to the era of disciplined, instrumental virtuosity.

BLG.name: The Dòta
BLG.desc: Bologna became the intellectual laboratory of Europe with the rise of its organized university, the oldest in the world, earning the nickname of La Dòta (La Dotta in standard Italian: the Learned). Culturally, this moved the society away from feudal trial-by-combat toward a civilian jurisprudence based on recovered Roman Law. This produced a class of professional lay notaries and judges who could manage complex urban administrations, giving Bologna an administration unmatched in its skill.

BOD.name: Guardians of the Thermopylae
BOD.desc: Our fief sits upon the most famous pass in history, and we have taken the lessons of Leonidas to heart by fortifying the mountain tracks with Frankish stone. Every narrow path is a deathtrap for the invader, and every cliffside is a vantage point for our archers and scouts. To pass through Bodonitsa is to run a gauntlet of steel, ensuring that the heart of Greece remains shielded from northern threats.

BOD.name: The Alpine Skirmishers
BOD.desc: Living among the crags of Mount Kallidromos, our people have developed a form of light infantry combat that emphasizes vertical mobility and the use of the crossbow. These 'Mountaineers of the Pass' can disappear into the rocks after a volley, making them impossible for traditional heavy infantry to engage. They serve as the eyes and ears of the southern states, providing early warning of any movement from the north.

BOD.name: The Curia of the Three Keys
BOD.desc: To manage the wealth generated by the resurgence of the northern trade routes, the Marquisate has established the Curia of the Three Keys. The state treasury and the legal archives are locked in the citadel of Bodonitsa, requiring three separate keys held by the Marquis, the Latin Bishop, and a representative of the local Greek burgesses. This primitive but effective system of 'Checks and Balances' prevents the embezzlement that often plagues small feudal states, ensuring that the heavy tolls collected at Thermopylae are actually spent on the fortress walls.

BOD.name: The Maritime Consulates
BOD.desc: Reflecting our Venetian heritage, we have established consulates in the major ports of Euboea and Attica to represent the interests of Bodonitsan merchants. These offices act as intelligence hubs, funneling information about naval movements directly to the Marquis. We may be a mountain state, but our eyes are always fixed on the horizon of the sea.

BOD.name: The Oeta Riflemen
BOD.desc: In the age of gunpowder, the rugged woodsmen of the Oeta mountains have been organized into specialized light infantry corps. These riflemen excel in hit-and-run tactics, using the steep terrain to harass invading columns with lethal precision. They are the nightmare of any general attempting to force the northern passes of Greece.

BOD.name: The Spercheios Civil Chancellery
BOD.desc: The Marquisate of Bodonitsa had evolved from a mere frontier watchtower into the administrative nerve center of Central Greece, necessitating a transition from feudal whim to a professionalized civil service. The establishment of the Great Chancellery overlooking the Spercheios valley signals a move toward a centralized, modern state where the old Frankish baronial privileges are replaced by a cadre of legally trained 'Civil Knights' who manage the complex tolls and land registries of the Phocian heartland.

BOH.name: Commonwealth
BOH.desc: The Commonwealth represents a reformed constitution of the realm, giving more privileges and freedom to the various nations living within our borders.

BOH.name: Inaugural Diplomas
BOH.desc: In a bid to forge strong ties with the elite members of our society, we have granted them a series of benefits under the agreement of the Inaugural Diplomas. Among the concessions are reduced levy obligations to the Crown and the right to reduced taxation.

BOH.name: Maiestas Carolina
BOH.desc: A set of laws and articles, drafted to greatly curb the power of the Nobility. The code entails the passing of noble property to the state in certain circumstances, as well as limiting the arbitrary powers of the Nobility throughout our realm.

BOH.name: Wagenburg
BOH.desc: During the Hussite Wars, our armies relied on wagon forts called Wagenburg to win battles against superior forces. While we may not always deploy wagons, the principle remains: infantry sharpshooters fighting from prepared defensive positions become our standard doctrine.

BOH.name: Bohemian Crystal
BOH.desc: There are very few workshops in the known world with the capacity to craft glass and crystal with the same quality and clarity as ours, let alone rival our superior production techniques.

BOH.name: Bohemian Holy Roman Standing
BOH.desc: Our place within the Holy Roman Empire is one of prestige, grandeur, and authority. Few members wield as much soft power as us, due to our capable diplomats and alliance networks.

BOH.name: Bohemian Thaler
BOH.desc: For years, the standard currency in our country has been the groschen, a coin made of silver and used all throughout the Holy Roman Empire. The discovery of new sources of silver allows us to create another kind of bigger coin, the thaler, also called 'toler' or 'daler', which will become strong and influential enough to dominate all trade and become a new standard.

BOH.name: Fortified Towns
BOH.desc: Through the ravages of the Hussite Wars, and in an effort to safeguard our faith and people, we funded many fortified towns. Since then, we have gained great expertise in erecting fortifications and engineering impenetrable defenses.

BOH.name: Hussite Traditions
BOH.desc: Through struggle and brotherhood, the adherents of our faith withstand all external conversion pressures. Our unshaken religious roots, stemming from ancient teachings, ring true to the hearts of all those who seek to protect their beliefs and live in peace alongside their fellow Christian faithful.

BOH.name: Students of Foreign Courts
BOH.desc: Members of our royal dynasties are accustomed to journeys abroad. They have spent much of their upbringing as students of illustrious courts far away from home, in the pursuit of a thorough education in matters of statesmanship.

BOH.name: The Kutnohorian Deal
BOH.desc: The nobility will always be rather sensitive about protecting their privileges. It would go far towards winning their loyalty if said privileges were to be guaranteed forever.

BOH.name: Urbanization Decrees
BOH.desc: As part of our efforts to modernize Prague, we will issue grants encouraging prominent figures to relocate their business to the capital while offering privileges to attract skilled and wealthy foreign immigrants. This influx of talent and capital will transform our Prague into a thriving, cosmopolitan metropolis.

BOH.name: Wagenburg
BOH.desc: During the Hussite Wars, our armies relied on wagon forts called Wagenburg to win battles against superior forces. While we may not always deploy wagons, the principle remains: infantry sharpshooters fighting from prepared defensive positions become our standard doctrine.

BOS.name: Bosnian Ljekaruše
BOS.desc: In the secluded valleys of our nation, monks of our monasteries have compiled the Ljekaruše, extensive medicinal codices written in the native Bosančica script. By synthesizing ancient Greco-Byzantine theory with the high-altitude herbalism of the Dinaric Alps, these manuals provide a sophisticated system of community healthcare in an era where professional physicians are a rarity. This mastery of folk medicine and surgery ensures our population remains resilient against the plagues that devastate the lowlands, fostering a cultural identity defined by intellectual self-reliance and the preservation of Slavic scientific knowledge.

BOS.name: Kingly Ambitions
BOS.desc: The achievements and hard work of our people deserve recognition and protection. We will establish a prestigious title for ourselves and thereby secure that recognition from neighboring rulers, formalizing our status through diplomatic bonds.

BOS.name: Many Churches of Bosnia
BOS.desc: Bosnia is home to several faiths. Not only is our land shared between the Orthodox and Catholic Churches, but it is also home to the South Slavic Christian faithful, the Krstjani. Isolated from central supervision, we will have to foster a local understanding and harmony between these different groups to maintain our stability.

BOS.name: Stanak Meetings
BOS.desc: Our nobility regularly gathers together to discuss the most pressing issues for our country. These meetings ensure our noble lords are aligned in their policies and show unity during our parliament sessions.

BOS.name: The Filigree Guilds
BOS.desc: Drawing on the inexhaustible silver veins of the central mountains, our urban craftsmen have perfected the art of Filigran, intricate silver wirework that has become the hallmark of Bosnian luxury. These guilds operate as a powerful economic estate, exporting ceremonial daggers and fine jewelry to the markets of Venice and Vienna. By turning our raw mineral wealth into high-value artistic exports, we have created a prosperous urban middle class that is fiercely loyal to the Crown. This industrial refinement elevates the prestige of our nation in every foreign court, proving that the 'Iron Heart' of the Balkans possesses a sophisticated cultural edge that rivals the great capitals of the West.

BOS.name: The Srebrenica Mint Office
BOS.desc: As the mines of Srebrenica become the premier source of bullion in the Balkans, the realm has moved beyond the mere export of raw ore. We have established a Royal Mint and an Assay Office to regulate the purity of Bosnian silver, producing a coin which rivals those of Venice in reliability. By mandating that all silver extracted by Ragusan or Saxon miners be processed through state-controlled refineries, we capture a massive share of the value-added profit. This liquid wealth allows us to make Bosnia the most financially solvent power in the Dinaric Alps.

BRA.name: Unified Legal System
BRA.desc: We have gone to great lengths to unify our internal legal systems, rooting out abuse and malpractice while creating a professional judiciary.

BRA.name: Canton System
BRA.desc: The Canton System will divide the country into adminstrative districts called cantons, each responsible for army recruitment and linking the local population closely to the government. This system relies on voluntary enrollment rather than coercive recruiting. However, each canton must provide a minimum number of soldiers.

BRA.name: Prussian Virtues
BRA.desc: The virtues of Pietism — diligence, sincerity, and a sense of duty above all — are the core values of our society.

BRA.name: Berliner Aufklärung
BRA.desc: New ideas spread fast in our cities, and the minds of Brandenburg have never been idle. We will cultivate this spirit of inquiry, drawing scholars and thinkers to our court. A nation that thinks clearly governs itself well.

BRA.name: Dispositio Achillea
BRA.desc: Dividing our lands between heirs has weakened dynasties across the Empire. We will establish a clear rule of succession, the eldest inherits all. Our nobles may grumble, but an undivided Mark is worth their discontent.

BRA.name: Divide the Estates
BRA.desc: United, the three estates form an effective block against the power of the ruler. To consolidate our control, we must systematically leverage the nobility against the other estates.

BRA.name: Edict of Potsdam
BRA.desc: Our neighbors drive out their most industrious subjects for the sake of religious conformity. Their loss is our gain. We open our doors to the persecuted and the skilled alike, and our cities grow richer for it.
mods: Possible Burghers in Towns and Cities

BRA.name: Expansive Policies
BRA.desc: Brandenburg's infertile, sandy soil has earned it the unflattering nickname 'Sandbox of the Holy Roman Empire.' Such poverty spurred the margraves to aggressively expand, pursuing claims to neighboring territories. These conquests have made our country much more culturally diverse than the rest of the Empire.

BRA.name: Found the Kammergericht
BRA.desc: In order to regularize control of the Mark of Brandenburg, we will replace local common law with Roman law. We will further regulate justice by moving the Supreme Court from the court of the Elector, who is prone to moving around, to a fixed central location. This will simultaneously improve justice and curb the power of local magnates.

BRA.name: Geheimer Rat für die Kurmark
BRA.desc: The authority of the Margrave is greatly threatened by the ever-increasing power of our Estates. The Estates are of great benefit to our nation, but the threat they represent to our base of power necessitates the creation of a new council, one which reduces the very real power that the estates hold over our nation into more of an advisory position for the Margrave. This way, we may continue to enjoy the benefits of our Estates while having fewer concerns about their needs.

BRA.name: Hohenzollern Court Culture
BRA.desc: A great court needs more than soldiers and clerks. By welcoming artists, philosophers, and men of science into our service, we turn the court of Brandenburg into a beacon of culture, and show the world that our ambitions reach beyond the battlefield.

BRA.name: Hohenzollern Privy Council
BRA.desc: Our estates have long held sway over the governance of the Mark. By establishing a council of advisors answerable to the Elector alone, we bring our ablest men to the center of power, and quietly reduce the estates to a consultative role.

BRA.name: Iron Tooth
BRA.desc: Enhancing our court's control over the Margraviate's lands will earn our ruler the moniker Iron Tooth, as if we bit it like an attack dog. Our rule will leave a mark on our nation, a mark which will instill a sense of pride and loyalty in even the lowliest peasant in Brandenburg.

BRA.name: Religious Toleration
BRA.desc: Stability in our home regions is the key to our success elsewhere. Expanding outwards while fostering religious tolerance, we not only improve stability at home, but we also make our realm a haven for those fleeing persecution elsewhere.

BRA.name: Soldiers of Fortune
BRA.desc: Our lands are sparsely populated, for the most part, and surrounded by enemies. The necessity for more robust defenses has prompted us to hire soldiers from foreign lands, who will fight under our banner for a price.

BRA.name: The Northern March
BRA.desc: In the early days of the Holy Roman Empire, the Brandenburg area was settled and governed by Slavic tribes, until the Emperor created the Northern March to subjugate and fortify the area. Over time, this Northern March evolved into Brandenburg, becoming one of the most important regions in the Holy Roman Empire.

BRB.name: Joyous Entry
BRB.desc: The Joyous Entry grants liberties to our Burghers, akin to a Magna Carta for the Low Countries. This document upholds freedoms for the church, towns, and Nobility, emphasizing consent for taxes and commitments to our nation's indivisibility.

BRB.name: A Land of Culture
BRB.desc: With the foundation of the University of Leuven, Brabant has placed itself firmly at the center of culture in the Netherlands. Students from all over Europe come to our lands to study and share their knowledge.

BRB.name: Brabantian Rights
BRB.desc: As other nations have, it is time to codify the liberties of our subjects, in order to identify and safeguard their rights and motivate them to continue working towards a better future for our country.

BRB.name: The Four Quartiers
BRB.desc: The Four Quartiers are the four provinces into which the core of Brabant is divided. Each quartier is formed by a satellite of large and smaller towns, some walled and others not. They all work in perfect synergy like a well-greased engine, filling our coffers with great riches.

BRG.name: Order of Saint Hubert
BRG.desc: The Hubertusorden will serve as a glorious reminder of our knights' combat prowess! Joining the order will be a reward for our loyal knights, and its members will display our glory for all to see.

BRG.name: Order of Saint Hubert
BRG.desc: The Hubertusorden will serve as a glorious reminder of our knights' combat prowess! Joining the order will be a reward for our loyal knights, and its members will display our glory for all to see.

BRI.name: Breton Peninsula
BRI.desc: Ever since our ancestors came from Britain, our extensive coastal holdings have been bustling with activity. Our people live by the sea and for the sea, and our ports are always full of trade and fishing boats.

BRI.name: Legacy of Breton Independence
BRI.desc: Brittany has never truly been part of France Though we have been ravaged by Franks, Vikings, and the English in the past, we have, thus far, maintained our unique identity as a people. Let all of our neighbors be aware that Brittany shall remain forever free, the last bastion of true Gallic traditions!

BRI.name: The Estates of Brittany
BRI.desc: First called in the 14th century, the Estates of Brittany allowed free men from all rungs of society, even the Third Estate, to share their grievances and petition the ruler for redress. By calling in the Estates, we can mitigate some of the tension felt throughout our domain.

BRI.name: Order of the Ermine
BRI.desc: The Order of the Ermine draws inspiration from the Order of the Garter. With the ermine as its symbol, representing unwavering personal honor, the order recognizes both men and women, regardless of social status, for exceptional service to the Duchy of Brittany.

BRM.name: Wendischer Münzverein
BRM.desc: A newly founded organization between cities with a strong Hanseatic presence, the Wendish Coinage Treaty will provide us with a strong basis to facilitate trade and commerce in our lands.

BRM.name: Port Networks
BRM.desc: Our country survives through its strong ties to maritime trade and the constant exchange of goods. To maintain an orderly harbor, we will need to dredge fresh waterways and build more docks and warehouses, attracting new merchants and their ships.

BRM.name: Wendischer Münzverein
BRM.desc: A newly founded organization between cities with a strong Hanseatic presence, the Wendish Coinage Treaty will provide us with a strong basis to facilitate trade and commerce in our lands.

BTL.name: Aurès Maraboutic Authority
BTL.desc: The maraboutic shayḵs of the Aurès, descended from the early medieval saints whose tombs anchor our highest pilgrimage sites, bind our scattered villages and our wandering pastoralist clans to a single religious and judicial network whose authority no purely secular chieftaincy can match. Our crown endows the lodge shrines, our chiefs receive their ijāza from the Aurès shayḵs, and our religious establishment gains the depth that comes from hereditary scholarly succession. Anchored in the Aurès, our spiritual authority keeps the clergy content and lends our government a legitimacy that flatland courts struggle to build.

BTL.name: Berber-Arabic Press
BTL.desc: Our late period printers and lithographers at the Aurès market towns publish bilingual Berber-Arabic periodicals, religious tracts, and tribal history chronicles, circulating our distinctive cultural identity through the literate Maghrebi reading public. We engage in dialogue with the wider Arab-Islamic reformist movements while preserving our confederation's particular linguistic and ritual inheritance. This bilingual press revival binds our scattered confederation into a shared modern identity and draws the wider Tellian region into our language and faith.

BTL.name: Constantine Hinterland
BTL.desc: Our confederation occupies the immediate hinterland of the great fortress city of Constantine, supplying the city's grain, wool, leather, and livestock markets while our chiefs negotiate caravan protection and toll immunity treaties with whichever power holds the city. Our merchant houses ride the constant trade of the Constantine markets, and our envoys gain experience negotiating with the central courts of Algeria and Tunisia alike. Standing in the hinterland of a great city gives our state a merchant's reach and a diplomatic experience unknown to purely mountain confederations far from the cities.

BTL.name: Mountain Raiding Tradition
BTL.desc: Our mounted light cavalry (drawn from the youngest sons of every clan, mounted on the swift Berber horses our pastoral economy raises) patrol the contested frontiers of our confederation, riding down rival raiders, extracting tribute from passing caravans, and gathering reputation in the cross-clan competitive games of the seasonal fairs. Our cavalry tradition transmits its tactical knowledge through hereditary apprenticeship within the warrior families. Our raiding tradition fills the state with swift riders and a soldiery that recovers quickly from setbacks, which the more sedentary Maghrebi states cannot reproduce through formal training.

BTL.name: Tellian Atlas Pastoralism
BTL.desc: Our confederation thrives on the transhumant pastoralism of the Tellian Atlas. Sheep, goats, and camels move seasonally between the upland summer pastures of the Aurès and the winter lowlands of the Constantine plain, sustained by a kinship economy that purely agricultural states cannot replicate. Our tribal chiefs hold their authority through the seasonal grazing rights they negotiate among the constituent clans, and our pastoral wealth supports a tribal warrior class whose flocks travel as both wealth and rations. Pastoralism holds the tribesmen loyal to the state and brings a prosperity independent of the rain-fed harvests.

BTL.name: Tellian Dialect Prestige
BTL.desc: Our distinctive Tellian Berber dialect, preserving features of the older Zenata speech that the surrounding Arab-Berber blend has dissolved elsewhere, anchors our scholarly tradition through the manuscripts of our Aurès qādīs and the religious poetry of our marabouts. Our literate clergy preserves dialect dictionaries, religious poetry manuscripts, and tribal history chronicles that the more Arabized neighboring confederations have lost. Our distinct tongue keeps the clergy literate and fills our state with a spiritual and cultural confidence that the more centralized lowland courts lack.

BUL.name: Bulgarian Tsardom
BUL.desc: Our realm upholds the illustrious legacy of Simeon the Great and the emperors of the Tsardom who came before us. Acclaimed by both clergy and nobility, our ruler stands as the guardian of the faith and the cornerstone of South Slavic imperial power in the Balkans.

BUL.name: Legacy of Ivan Asen II
BUL.desc: The reign of Ivan Asen II marked a new height of Bulgarian power, diplomacy, and economic expansion. His legacy endures as a foundation for a strong and centralized state.

BUL.name: The Bastion of Tsarevets
BUL.desc: The capital of Tarnovo, perched upon the cliffs of Tsarevets and Trapezitsa, is arguably the most formidable fortress in the Balkans, symbolizing the power of the Asen dynasty. By continuously expanding the complex of palaces, patriarchal cathedrals, and triple-layered walls, we have created an administrative center that is immune to sudden coups or sieges. This architectural dominance projects an image of imperial stability that cowers the local Boyars and convinces the populace that the 'Third Rome' has truly moved to the banks of the Yantra.

BUL.name: The Boyar Council
BUL.desc: To prevent the internal strife that plagued the 14th century, we will evolve into a 'Consultative Autocracy' where the most powerful Boyars are integrated into a permanent State Council. This body will serve as a high court and a military planning board, ensuring that the interests of the landed nobility are aligned with those of the crown. This political stability will allow us to maintain a large standing army and avoid the devastating civil wars that have historically left the empire vulnerable to its neighbors.

BUL.name: The Bulgarian Census Bureau
BUL.desc: Knowledge is power. We have instituted a decennial census that records every person, unit of livestock, and hearth in the empire. This precise data allows for the most efficient taxation and conscription system in the Balkans. By knowing exactly what the nation can provide, we can plan long-term campaigns with a level of logistical certainty that ensures our armies are always well-fed and our coffers never empty.

BUL.name: The Bulgarian Gunpowder Foundries
BUL.desc: Drawing on the iron mines of the Balkan mountains and the expertise of Saxon miners, we will establish the first major domestic gunpowder industry in the region. These foundries will produce heavy siege cannons and early handguns, allowing the Bulgarian army to transition away from purely feudal cavalry toward a more modern, infantry-heavy force. By controlling the production of saltpeter and iron, we will ensure that our walls remain the most dangerous obstacle for any would-be conqueror in the Balkans.

BUL.name: The Chancery of the Asens
BUL.desc: At its peak, the chancellery in Tarnovo was the most sophisticated diplomatic hub in the Orthodox world, producing intricate Slavic charters that influenced the courts of Serbia and Russia. By professionalizing the class of Logothetes and scribes, the Tsars will ensure that every land grant and international treaty is meticulously recorded and legally binding. This administrative rigor will allow the state to extract taxes more efficiently and manage its complex network of vassalage with a degree of central control that is rare in the late medieval period.

BUL.name: The Grand Academy of the Yantra
BUL.desc: The intellectual legacy of the 14th-century Tarnovo Literary School is revived in the 17th century through the creation of a modern state university. This institution focuses on civil law, engineering, and the translation of Western scientific texts into the Bulgarian vernacular, creating a class of bureaucrats who are as capable as any in Paris or Vienna. This modernization of the elite will ensure that we can manage a complex, multi-ethnic empire while maintaining the cultural purity of its Bulgarian core.

BUL.name: The Hesychast State Philosophy
BUL.desc: The spiritual teachings of Grēgórios Sinaítēs have moved from the hermit's cell to the halls of power. By adopting Hesychasm, a philosophy of inner stillness and divine light, as the unofficial state ideology, we foster a populace that is deeply pious and resilient. This shared spiritual identity acts as a powerful deterrent against the influences from our enemies, making the Bulgarian subjects immune to foreign conversion or subversion.

BUL.name: The Imperial Restoration Doctrine
BUL.desc: We have fully embraced our role as the natural leader of the Balkan peoples, articulating a formal doctrine for the reunification of all former Bulgarian lands. This fate is backed by a modern, professionalized army and a sophisticated diplomatic corps that seek to play the Great Powers against one another. The belief in a 'Greater Bulgaria' becomes the central pillar of the state, driving a policy of aggressive expansion and cultural assimilation that seeks to restore the empire of Simeon the Great.

BUL.name: The Silk and Rose Guilds
BUL.desc: Utilizing the fertile Thracian plains and the unique climate of the Rose Valley, we have established state-protected guilds for the production of luxury oils and silk. These high-value, low weight goods are perfect for overland export to the courts of Europe and Asia. The wealth generated by these guilds allows the state to build a massive gold reserve, making our economy one of the most stable and credit-worthy in the entire Mediterranean basin.

BUL.name: The Standing Drilled Infantry
BUL.desc: Moving away from seasonal levies, we have established the first permanent 'Regiments of the Lion'. These infantrymen are trained year-round in the use of firearms, following a rigorous drill based on the successes of neighbor models but adapted for Balkan terrain. This professional infantry core give us a reliable tool for offensive warfare, capable of out-marching and out-shooting the traditional armies of our neighbors.

BUL.name: The Tarnovo Artistic Schools
BUL.desc: Under the direct patronage of the Shishman Dynasty, the nation has undergone a spectacular cultural growth, positioning itself as a true Third Rome and the primary guardian of Orthodox high culture. By funding the reconstruction of the Patriarchal Cathedral and the royal palaces of Tsarevets, the state has gathered a new generation of master iconographers, hagiographers, and architects who blend traditional Byzantine aesthetics with a unique, emotive Bulgarian realism. This school of thought does not merely produce religious icons; it serves as a powerful instrument of imperial propaganda, codifying the Bulgarian recension of Church Slavonic and producing the Manasses Chronicle to legitimize the Tsar's claim to the Byzantine heritage.

BUR.name: Between Two Realms
BUR.desc: We can consider ourselves to be both members of the traditional lands of the Holy Roman Empire, and of the realm of France. While this can complicate feudal relations, the situation has molded us into adept diplomats, able to skillfully play both sides to our own advantage.

BUR.name: Compagnies d'Ordonnance
BUR.desc: Our reliance on feudal levies has proven inadequate for the demands of modern warfare. The creation of permanently contracted cavalry units, the Compagnies d'Ordonnance, provides us with a reliable and professional military force directly loyal to the Crown.

BUR.name: Create the Regimental System
BUR.desc: To ensure consistent recruitment and sufficient supply of fighters, we must establish a formal regimental system. This reform will allow us to organize manpower more effectively, centralize command structures, and reduce dependence on local nobles and foreign mercenaries.

BUR.name: Foster Agriculture
BUR.desc: The lands of Burgundy are well-suited to growing plants and herding animals. Grapes are particularly apt for local growing conditions. With skilled cultivation, it should be easy to foster an agricultural industry.

BUR.name: Influence of the Burgundian Towns
BUR.desc: The traditional Estates General favors the clergy and nobility, but the rising wealth and political importance of towns can no longer be ignored. By refining its structure to reflect the growing strength of the merchant class, we ensure more balanced governance while preserving the privileges of the other estates. A stronger urban voice will also enhance our administrative capacities and speed up the rate of urbanization.

BUR.name: Knightly Prowess
BUR.desc: We occupy a prestigious position within the feudal system of France. Therefore, it is only right that our troops are seen as a reflection of the Burgundian spirit.

BUR.name: Promote the États Généraux
BUR.desc: Burgundy is a feudal creation with various parts conjoined under different conditions, which has created strong local identities. By promoting a central assembly, we give a forum for these interests, promoting a smooth and uncontested rule.

BUR.name: Reform the Feudal Army
BUR.desc: The feudal levy system has proven slow and unreliable in this new age of professional warfare. Inspired by the French model, we will replace our scattered vassal hosts with salaried companies, skilled officers, and integrated armies. A disciplined core of professional soldiers will form the backbone of a modern and adaptable army.

BUR.name: The Order of the Golden Fleece
BUR.desc: One of Europe's foremost chivalric orders. Being a Knight of the Golden Fleece is a mark of great status, and reflects well upon us.

BUR.name: Order of the Golden Fleece
BUR.desc: Founded by Philip the Good of Burgundy, the Order of the Golden Fleece is among the most illustrious chivalric orders in Christendom. Membership binds its knights by solemn oath to uphold the glory and honor of their lord, and to stand united against all threats to Christendom.

BYZ.name: Court Ceremonies
BYZ.desc: The introduction of the Court Ceremonies ensures grand ceremonies are carried out in accordance with traditions. Meticulous court etiquette is upheld, thereby elevating the prestige and splendor of the ruling elite.

BYZ.name: Decayed Theme System
BYZ.desc: A system of provincial headquarters and armies, spearheaded by a strategos with dual responsibilities to protect the locals and establish authority at the behest of the realm. This system replaced the provincial administration of Diocletian and has served our people ever since. Yet time has worn it thin, it endures still, a relic of ages long past.

BYZ.name: Katepanáta
BYZ.desc: The answer to warmongering neighbors is the consolidation of newly conquered territory through resolute military authority. Originating from the word katepánō — the one placed at the top — the Katepanáta stand above the ordinary themes, grouping provinces beneath a single commander invested with both civil and martial power. First employed with prominence in the 10th and 11th centuries, from Italy with its seat at Bari to the volatile frontiers of Armenia under emperors such as Basil II, these great districts ensured that distant and contested lands were not left to fragmented rule. Let these bastions of our willpower serve as a banner against all those who seek to take our crown from us!
mods: Speed of Integration (We have completed the Fate of the Phoenix disaster victoriously)

BYZ.name: Kritai Katholikoi
BYZ.desc: The Kritai Katholikoi, colloquially referred to as the Universal Justices of the Romans, have come to represent the pinnacle of legal authority, born from the reforms of Byz Andronikos Ii Palaiologos and initially comprising of twelve judges from both secular and ecclesiastical backgrounds. Later streamlined to a panel of four, this illustrious court holds unparalleled authority with no recourse for appeal.

BYZ.name: Modern Imperial Army
BYZ.desc: The old Decayed Theme System of Byzantium proved faulty, strengthening the authority of governors and generals rather than the ruler. As a result, a new Imperial Army has formed, one where being a soldier is a profession rather than a duty.

BYZ.name: Mōs Maiōrum
BYZ.desc: Rome was never exclusively Greek. Our titles, our laws, and the memory of the Eternal City descend from a Latin tradition older than our current tongue. The Mōs Maiōrum formalizes this heritage: palace offices are reordered around ancient Roman precedent, the court tongue shifts to Latin, and our diplomats find their work cheaper to sustain.

BYZ.name: Reformed Kritai Katholikoi
BYZ.desc: Although the judiciary system created by Byz Andronikos Ii Palaiologos saw initial success, there were still internal issues, which the judges exploited to pursue their interests. With the reforms of this Supreme Court, existing legal processes have been streamlined while ensuring no corruption between the judges.
mods: Efficiency of Our Cabinet (Fate of the Phoenix is currently active or we completed it victoriously)

BYZ.name: Komnénian Prónoia
BYZ.desc: Under the Komnénian emperors, the informal Prónoia system had been codified into a rigorous instrument of imperial policy. Grants were formally contracted, with each holder obligated to furnish a cavalry contingent proportional to the revenues they received. The Emperor retained the right of revocation, and a reorganised imperial registry tracked every grant and its associated military obligation ensuring that the land revenues of the realm translated directly into mounted levy strength under the crown's direct control.

BYZ.name: Mégas Doméstikos Command
BYZ.desc: The office of Mégas Doméstikos Command Great Domestic of the Schools places supreme field command of all imperial armies in the hands of a single appointed commander. Rather than dispersing military authority among competing tagmata officers, the Mégas Doméstikos coordinates strategy across the entire theater of war. The prestige of the office draws the finest Nobles to serve under its banner, and battles won under his banner forge our army into a well tempered one at twice the rate of ordinary campaigns.

BYZ.name: Palaiológian Hereditary Prónoia
BYZ.desc:
Facing an exhausted treasury and the constant pressure of civil war and foreign invasion, the Palaeologan emperors have conceded the irrevocable.
Prónoia grants are henceforth hereditary. Noble families who previously served at imperial pleasure now hold their lands as permanent patrimony, bolstering the legitimacy of the dynasty through aristocratic loyalty but at the cost of the military obligations that once gave the system its purpose. The cavalry that the grants were meant to fund must increasingly be hired at the state's own expense.

BYZ.name: Porphyrogénitus Court
BYZ.desc: An emperor born in the sacred Purple Chamber of the Great Palace carries an aura of legitimacy unmatched by any rival. Our court ceremony, codified in the De Ceremoniis, projects the majesty of a living Roman Empire to every envoy who enters our capital. The elaborate protocol is costly, but the prestige it radiates solidifies the dynasty's claim before the world.

BYZ.name: Prónoia System
BYZ.desc: The Prónoia System functions as a means of temporarily transferring imperial fiscal rights, such as taxes or income from various sources, to individuals or institutions. Unlike the feudal system prevalent in Europe at the time, Prónoia grants were neither hereditary nor transferable, and ultimate ownership remained with the Emperor. In exchange for these privileges, the system ultimately served the purpose for the head of state to raise an army in times of need, and entailed that the troops had to mostly cover their own expenses.

BYZ.name: Reformed Prónoia System
BYZ.desc: Rather than allow the Prónoia governors to strengthen their hold on their lands, the system has been changed so any loopholes that made the title of governor hereditary or transferable can no longer be exploited.

BYZ.name: Reformed Tágmata
BYZ.desc: Through the sweeping reforms born of crisis, the Tágmata have been reforged into something closer to the fearsome professional soldiers of old. Stricter drill, restored imperial funding, and a renewed sense of purpose have elevated the regiments above the diminished force they had become. These soldiers stand apart from the feudal levy not merely in name but in discipline, cohesion, and battlefield effectiveness.

BYZ.name: Varangian Guard
BYZ.desc: The Varangian Guard, drawn from Norse, English, and other northern peoples, bound by personal oath to the Emperor serve as the imperial bodyguard and household shock troops. Their loyalty is purchased, not inherited, making them immune to the factional intrigues that plague Greek noble officers. Their axes have defended the throne for generations, and their fierce discipline sets a standard for the whole army.

BYZ.name: Akritai
BYZ.desc: The Akritai rose to prominence as the defenders of Anatolia against the eastern threats that the empire faced. These soldiers were given grants through the Decayed Theme System to cultivate and protect, as a means to provide them with a reward and a reason to defend our homeland.

BYZ.name: Byzantine Cataphracts
BYZ.desc: A powerful body of heavily armored knights, the Cataphracts make up the elite of our cavalry units. Armed with a short lance named 'kontos' and covered in scale armor, these troops strike fear at the heart of our enemies. A whirlwind of steel in the form of an unstoppable wave of horsemen delivers the killing blow to all those who seek to trample our people.

BYZ.name: Imperial Varangian Guard
BYZ.desc: Powerful warriors that originally hailed from the northern Viking lands, these select few ferocious soldiers make up the core of the royal guard. Armed with axes and shields, they have often been described as pelekyphóroi bárbaroi, axe-wielding barbarians.

BYZ.name: Imperial Varangians
BYZ.desc: Powerful warriors that originally hailed from the northern Viking lands, these select few ferocious soldiers make up the core of the royal guard. Armed with axes and shields, they have often been described as pelekyphóroi bárbaroi, axe-wielding barbarians.

BYZ.name: Modernized Helepolis
BYZ.desc: The Helepolis has served many Byzantine emperors in the past. With the introduction of gunpowder and the advent of new siege machines of warfare, the city-taker artillery has now embraced its new deadly form.

BYZ.name: Modernized Varangians
BYZ.desc: Powerful warriors that originally hailed from the northern Viking lands, these select few ferocious soldiers make up the core of the royal guard. Armed with axes and shields, they have often been described as pelekyphóroi bárbaroi, axe-wielding barbarians.

BYZ.name: Pelekyphóroi Varangians
BYZ.desc: Powerful warriors that originally hailed from the northern Viking lands, these select few ferocious soldiers make up the core of the royal guard. Armed with axes and shields, they have often been described as pelekyphóroi bárbaroi, axe-wielding barbarians.

BYZ.name: Restored Varangians
BYZ.desc: Powerful warriors that originally hailed from the northern Viking lands, these select few ferocious soldiers make up the core of the royal guard. Armed with axes and shields, they have often been described as pelekyphóroi bárbaroi, axe-wielding barbarians.

BYZ.name: Varangian Guard
BYZ.desc: Powerful warriors that originally hailed from the northern Viking lands, these select few ferocious soldiers make up the core of the royal guard. Armed with axes and shields, they have often been described as pelekyphóroi bárbaroi, axe-wielding barbarians.
