ENG.desc: In a world of rapid change, the seas remain crucially important to our nation. Both as a means to secure our dominance and as the first line of defense, our 'wooden wall' of warships shall prevail.

ENG.name: Yorkist Tradition
ENG.desc: Educated men of lower stature can contribute just as readily as the Clergy, and their practical experience makes them excellent additions to any governmental office. The Yorkist Tradition states that any literate man of notable background may join the ranks of governance, along with those who have devoted themselves to the service of God.

Possible Burghers in Towns and Cities

ENG.name: Experimental Riflemen
ENG.desc: Elite marksmen equipped with the long-range Baker Rifle and trained to screen the main force in small independent pickets, Experimental Riflemen represent a modern vision of infantry combat formations.

ENG.name: Redcoats
ENG.desc: Redcoats is the name given to the English Line and Column Infantry, after the adoption of red coats by soldiers fighting in Ireland, and their generalization in the New Model Army.

ENG.name: A Royal Navy
ENG.desc: Beginning around 1495, the Tudor monarchy invested heavily in not just ships, but extensive infrastructure to maintain and otherwise support them. This for many marked the official founding of the Royal Navy.

ENG.name: Blake's Sailing and Fighting Instructions
ENG.desc: Robert Blake has written several sets of rules and regulations that resulted in sweeping naval reforms. These include new tactics for blockades and landings, as well as adoption of the single line ahead battle formation.

ENG.name: Coke Smelting
ENG.desc: The invention of coke smelting, specifically its application in Iron and Steel production, is closely tied to the Industrial Revolution. Iron and Steel are currently produced using traditional methods like charcoal smelting, whereas this new method promises greater yields and cheaper upkeep.

ENG.name: English Bill of Rights
ENG.desc: A sweeping series of reforms limiting royal power, particularly in judicial matters. Among other stipulations, they state that the monarch may not unilaterally raise armies, prescribe cruel and unusual punishment, or interfere with the free election of members of Parliament.

ENG.name: Experimental Riflemen
ENG.desc: Elite marksmen equipped with the long-range Baker Rifle and trained to screen the main force in small independent pickets, Experimental Riflemen represent a modern vision of infantry combat formations.

ENG.name: Lionhearts
ENG.desc: The bravery and discipline of English foot soldiers has been witnessed from the shieldwalls of Northumbria to the darkened skies of France. Inspired by the lion-hearted spirit of our kings and the stoicism of the common man, our infantry fights with the ferocity of the Anglo-Saxon warriors before them.

ENG.name: Magna Carta
ENG.desc: The 'Great Charter' is a legal document that aims to protect the feudal rights of our barons against unjust taxation and legal maneuvers by the Crown. It is also one of the earliest documents to enshrine the idea of civil liberties, such as the right to a fair trial and protection from illegal imprisonment.

ENG.name: Our Island Home
ENG.desc: Our island protects us from outside enemies, but that will not matter if we do not protect the surrounding waters. By being true masters of our surrounding seas, we will keep a firm control on those who threaten our land.

ENG.name: Palladian Architecture
ENG.desc: The architectural innovations made by Inigo Jones will undoubtedly have a significant impact on future generations of architects. His promotion of classical architecture and his priority on proportion and harmony are considered hallmarks of the neoclassical movement in England.

ENG.name: Redcoats
ENG.desc: Life in the English army is grueling and strictly regimented, but it instills in one a certain character. The unflappable nature of our troops, as well as their expertise with firearms, strikes fear into the hearts of our enemies.

ENG.name: Rulers of the Waves
ENG.desc: A massive sea presence is required for any nation attempting to rule the waters. Our fleet will be so imposing that the shores of our enemies will always be surrounded by our vessels.

ENG.name: Secretaries of State
ENG.desc: The monarch has always had a secretary responsible for their royal correspondence. This position eventually evolved into that of the Secretary of State, a powerful minister who not only transmits royal decrees, but also has a high level of administrative authority.

ENG.name: The Eltham Ordinance
ENG.desc: The Eltham Ordinances represented England's first attempt to streamline royal bureaucracy and make it more adaptable and cost-effective. The Ordinances attempted reform through reducing royal household expenditures and consolidating certain bureaucratic functions.

ENG.name: The Navigation Acts
ENG.desc: These acts represent the apex of mercantilism. Trade must be conducted with our ships and pass through our ports first, where we will collect customs duties and any other applicable taxes.

ENG.name: The Sick and Hurt Board
ENG.desc: This institution looked after the welfare of ordinary enlisted seamen in the Navy. It brought about a series of reforms that greatly improved the health of sailors on duty.

ENG.name: Water Frame
ENG.desc: The water frame is a spinning frame used in the textile industry to produce cotton thread. This innovation will contribute to the establishment of large textile factories powered by water wheels.

EPI.name: Adriatic Gatekeepers
EPI.desc: By securing the ports of Valona and Butrint, Epirus sits as the warden of the Adriatic Sea. We have used this position to negotiate favorable trade treaties with Venice and the Italian city-states, who must pass through our sphere of influence to reach the Levant. By levying precise tariffs and providing 'protection' services against corsairs, we have transformed our once-isolated despotate into a wealthy commercial hub that bridges the gap between East and West.

EPI.name: Arvanite Communities
EPI.desc: To bolster our dwindling numbers, we have invited the fierce Arvanite clans to settle in the fertile valleys of Epirus and Acarnania. In exchange for land and autonomy, these warriors provide us with a tireless light infantry force that excels in the brutal, close quarters combat of the Balkan frontier. Their unique martial culture, blended with our Roman military tradition, creates a hybrid force that is both exceptionally loyal and terrifyingly aggressive in the shock of battle.

EPI.name: Balkan Marriages
EPI.desc: Epirus sits at the crossroads of the Greek, Slavic, and Latin worlds, and we have turned our royal daughters into our most effective diplomats. Through a complex web of strategic marriages with Serbian Kings, Albanian Chieftains, and even Italian Counts, we have made the House of Doukas-Komnenos the indispensable arbiter of Balkan politics. These blood ties ensure that when we go to war, we are never without powerful allies willing to strike from our enemies' flanks.

EPI.name: Fortresses of Ioannina
EPI.desc: The city of Ioannina has been transformed into a true stronghold. Utilizing the latest in Italian military engineering, we have surrounded our capital and its lake with a series of interlocking bastions and water forts that can withstand months of sustained bombardment. This defensive network serves as the anchor for our entire national strategy, allowing us to retreat into an impregnable core whenever the tides of war turn against us in the open field.

EPI.name: Sublime Diplomacy
EPI.desc: Centuries of survival between powerful enemies have made our diplomatic corps the most sophisticated in the world. We have developed a 'neutrality-of-strength' doctrine, playing the great powers against one another so skillfully that they compete for our favor rather than seeking our conquest. Our ambassadors are renowned for their ability to weave peace treaties that always seem to leave Epirus with more territory and influence than when the conflict began.

EPI.name: The Eagle of the Pindus
EPI.desc: In the rugged, rain-swept peaks of the Pindus mountains, the Despots of Epirus have carved out a sanctuary that no Latin army can penetrate. We have mastered the art of 'mountain-ambush' warfare, using the vertical geography of our realm to trap and destroy much larger forces in narrow defiles. This environmental mastery turns our entire country into a deathtrap for invaders, ensuring that while the plains may fall, the mountains remain forever Greek.

ETH.name: Ç̌äwa Arquebusiers
ETH.desc: The introduction of gunpowder makes the traditional bows and javelins obsolete, but gives a new edge to the Ç̌äwa.

ETH.name: Ç̌äwa Columns
ETH.desc: The most modern version of the Ç̌äwa. These fighters have reached the highest point in discipline and effectivity, becoming the terror of their enemies.

ETH.name: Ç̌äwa Line Infantry
ETH.desc: The Ç̌äwa adapt a line formation, marching side by side and firing in order. When the first line in combat reloads their firearms, the second takes their position to fire, just to be replaced by the next one in a continuous motion.

ETH.name: Ç̌äwa Musketeers
ETH.desc: The discipline of the Ç̌äwa Regiments gets further improved, making them fight more coordinated, inflicting deadly volleys to their enemies.

ETH.name: Ç̌äwa Regiments
ETH.desc: A better structure system allows the Ç̌äwa to be better trained and become a mighty force for Ethiopia.

ETH.name: Ç̌äwa Units
ETH.desc: In Ethiopia, the arsenal of the Ç̌äwa encompasses the formidable curved sword known as the shotel, the versatile spear called the tor, and proficiency in ranged weaponry such as bows and javelins known as armah. Notably, the use of protective armor, including the renowned coat of mail, is prevalent among them, further enhancing their defensive capabilities.

ETH.name: A Modern Nation
ETH.desc: Despite our apparent isolation, we are well aware of the innovations happening around the world, and we waste no time in implementing these modernizations in order to maintain a competitive advantage over our rivals.

ETH.name: A Permanent Capital
ETH.desc: For centuries, our nation has lacked a permanent capital, with the court following the rulers wherever they desired. While this approach has its advantages, in order to effectively govern our vast nation we need to establish a strong central authority in a proper permanent location.

ETH.name: A True Ethiopian Church
ETH.desc: External influences have their uses, but exposure to them can alter the nature of our beliefs. In order to maintain our identity, we must secure the domestic primacy of our own Tewahedo Church.

ETH.name: An Eternal Crusade
ETH.desc: As a Christian nation, we find ourselves surrounded by Muslim adversaries who seize every opportunity to attack us. To ensure our survival, we must be prepared to fight back immediately.

ETH.name: An Iron Fist
ETH.desc: Our region is diverse in cultures and religions, and the only thing that keeps it united is not compassion, but a powerful ruler, capable of dealing swiftly and decisively with any attempt at revolt.

ETH.name: External Friends
ETH.desc: Our envoys to Rome and Iberia, looking for military support, were quite successful — in fact, they put us on the map. These endeavors to find allies should continue.

ETH.name: Nəgusä Nägäst
ETH.desc: Our ruler is the king of all kings; the heir to the pedigree of the kings of Aksum along with that of the first ruler, Menelik I, the son of King Solomon and the Queen of Sheba. All of our kings are descended from the Solomon dynasty, and the line of inheritance need not be from father to son.

ETH.name: Origin of Coffee
ETH.desc: It is from our lands that Coffee comes, as we have the perfect growing conditions. While it can be cultivated in other places, ours is revered for its quality and exported by the ton. We have to make this a way to channel wealth into our nation.

ETH.name: Prester John
ETH.desc: People from Europe have been looking for Prester John for centuries, and are convinced that our ruler has to be him, somehow, as we are fellow Christian worshippers. There is no reason to point out that they are wrong, however, as they are now happy to share their ideas with us.

ETH.name: Solomon Dynastic Claim
ETH.desc: Our rulers' forefathers are descended from the monarchs of Aksum; from the bloodlines of King Solomon and the Queen of Sheba. We have deposed the Zagwe monarchs in order to legitimize our rule and firmly establish the kingdom being restored to its rightful dynasty.

ETH.name: The Ark of the Covenant
ETH.desc: We are the only nation to house the sacred Ark of the Covenant after it was secretly taken by Menelik I with divine assistance thousands of years ago. It is hidden away from public view, lest someone attempt to steal our sacred national treasure. Replicas of the Ark are placed in every single one of our churches as a reminder that our rule is blessed by God.

ETH.name: The Roof of Africa
ETH.desc: Our people have inhabited the highlands for generations, enduring extreme conditions that have made us resilient and strong. This gives us a significant advantage over our enemies whenever we engage in conflict.

ETH.name: Ç̌äwa Arquebusiers
ETH.desc: The introduction of gunpowder makes the traditional bows and javelins obsolete, but gives a new edge to the Ç̌äwa.

ETH.name: Ç̌äwa Columns
ETH.desc: The most modern version of the Ç̌äwa. These fighters have reached the highest point in discipline and effectivity, becoming the terror of their enemies.

ETH.name: Ç̌äwa Line Infantry
ETH.desc: The Ç̌äwa adapt a line formation, marching side by side and firing in order. When the first line in combat reloads their firearms, the second takes their position to fire, just to be replaced by the next one in a continuous motion.

ETH.name: Ç̌äwa Musketeers
ETH.desc: The discipline of the Ç̌äwa Regiments gets further improved, making them fight more coordinated, inflicting deadly volleys to their enemies.

ETH.name: Ç̌äwa Regiments
ETH.desc: The Ç̌äwa serve as Ethiopia's noble feudal warriors, recruited and appointed for the Emperor's army service. They are a professional soldier class, renowned for their ferocity.

ETH.name: Ç̌äwa Regiments
ETH.desc: A better structure system allows the Ç̌äwa to be better trained and become a mighty force for Ethiopia.

FEO.name: Black Sea Fur Trade
FEO.desc: Despite our small size, we control the vital ports that connect the vast fur-producing forests of Russia to the markets of the Mediterranean. We have negotiated exclusive rights with the local Tatar Khans to be the sole shippers of these furs across the Black Sea. The profits of this monopoly pay for Genoese engineers and Byzantine scholars, keeping our tiny principality a center of wealth and sophistication amid the steppe.

FEO.name: Gothic-Hellenic Synthesis
FEO.desc: In the isolation of the Crimean mountains, the remnants of the Crimean Goths and the local Greek population have fused into a single, resilient identity. This culture combines the stoic, martial heritage of the North with the administrative and maritime brilliance of the South. This 'Theodoran' spirit is our greatest defense, creating a population that views itself as the last true guardians of the Roman frontier, willing to fight to the last man for their unique way of life.

FEO.name: The Bastion of Mangup
FEO.desc: Our capital, Mangup-Kale, is a literal mountain carved into a fortress, surrounded by sheer cliffs that defy any siege engine. We have expanded these natural defenses with a series of sophisticated tunnels, cisterns, and hidden sally ports, allowing the city to hold out for years if necessary. This impregnable base ensures that even if our lands are ravaged by the Golden Horde, the heart of our Principality remains safe, serving as a beacon of hope for all Christians in the North.

FEO.name: The Gothic Red Guard
FEO.desc: Drawing upon the ancient, grim traditions of our Gothic ancestors and the disciplined military manuals of the Romans, we have formed the Red Guard. These elite shock troops are recruited exclusively from the highest mountain villages of the Crimea, trained to fight in the pitch-black tunnels of our fortresses and the claustrophobic ravines of the coast. Armed with heavy polearms and the latest flintlock pistols, they are masters of the sudden, devastating raids. Their reputation for never taking prisoners and never retreating makes them the most feared infantry in the Euxine basin, capable of breaking the morale of even the most hardened regiments.

FEO.name: The Iron Harvest
FEO.desc: The Gothic-Greek hybrid culture of Theodoro has fully shed its defensive shell, transforming into a 'War Machine'. No longer content with mere cliffside survival, we have industrialized our mountain strongholds into massive foundries and barracks, producing a professional officer corps and a conscript army trained in the brutal school of steppe warfare. Every citizen of the Principality is now a soldier first, viewing the surrounding plains not as a threat, but as a harvest field for Gothic glory and Roman reclamation. This 'Total War' footing allows us to strike with a ferocity that terrifies our larger neighbors, as we field a military machine that is disproportionately powerful relative to our small territorial size.

FEO.name: The Northern Star of Greece
FEO.desc: As the main Greek-speaking state in the North, Theodoro has become a symbol of religious resistance and cultural survival. We have established our Prince as the Protector of the Pontic Greeks, drawing immigrants and scholars from distant places. This prestige gives us a moral authority that transcends our borders, making us a key player in the grand religious struggles as the Northern Star of the Greek Orthodox faith.

FER.name: Ferrarese Silk
FER.desc: The silkworms of our lands and the skilled hands of our weavers have long produced cloth of exceptional quality, and we have turned this craft into one of the most reliable pillars of our economy. By regulating the trade and protecting our master artisans, we ensure that raw silk is processed into finished goods here rather than exported cheaply to competitors. This mastery of the cloth trade keeps our merchant guilds prosperous and ensures that every bolt produced here carries the prestige of our name to the markets of Europe.

FER.name: L'Adizión Erculéa
FER.desc: Ferrara has originated the concept of the 'Ideal City'. Instead of organic medieval growth, the state will implement large-scale, planned urban expansions with wide boulevards and symmetrical plazas. This will be the first example of modern urban planning in Europe, designed to reflect the order and majesty of the state. It will improve public health, facilitate military movement, and make Ferrara the most modern and prestigious nation in the West.

FER.name: Lo Studio di Ferrara
FER.desc: The University of Ferrara, founded by the Este and among the first of its kind, has attracted humanists and jurists from across Italy to our court. Under the guidance of eminent scholars, our classrooms become workshops of the New Learning, training the lettered servants and diplomats our growing state requires. This institution ensures that knowledge and new institutions spread faster through our lands than in any realm that relies on war alone.

FER.name: The Court of Letters
FER.desc: Our court has become the most celebrated literary gathering in Italy, where poets recite in the great halls and scholars debate philosophy in the gardens, their work supported as an instrument of statecraft as much as a private pleasure. Our name is synonymous with excellence in the vernacular tradition, attracting talents from every corner of the peninsula who compete for our favor and patronage. This reputation for culture deepens our artistic heritage and turns every great work produced here into an advertisement for the prestige of our state.

FER.name: The Curtesia
FER.desc: As the free communes transitioned into Signorie (Lordships), the Ferrarese court became a center of Late Medieval chivalry. This was a cultural synthesis of French Arthurian legends and Italian humanist wit. It created a sophisticated courtly etiquette that has become the gold standard for European nobility, turning our court into a diplomatic hub where the 'Art of the Possible' is practiced through refined conversation and artistic patronage.

FER.name: The Po Delta Reclamation
FER.desc: The marshy delta of the Po has long been a wasteland of standing water and malarial fog on our doorstep. By organizing a systematic program of drainage and embankment, we transform these wetlands into productive farmland, adding to our tax base while reducing the disease burden on our border communities. This transformation of the landscape into something orderly and profitable is our approach to governance made visible, the state as engineer of the land itself.

FLA.name: Flemish Cloth
FLA.desc: The Flemish Cloth industry is the envy of the world. Merchants come from far away to sell their Wool in Flanders, where we manufacture the best quality Cloth.

FLA.name: Flemish Renaissance
FLA.desc: As one of the most prosperous regions on the continents, much of the wealth we have created naturally flows toward artistic patronage. Flemish merchants commission master painters to create art that, while perhaps not practical, casts light over even the cloudiest of days. With dozens of our merchants actively hiring artists and commissioning new pieces, we are creating a distinctive Renaissance of our own.

FLA.name: Prospering Agriculture
FLA.desc: As our cloth, luxury goods, and financial industries face growing competition, it is becoming obvious that we need to manage our land use better. By creating regional granaries, we further diversify our economy, and bolster our food stores against famine or poor harvests.

FLO.name: Arte della Lana
FLO.desc: The Arte della Lana — the Wool Guild — is one of the most powerful of the seven major guilds of Florence, controlling every stage of the wool trade from the purchase of raw fleece to the sale of finished cloth. Its membership encompasses merchants, dyers, weavers, and finishers, all bound by strict quality standards enforced by guild inspectors. Granting formal recognition to the Arte entrenches the influence of the merchant class and ensures that Florence's reputation for fine cloth remains unmatched across the continent.

FLO.name: Florence Guilds
FLO.desc:
The different artisans and merchants of Florence traditionally are associates in different guilds. This ensures not only a high standard of quality for the products, but also avoids breeding unfair competition. However, the power and influence these guilds hold as a result is undeniable.

This unlocks the law Primacy of Florentine Guilds.

FLO.name: Signoria Council
FLO.desc: The Signoria of Florence is the name of the council of nine that governs the city, its members taken from the different guilds. Every two months, a lottery is held to reelect the council members. This constant shuffling ensures that the interests of the Republic prevail over personal ones. The fact all its members come from the guilds, though, makes it so that the same families are always the ones in charge.

FLO.name: Fiorino d'Oro
FLO.desc: Since 1252, the gold Fiorino d'Oro struck at our mint has been the most trusted currency in Christendom, accepted without question from the counting houses of London to the bazaars of Alexandria because its weight and purity never varied through the ambitions of a dozen kings. Merchants who trade in florins trade in our reputation: every exchange carried out in our coin is a quiet advertisement for the solidity of Florentine governance and the reliability of the institutions that stand behind it. This universal confidence in our currency smooths every transaction conducted in our courts, and keeps the treasury supplied with the tax revenue that only a genuinely trusted medium of exchange can consistently generate.

FLO.name: Florentine Bastions
FLO.desc: The military engineers of our city have mastered the design of low-profile angled bastions whose sloped walls scatter artillery fire and eliminate the blind spots that made older round towers so easy to undermine. Every significant stronghold we build draws on the geometry our architects have refined, producing fortifications that are both cheaper to garrison and far harder for any attacker to breach. This mastery of the Trace Italienne makes our walls the most modern in Italy and transforms the cost of holding them into a manageable advantage rather than a treasury drain.

FLO.name: Florentine Citizen Militia
FLO.desc: Machiavelli's argument against mercenary armies fell for generations on reluctant ears (the guilds preferred to pay condottieri than to march themselves) but the catastrophes of 1494 and 1512 demonstrated at ruinous cost what hired soldiers will and will not die for. We answer by organizing the men of our districts into standing companies, trained and equipped at public expense, whose stake in the defense of Florence is not a monthly wage but their own homes and trades. Arming our own citizens produces infantry that will hold when paid soldiers would retreat, a core of men who fight for something that cannot be renegotiated at the end of the campaign season.

FLO.name: Florentine Merchant Houses
FLO.desc: The great families of our city have built commercial networks that span the continent (agents in London, factors in Bruges, correspondents in Alexandria) so that the letters of exchange bearing our names pass as freely as coin in cities that have never seen our walls. By formalizing and expanding these networks under the protection of our constitutional government, we ensure that our merchants operate from a position of stability and trust that no prince-led rival can easily replicate. This reach of our Merchant Houses drives the revenue of every trade we conduct and opens the most distant and profitable markets to the goods our workshops produce.

FLO.name: Florentine School
FLO.desc: The workshops of Florence (Giotto, Brunelleschi, Masaccio, Botticelli, and Leonardo) have redefined what painting and sculpture mean to an entire civilization, each generation expanding the boundaries of what the human eye and human hand can achieve in stone, pigment, and bronze. No patron who wishes to be taken seriously commissions a work without first consulting Florentine masters, and our artists carry this reputation wherever they are summoned, turning the name of the city into a credential that outlasts any individual canvas. This unbroken tradition of artistic leadership fills our ateliers with the finest talent in Italy and ensures that the works we produce command the admiration, and the gold, of the most demanding patrons in Christendom.

FLO.name: The Camerata Fiorentina
FLO.desc: In the house of Count Giovanni de' Bardi, musicians, poets, and scholars have been gathering to recapture what they imagine the performance style of ancient Greek tragedy must have sounded like, a quest that will produce something entirely new and entirely ours. The conversations, experiments, and compositions that emerge from these evenings are drawing gifted performers who value the creative freedom our court offers over the higher wages they might command elsewhere. This circle of artistic innovators, the Camerata Fiorentina, makes our city the origin of a musical revolution that will spread our influence into every court that hears what we have created.

FRA.name: Ancient Taxation
FRA.desc: Historically, taxes have been imposed and collected only in times of need, not by a recurrent system.

FRA.name: Feudal Nobility
FRA.desc: Feudalism has a tight grip on court affairs. Powerful nobles and autonomous, decentralized subjects have unprecedented amounts of freedom and say in our internal administration.

FRA.name: Gabelle
FRA.desc: A government reform permitting a Salt tax, which places great strain on the populace — and plentiful gold in the state coffers.

FRA.name: Louis Legal Code
FRA.desc: Following centuries of disparate legal codes across Northern and Southern France, the Code Louis has been established, unifying France under one universal legislative system.

FRA.name: Monarchy
FRA.desc: Following centuries of heavy decentralization, France has consolidated many of its fragmented appanage and ducal lands, paving the way for a more modern state.

FRA.name: Chancellor Nobles
FRA.desc: Deriving from the lesser branches of the Nobility, these administrators are responsible for drafting governmental decisions into legal documents, forming the basis of our administration.

FRA.name: Compromise Great Ordinance
FRA.desc: A compromise agreement between the Crown and Étienne Marcel, where the Crown cedes power to Marcel. In return, the Estates-General has granted the request to levy more taxes.

FRA.name: Great Offices of the Crown of France
FRA.desc: The most important governmental offices within our central administration are reserved for the Nobility within our realm.

FRA.name: Leadership of Étienne Marcel
FRA.desc: Étienne Marcel's influence has made the Burghers a powerful force in the Estates-General.

FRA.name: Noble Armies
FRA.desc: Permitting the Nobility to maintain personal armies is an excellent way to ensure they contribute when we form larger state armies, while also incurring more influence.

FRA.name: Permanent Residence in Versailles
FRA.desc: Expansions have been made to Versailles allowing for members of the Nobility to take up permanent residence at the palace alongside the family. While those not of the family enjoy the luxuries of the palace, it has come at the cost of greatly diminished political influence, in order to maintain the favor of the ruler. This abandonment of their personal estates has also left less room for political intrigue and plotting, making them beholden to the rule of Versailles.

FRA.name: Residence in Versailles
FRA.desc: The family has extended an offer of residence for members of the prominent Nobility dynasties to live in the palace of Versailles.

FRA.name: The Great Ordinance
FRA.desc: Following immense pressure from Étienne Marcel, France is currently governed by terms of Marcel's Great Ordinance. In return for granting him great influence, the state has the backing of the Estates-General to levy more taxes.

FRA.name: Villes Franches
FRA.desc: Several of our market towns have experienced considerable growth in recent decades. As a result, they have become symbols of the expansion of the Crown's power throughout the kingdom, in opposition to the feudal lords who dominate the countryside.

FRA.name: Estates General
FRA.desc: The Estates General is the assembly of the feudal government of. It has a legislative and consultative role, and represents the three estates of the country: the Nobility, the Clergy, and the Commoners, which itself encompasses the Burghers. Unlike other Parliaments and Assemblies, the approval of the Estates General when making adjustments to the law, such as tax increases, is optional.

FRA.name: A Knightly Nobility
FRA.desc: The aristocrats of our nation have always provided the best soldiers for our armies. Their well-trained fighters will serve our nation and defeat our enemies in the name of righteous glory!

FRA.name: Code Civil
FRA.desc: We must replace the chaotic patchwork of laws governing our state with a single, unified legal code that applies to our entire population. This Code Civil will serve as the foundation of our government and establish a just system for everyone in our realm.

FRA.name: Consolidation of the Country
FRA.desc: Our influence over other states is undeniable. Why not use this persuasive power to incorporate them directly into our country?

FRA.name: Establishment of Recettes Générales
FRA.desc: The intendants responsible for collecting the taxes of the people shall not be appointed by the estates, but by our ruler directly. This way, we will ensure these officers will be loyal to the ruler alone, and gather all of the rightful tribute owed.

FRA.name: Estates-General
FRA.desc: According to some, the Estates-General have existed since 1303. Over time, its form has shifted from being a council of royalty appointees to one of elected representatives. This change in structure has given the Estates-General, and the taxes levied by them, greater legitimacy.

FRA.name: French Language in All Courts
FRA.desc: For a long time, Latin has been the language of cultural exchange in Europe... but to be honest, that language is nearly as dead as the ancient Romans who spoke it. We need to find a new lingua franca, and nothing says 'lingua franca' like French.

FRA.name: Gendarme Companies
FRA.desc: Reliance on a levy system has exposed our government to great risks, and has proved to be severely limiting. We should recruit heavily armed cavalrymen and pay them a fixed salary in order to create a standing army.

FRA.name: Grande Armée
FRA.desc: When measured against our adversaries, our need for military reform becomes painfully apparent. By introducing modern drilling techniques, we can transform our troops into a disciplined force capable of destroying any foe in combat.

FRA.name: Historic Claims
FRA.desc: We trace our nation's lineage back to the empire of Charlemagne, and can therefore claim all those lands to be part of our rightful territory. With the support of dedicated courts, we will be able to identify and re-claim all of this long territory.

FRA.name: Innovative Fortifications
FRA.desc: Our genius in fortification does not represent a radical departure in their design; rather, the innovation comes from the placement of the fortresses. By taking maximum advantage of local terrain, even the most basic fort requires more effort and supplies to take.

FRA.name: La Cour de France
FRA.desc: Our diplomatic maneuvers are renowned for their complexity and finesse, and our skilled envoys emulated across the continent. Yet only a fool would become complacent now; we could further refine our diplomacy through measures such as cultivating networks of informants and perfecting the art of negotiation. Let other nations muddle through yesterday's techniques while we pioneer tomorrow's.

FRA.name: Liberté, Egalité, Fraternité
FRA.desc: With all men declared to be equal under our new laws, adherents of other beliefs are finally allowed full participation in our government, and may thus now contribute to our national progress.

FRA.name: Northern Mannerism
FRA.desc: As a nation much enriched by the Renaissance, we should invest in the creation of a unique, distinctively French aesthetic. By inviting foreign artists to our realm and sponsoring a school for artist training directly, we will be able to brand any artistic works produced as identifiably French.

FRA.name: Reliance on Privateers
FRA.desc: Direct competition with other maritime powers could be detrimental to our finances. We should empower our mercantile fleet to plunder and seize the merchant ships of our enemies. This will not only ensure a healthy income for our state, but also disrupt the maritime economies of our rivals.

FRA.name: The Philosophes
FRA.desc: We are proud to be the home of so many of the most renowned philosophers of these enlightened times. These thinkers produce a constant stream of groundbreaking ideas, which are stimulating advances in all fields, from the most trifling to the most vital.

FRA.name: Élan!
FRA.desc: Cultivating the doctrine of attack is the hallmark of our army. Our men must fight with élan, spirit and vigor, giving us a clear edge on the battlefield.

FRE.name: An Army for Bavaria
FRE.desc: Only with a formidable standing army will we have the military might necessary to match our ambitions. With careful focus, we can expand it without having a ruinous impact on our state's finances.

FRE.name: Bavaria Coin
FRE.desc: Our realm needs a new standardized coin to serve as our national unified currency. Establishing a state-owned mint in our capital would ensure our total control over this new coinage.

FRE.name: Bavarian Cultural Institutions
FRE.desc: With our homeland at the feet of the beautiful Alps, we are a destination for artists from all over Europe, who seek inspiration in our incredible landscape. If we were to construct and support the appropriate cultural institutions, we could refine our court into a center of refinement and elegance, one that could rival even the most prestigious powers of Europe.

FRE.name: Bavarian Dukedom
FRE.desc: We have been granted the rulership of Bavaria directly by the Emperor! By embellishing ourselves as the divinely-appointed protectors of Bavaria, we will ensure our legitimacy cannot be questioned.

FRE.name: Bavarian Hofkriegsrat
FRE.desc: Establishing a council with the sole duty of advising our ruler during times of conflict will help us develop a more capable fighting force.

FRE.name: Bavarian Imperial Knights
FRE.desc: Our nobles have distinguished themselves as formidable knights in the service of the Holy Roman Empire. We should nurture and scrupulously maintain these troops to ensure the survival of our ducal integrity.

FRE.name: Bavarian Purity Law
FRE.desc: The excellent quality of our beer has been celebrated for centuries, but for our brews to achieve legendary status, we must ensure their continued prestige and superiority for all time. Several rulers in the past have created regulations and standards for the brewing of this wonderful substance; and we could use this fact as a stamp of our breweries' quality.

FRE.name: Dreams of Unification
FRE.desc: We once were ruled by Bavaria, unified in culture and allied under a single banner. We must ensure that the new Bavarian state is equally mighty, a home worthy of its strong and proud people.

FRE.name: One Faith for Bavaria
FRE.desc: We must ensure our people remain united in their faith, and that they will not be divided by heretical thoughts.

FRE.name: Practical Diplomacy
FRE.desc: No matter if we are answering to an Imperial overlord or cozying up to a potential foreign ally, our diplomats must be prepared for everything. But only if they keep Bavarian interests first and foremost in their efforts will we be able to claim true success in our diplomatic maneuverings.

FRE.name: Skilled Brewers
FRE.desc: Our lands are rich in the crops and fresh water required to brew beer, and our people readily enjoy this abundance. Many small breweries could grow into successful businesses, with the right support.

FRE.name: Trading Hubs of Bavaria
FRE.desc: Our lands are frequently crossed by merchants wishing to trade Salt, Silver, and Livestock in the rich lands to our south. We would be foolish not to take advantage of their presence, and therefore will establish bustling trade hubs in our own lands to attract their business.

GBS.name: Chott Salt Works
GBS.desc: Our salt flat works at the edge of the Chott el-Djerid, the great seasonal salt pan stretching inland from the Gulf of Gabes, supply the Mediterranean and Saharan salt trade with grades from coarse industrial salt to the fine table salt our coastal evaporation produces. Our salt houses, scale houses, and customs posts route every load through bonded accounting, and the central treasury captures revenue from both ends of the salt trade chain. The salt trade fills the crown's coffers with large and steady revenues.

GBS.name: Coastal Date Industry
GBS.desc: Our crown develops the date export economy of the Gulf coastline, sinking new artesian wells, extending the palm groves along the coastal plain, and laying paved roads that link Gabes, Djerba, and the smaller coastal markets to the central oasis. With each expansion the shared works lower the cost of working the land across the oasis hinterland. Along the coast our fields and roads spread farther than the inland oases, cut off from the sea, can ever reach.

GBS.name: Coastal Oasis
GBS.desc: Our unique geography of sea and oasis, with palm groves growing within sight of the Mediterranean shore on the Gulf of Gabes, supports a rare combination of date palm production, citrus orchards, henna gardens, and sea fishing in the same agrarian unit. Our peasants harvest dates in autumn, sail for tuna in spring, and trade across both the Saharan and the Mediterranean trade circuits without ever leaving our oasis hinterland. Where coast meets oasis, our state enjoys richer harvests and a steadier prosperity than purely inland oases can know.

GBS.name: Djerba Commercial Bond
GBS.desc: Our tight commercial bond with the island of Djerba, sustained by daily traffic of fishing and trade across the narrow Gulf of Gabes channel, extends our merchant network across the Mediterranean basin through the Djerba-resident Sephardic, Genoese, and Maltese commercial houses. Our agents conduct business in every Mediterranean port through Djerba intermediaries, and our shipping factors coordinate with the Djerba pilot houses. Customs posts capture revenue from both the island and the mainland traffic. By way of Djerba our state holds the sea trade more surely, and our merchants reach farther than those of purely inland coastal cities.

GBS.name: Gulf of Gabes Anchorage
GBS.desc: Our natural harbor on the Gulf of Gabes, sheltered by the Kerkennah islands, deep enough for Mediterranean galleys, and supplied with fresh water from the oasis itself, supports a fleet of coastal galleys and a sailor pool drawn from our oasis and coastal inhabitants in equal measure. Our shipwrights train in the techniques of both the eastern Mediterranean galley building and the Saharan caravan camel husbandry that our hinterland requires. Our anchorage on the Gulf draws a steady stream of sailors and builds a tradition of the sea unknown to purely inland oases.

GBS.name: Henna and Dye Export
GBS.desc: Our coastal oasis henna gardens, indigo plots, and saffron fields produce the dyes that European cloth finishers and Maghrebi tanneries demand in the highest grades, supplying the colorants for Andalusi-style tilework, Mediterranean wool dyeing, and our own coastal cotton industries. Our merchant houses control the bonded warehouses at the Gulf shore, and our brokers extend credit to the dye grove owners. Shipping agents route the export through Tunis, La Goulette, and the smaller Tunisian ports. Our dye exports fill the crown's coffers with the profits of a luxury trade and keep our merchants thriving.

GEL.name: A Healthy Economy
GEL.desc: We have expanded our borders not only by the sword, but through careful financial planning, which allowed us to purchase influence over desirable territories — or to buy them outright. With continued wise budget management, this economic trend should be sustainable.

GEL.name: A Warring Spirit
GEL.desc: Some may call us bellicose, but that is only because they fear our might. A well-trained standing army is essential for survival in this chaotic age. Our adversaries will soon learn to respect our hardened spirit.

GEL.name: Expand the Kwarteers
GEL.desc: As in the case of Brabant, Guelders has traditionally been divided into four quarters. This system of provinces arranged around a strong central city has proven to be an efficient way to govern our nation, and we should apply this system to new regions that join our realm in the future.

GEN.name: Compagna Communis
GEN.desc: This is the meeting of all the trade associations of Genoa, and the noble lords of the surrounding valleys and coast, joining together to form the city's government.

GEN.name: Diarchy Republic
GEN.desc:
No man should rule a country alone, or else we are no better than the tyrannical despots who try to subjugate our people.
The Capitano del Popolo shall be a dual position where members of the Spinola and Doria families will each hold office. The rivalry between their alberghi keeps the Republic restless, but their Diarchs share the burdens of state and their countinghouses keep the coin flowing.

GEN.name: Great and Minor Councils of Genoa
GEN.desc: Created by Admiral Andrea Doria after reforming the government, the Great and Minor Councils of Genoa are the two legislative bodies of the state. The Great Council represents the members of the Burghers while the Minor Council is made up of the Nobility.

GEN.name: The Twenty-Eight Alberghi
GEN.desc: After the political changes of the last century, the influential House of Doria is promoting a reform of the constitution, eliminating the factions that plagued our republic in the past. These factions are replaced by a new oligarchic government, which includes the twenty-eight most important families, referred to as the -Eight Alberghi.

GEN.name: Genoese Crossbowmen
GEN.desc: Genoese Crossbowmen are a respected military unit that was used by the Genoese during the First Crusade up until now. Equipped with Genoese crossbows and the pavise, these infantrymen serve as the protection of their home as well as mercenaries in Europe.

GEN.name: Genoese Galley
GEN.desc: The Genoese Galley is the backbone of the Genoese navy. Lighter and longer than other galleys used in the Mediterranean Sea, this ship is able to achieve unmatched speed while also having a significant cargo advantage at the cost of maneuverability and durability.

GEN.name: Genoese Crossbowmen
GEN.desc: Genoese Crossbowmen are a respected military unit that was used by the Genoese during the First Crusade up until now. Equipped with Genoese crossbows and the pavise, these infantrymen serve as the protection of their home as well as mercenaries in Europe.

GEN.name: Genoese Galley
GEN.desc: The Genoese Galley is the backbone of the Genoese navy. Lighter and longer than other galleys used in the Mediterranean Sea, this ship is able to achieve unmatched speed while also having a significant cargo advantage at the cost of maneuverability and durability.

GEN.name: Genoese School
GEN.desc: The prosperity of centuries of trade has made Genoa a city of collectors and patrons, and from this milieu there has emerged a distinct Genoese School of painting celebrated for its mastery of dramatic light and rich texture. Artists nurtured in our republic have carried Genoese taste and prestige to courts and collections across Europe. This flourishing of artistic culture deepens our traditions and extends our influence far beyond what politics alone can achieve.

GEN.name: La Superba
GEN.desc: We have built our republic on the twin pillars of commerce and credit, pioneering instruments of debt and exchange that have funded our trading posts from the Levant to the Black Sea since the early Middle Ages. Our colonies and comptoirs across the Mediterranean are as much diplomatic outposts as commercial ones, granting us a reach that no purely military power could match. This network of finance and statecraft ensures our bankers and envoys work as one, reducing the cost of credit and keeping more ambassadors in our service.

GEN.name: Porto Franco
GEN.desc: As the great Atlantic trade routes have drawn commerce away from the Mediterranean, we have answered by declaring our harbor a Porto Franco, a free port open to merchants of all nations, exempt from the duties and restrictions that weigh down our rivals. Ships that once bypassed Liguria now put in at our quays, and the city fills again with foreign factors, warehouses, and coin. This openness to all comers turns our harbor into one of the busiest entrepôts of the western Mediterranean, drawing trade and people in equal measure.

GEN.name: The Age of the Genoese
GEN.desc: The great banking fairs of Piacenza have made Genoese financiers the indispensable creditors of the Spanish crown and the arbiters of European capital flows for generations. The immense wealth that passes through our hands finds its way into the palaces and villas of our merchant nobility, who have built the most far-reaching commercial network in the Mediterranean world. This supremacy over European finance makes our merchant network more efficient than any rival's, and the trade it channels through Genoa fills our treasury with returns drawn from every major commercial circuit in Europe.

GEN.name: The New Republic
GEN.desc: In the turbulent years of the early sixteenth century, Andrea Doria restructured our republic, consolidating the old noble factions into twenty-eight great houses, the Aberghi (Alberghi in standard Italian: great houses), and granting us a political stability we had long been denied. That same pragmatic spirit reshaped our fleet, redirecting our naval expertise toward service across the Mediterranean rather than tying us to a single strategic posture. This reinvention allows us to maintain our navy at reduced cost and to convert our war galleys to lighter vessels when the moment demands it.
mods: Can Convert Galley to Light Ships

GEO.name: Office of the Eristavi
GEO.desc: One of the most influential cornerstones of our administration, the title of Eristavi is granted to powerful noble families, allowing them the undisputed authority to recruit and lead armies under their banner. Those who hold this office also enjoy a dominant position in our internal affairs.
mods: Head of the Cabinet Promotion Cost Modifier

GEO.name: Regulations of the Royal Court
GEO.desc: A series of documents denoting the main functions of our government, from coronation ceremony etiquette, to the daily activities of the Crown, to the maintenance of our army. This framework serves as a robust basis for our government and the privy council known as savaziro.

GEO.name: Bagrationi Dynasty
GEO.desc: A dynasty so old that its origins are shrouded in mystery, kings and queens of the Bagrationi house have ruled Georgia ever since the 9th century, first as its princes and then as monarchs.

GEO.name: Beacon of Christianity
GEO.desc: Georgia has been a haven for Christianity in the Caucasus for centuries, even after being surrounded and isolated by followers of Islam. The ardent faith of our people is a source of inspiration for all our religious brethren.

GEO.name: Davit the Builder
GEO.desc: Considered the greatest ruler in the history of our country, King Davit the Builder brought Georgia to its pinnacle. He built a powerful, culturally influential kingdom, and a beacon for Christianity and the Georgian people.

GEO.name: Georgian Golden Age
GEO.desc: Georgia enjoyed a cultural and religious Golden Age that was brought to a sudden stop, due to the Mongol invasions. That period witnessed the peak of our cultural achievements, but we will now return to it, and achieve even greater heights.

GEO.name: Georgian Numismatics
GEO.desc: Our country has a rich tradition of minting coins, inscribing them not only in Georgian but also in Arabic and Persian, as they serve as currency for trade through our country and those that neighbor us.

GEO.name: Georgian Principalities
GEO.desc: Our regional administration is divided into many different principalities and territories. Delegating authority this way allows us to exert our rule more effectively.

GEO.name: Georgian Resilience
GEO.desc: Our country has been torn apart, by external and internal influences, more than once in its long history. However, like the phoenix of legend, it has risen from the ashes and established itself as a presence to reckon with each time. The resilience of our people is commendable.

GEO.name: Georgian Titles
GEO.desc: 'King of Kings, strong and invincible, majestic and protector of the holy kingdom of the Abkhazians, Iberians, Ranis, Kakhetians, Armenians, Shahanshah and Shirvanshah, of the East and the West, of the South and the North, of both countries, of two thrones and crowns, the godlike Suzerain and the Sovereign of the Throne.' The titles of our ruler are numerous, and all at court shall respect them!

GEO.name: Legacy of Saint George
GEO.desc: Our association with the legendary Saint George is well known through both the Christian and Muslim worlds. As he bravely faced and slew the fearsome dragon, so will our soldiers face our enemies in battle.

GEO.name: Legacy of Tamar
GEO.desc: Tamar was one of the greatest rulers our nation ever had. Her military and cultural successes are legendary, and the mere utterance of her name still stirs reverence in all Georgian hearts.

GFS.name: Berber Substratum
GFS.desc: Our oasis preserves a distinct Berber substratum: the Gafsa-dialect, the matrilineal inheritance customs of the older clans, the pre-Islamic burial sites scattered across the Jebel Orbata, and the genealogies that trace many notable families back to the Zenata tribes of the pre-Hilāli era. Our Arabic and Berber speakers coexist in the same households, and our judicial customary law preserves Berber tribal precedent alongside the Mālikī shari'a. Oral traditions keep the Capsian and pre-Roman cultural memories that no Arabic-only southern oasis can claim. Our dual cultural inheritance makes our urban culture a hybrid, unlike the more thoroughly Arabized Sahel coastal towns.

GFS.name: Capsa Aqueduct
GFS.desc: The Roman aqueduct of Capsa, built in the second century to feed the legionary garrison and the surrounding olive estates from the springs of the Jebel Orbata, still channels water into our oasis through the same stone conduits that the Romans laid, maintained across the millennium by the resident communities of the ksar. Our hammam baths, orchard cisterns, and market troughs all draw from this single inherited engineering. Our masons preserve the techniques required to patch and clean the conduit when sections collapse. The Roman waterwork carries to Gafsa a flow of water that no purely medieval engineering could replicate from scratch.

GFS.name: Oasis Chamber
GFS.desc: Our inter-tribal majlis, convening representatives of the Hammama, the Frashich, the Awlad Bouyahia, and the resident urban notables, meets quarterly in the central qasba to apportion irrigation rights, mediate caravan route disputes, and ratify the local share of tribute owed to whichever northern power claims us this generation. The chamber is hereditary but consultative, our notables serve without salary but accept hospitality and customary gifts, and our resolutions bind the participating tribes through customary law rather than imposed force. A standing inter-tribal council keeps our frontier oasis politically continuous, as no purely tribal or purely urban government could in our exposed position.

GFS.name: Pomegranates and Dates
GFS.desc: The pomegranate orchards of Gafsa, famed across the Maghreb since the days of Ibn Khaldūn for their size, sweetness, and keeping qualities, and the date palms of our oasis belt produce fruits that the caravan buyers of Tunis, Tripoli, and Sijilmasa specifically commission rather than accept substitutes. Our orchard owners hold hereditary leases on individual plots of palm and pomegranate. Irrigation guildsmen apportion well-water by ancient share table, and our caravan masters price each consignment by origin grove rather than by bulk. Our specialization in fruit export gives our oasis a niche luxury trade that no broader fruit-producing oasis can displace from the elite markets of the Mediterranean.

GFS.name: Saharan Corridor
GFS.desc: Our oasis sits at the Mediterranean-end of the western Saharan corridor. Caravans from Touat, Tafilalt, and the central Sahara converge on Gafsa before continuing north to the Sahel coast or east to the Hafsid heartland, while our merchant houses provision the southbound legs with grain, cloth, and pottery. Our caravanserais host sub-Saharan, Berber, and Andalusi traders side by side; our customs officers tax the through traffic at modest rates that keep the corridor profitable; and our oasis economy depends on the seasonal arrivals as much as on the resident orchards. Standing on the desert road, Gafsa grows strong in trade and diplomacy as no purely agricultural oasis could.

GFS.name: Southern Intellectuals
GFS.desc: Our generation of reformist intellectuals, Gafsa-born and Zaytuna-trained, contributes correspondents, essayists, and modernist jurists to the Tunisian Nahḍa circles in the capital, balancing the metropolitan voices with the perspective of the southern oasis interior. Our pamphleteers debate beylical fiscal policy in the new Arabic press, and our jurist scholars publish commentaries on Khayr ad-Dīn's reform regulations. Young administrators staff the new bureaus that the Sadiki graduates open in Tunis. Our southern intellectuals give our oasis a reformist and modernizing voice from the frontier that no purely metropolitan reform movement could capture.

GLH.name: Kipchak Khanate
GLH.desc: Our great country is also called the Kipchak Khanate, ruling over all the territories of the Cuman-Kipchak Confederation. With such swathes of land under our command, the armies we can gather will be innumerable.

GLH.name: Legacy of Jochi
GLH.desc: After Genghis Khān died, his son Jochi also passed not long after. However, his presence and legacy are still felt in our country, to the point that we are still known as the Ulus of Jochi. Warriors flock to our banners to uphold that legacy.

GLH.name: Legacy of the Golden Horde
GLH.desc: We were one of the main constituent parts of Genghis Khān's empire, and we represent the main political force in Eastern Europe and the Steppes. The world shall tremble before us!

GLH.name: Modernization of the Steppes
GLH.desc: It was long ago that Genghis Khān's armies first seized control of the steppes. Our country has since surpassed our ancestor's every expectation, and now we stand as a global power on our own merit. We shall now begin the process of modernizing our territories, so that one day we shall be the beacon of all the world.

GLH.name: Perso-Mongol Administration
GLH.desc: Our ancestors refined our administrative system over the centuries, and they were not shy about incorporating the ideas and methods of the cultures they subdued. Our current system of administration is in part based on traditions dating back to the Great Genghis Khān himself, and in part on what we have adopted from Persian and Muslim bureaucrats in the lands conquered.

GLH.name: Religious Pragmatism
GLH.desc:
Constraining, inflexible doctrine has never won many admirers among the Tatar hordes. When the Great Öz Beg Khān adopted Islam, it was the faith of a Sufi Shayḵ or a zealous Qāḍī that he invited into his lands.

Centuries of tradition and loyalty are what we would rather build our state upon. Religion has a part to play, but we would prefer to see our country thrive than to fall apart in the chaos of forced religious homogeneity.

GLH.name: Secure the Trade Routes
GLH.desc: Not all riches in this world originate in our territory. Trade is the source of all wealth, and the Golden Horde has always protected merchants. By ensuring the safety of anyone who wishes to move goods through our country, we can ensure a steady stream of furs, silk, spices, and other necessities to our cities. Whether they choose to sell their goods to us or not, their mere presence will generate wealth for our people.

GLH.name: Tatar Traditions
GLH.desc: Our empire may no longer be ruled from horseback, but our armies remain masters of the mount. Over the centuries, we have stayed true to our origins, ensuring that few can match the skill of our riders. As we go forward and adopt new technology and tactics when needed, we build on the strong organization and martial traditions of the Mongol Empire.

GRA.name: The Jewel of Al-'Andalus
GRA.desc: We are the only surviving member of the formerly Muslim realms that populated Al-'Andalus in the past. Huge Muslim empires have risen and fallen throughout Iberia, fragmenting in the process. As one of those fragmented parts, it is our destiny to reunify the people of Iberia under our banner.
mods: War Score vs other Religion Efficiency
Pop Assimilation Speed (We must have won the Battle for the Strait situation)

GRA.name: Late Ṯaḡrī
GRA.desc: Generations of Ṯaḡrī service have settled the corps into a hereditary class of frontier wardens. The march is in their bones, the passes mapped in their grandfathers' songs, the drill inherited from their fathers' company. They still draw a peasant's wage and a peasant's bread, yet a column of them can hold the sierra through a full season of campaign while a knightly retinue would starve in a fortnight.

GRA.name: Ṯaḡrī
GRA.desc: Drawn from the marcher villages of the ṯuḡūr, the ṯaḡrī fight as foot spearmen who know every pass and watercourse of the Andalusi frontier. They train cheaply on village rations, march for weeks on what a Castilian column eats in days, and answer the call at the first beacon. Their weapons are plain and their pay is meager, yet no force in Iberia matches their endurance along the mountain marches.

GRA.name: A New Golden Era
GRA.desc: Al-'Andalus was once the intellectual heart of the Islamic world, producing Ibn Rushd's commentaries on Aristotle, az-Zahrāwī's surgical compendium, and Ibn Ṭufayl's philosophical novel Ḥayy ibn Yaqẓān. We will refound the Madrasa Yūsufiyya in Granada, recall scholars from Fez and Tlemcen, and translate the new Spanish and French scientific works into Arabic for the use of our physicians and astronomers. This intellectual revival proves that the lamp of Andalusi learning has only been dimmed, never extinguished, and gives our state an influence over minds across the Maghreb that no Christian neighbor can replicate.

GRA.name: A Strong Rule
GRA.desc: Three generations of Nasrid succession crises (the dethronements of Muḥammad VI, Muḥammad VIII, and Muḥammad IX) have made factional warfare between the Banū as-Sarrāj (the Abencerrajes) and the Banū l-'Aziz the defining feature of court politics. Under a strong emir, the rival clans are confined to ceremonial offices, the Alhambra guard is renewed with loyal Mudejars, and the great vizierate is reserved for men of demonstrated competence rather than blood claim. This dynastic consolidation ends the internal bleeding that has cost us more cities than every Castilian campaign combined.

GRA.name: Adaptive Trade
GRA.desc: For three centuries Granadan merchants have stood astride the only legal trade channel between the Christian Mediterranean and the gold caravans of the Sahara, exchanging Castilian wool and Genoese silver for Sudanese gold dust at the entrepôts of Málaga and Almuñécar. The Portuguese rounding of Cape Bojador now threatens to bypass us entirely, so we will charter new partnerships with the Wattāsid sultans of Fez and tighten Genoese commercial privileges at our ports. This reorientation of our trade lets the Nasrid economy survive the opening of the African coast that would otherwise have ended our centuries of commercial advantage.

GRA.name: Banū Naṣr
GRA.desc: We descend from the Banū l-Ḵazraj tribe of Yaṯrib through the lineage of Sa'd ibn 'Ubāda, a ṣaḥābī and companion of the Prophet Muḥammad. Our founder Muḥammad I ibn Naṣr, having served first as ally to Ferdinand III, secured the territories of Granada, Jaén, Almería, and Málaga as a tributary emirate after 1238. This dynastic legitimacy, rooted simultaneously in Arab tribal genealogy and prophetic association, gives the Nasrid throne a sacral authority that no Berber successor dynasty in al-'Andalus could ever claim.

GRA.name: Frontier Warriors
GRA.desc: Along the ṯuḡūr, every marcher village owes its sons to the beacon line, and the ṯaḡrī who answers that call knows the passes, the wells, and the seasonal raids of the Christian kings as well as any shepherd knows his hills. We arm him cheaply, feed him from his own village stores, and let the frontier itself school him in the only war that matters. This light infantry costs our treasury little but holds the sierra roads against forces that would need a season's supplies to match their knowledge of the ground.

GRA.name: Muṭawwi'a Armies
GRA.desc: The Muṭawwi'a, religiously motivated volunteers from the wider Islamic world, have been coming to Granada since the late thirteenth century to fight a defensive jihad on the last Andalusi frontier. North African Berber riders, Turkish archers passing through Ifriqiya, and Mamlūk-trained officers from Cairo accept Nasrid coin and the promise of paradise to swell our ranks beyond what our small population could ever raise. This pool of volunteer reinforcement lets a kingdom of three hundred thousand subjects field armies whose ferocity surprises every Castilian commander who has not faced them before.

GRA.name: Skillful Envoys
GRA.desc: The survival of the Nasrid emirate for two centuries past every other taifa rests not on armies but on the agility of our envoys at the courts of Castile, Aragon, the Marīnids, and the Genoese. The kātib al-sirr, our secretary of secrets, maintains a permanent cipher correspondence and a network of merchants doubling as informants from Tunis to Toulouse. This diplomatic skill plays Christian kingdoms against each other through six successive Castilian successions and three Marīnid invasions, buying our emirate decade upon decade of survival.

GRA.name: The Jamā'a
GRA.desc: The Jamā'a, literally 'the Community', is the standing consultative body of our emirate, convening the qāḍī al-jamā'a, the wazīr, the ḥājib, and the šayḵ al-ḡuzāt who commands the Marinid jihad-volunteers alongside our own court. We convene this body in its extraordinary capacity as the embodiment of the Community of believers, transforming our decisions of war, tribute, and succession from emiral fiat into the consent of the whole polity. This council closes the door to unilateral concessions wrested from a divided emirate and ensures that no faction — Christian king, Maghrebi sultan, or frontier chieftain — can deal with any single voice of ours as if it spoke for all.

GRA.name: The Ṯuḡūr
GRA.desc: The ṯuḡūr are the frontier marches of al-'Andalus, the wild zones between settled Christian Iberia and our emirate that we name, garrison, and bind to our court through grants of land and warrior-family privileges. We build the ṯaḡr forts astride every pass and ford, linking them into a continuous spine of resistance that slows any Christian advance and gives our own riders a place to muster and resupply. This organized frontier transforms the border clans from autonomous raiding parties into defenders with a formal stake in the emirate's survival.

GRA.name: Veteran Ṯaḡrī
GRA.desc: Four generations of frontier service have hardened the ṯaḡrī in our marches into a permanent warrior class, their families rooted in the same passes their grandfathers held and passing their captaincies from father to son. We pay the Late Ṯaḡrī no more than a village wage, and still they march for our banners on rations that would halt any Christian column we send against them. This veteran infantry gives us the most cost-efficient defense our frontier can produce, holding territory that would otherwise demand expensive mercenaries to garrison.

GRA.name: Ṭā'ifa
GRA.desc: When the Caliphate of Córdoba fell, al-'Andalus broke apart into a mosaic of petty emirates, called the ṭawā'if, each a court unto itself. Brilliant in learning yet jealous of one another, they could never stand alone against the Christian north. Bound now to a restored power in Iberia, a Ṭā'ifa keeps its own character while bending to the authority of a single sovereign.

GRA.name: Al-Ḡuzāt al-Mujāhidīn
GRA.desc: Al-Ḡuzāt al-Mujāhidīn are the volunteers of the faith, the North African cavalry who cross the strait to wage holy war on the frontier under their own Šayḵ. These ardent warriors fight with a zeal born of devotion, and their piety inspires our people to follow in their fervor.

GRA.name: Dār al-Ṭirāz
GRA.desc: The ostentous embroided clothes originating from Persia have long been used in the Islamic world as robes of honor the sovereign bestows upon those he favors. A well-funded royal Dār al-Ṭirāz workshop that weaves silk, brocade, and embroidery will clothe the court in splendor and send prized fabrics to every market.

GRA.name: Dīwān al-Mustaḵlaṣ
GRA.desc: The Dīwān al-Mustaḵlaṣ administers the sultan's private domain of estates, mills, and revenues set apart from the public treasury to fund the court and the Al-Ḥamrā'. A diligent stewardship keeps the crown wealthy and independent of its estates, but lax oversight invites the very officials who manage it to divert its riches into their own coffers.

GRA.name: Jamā'a
GRA.desc: The standing consultative body of our emirate, gathering the qāḍī al-jamā'a, the wazīr, the šayḵ al-ḡuzāt, and the leading clans of the frontier under a single roof, so that no faction speaks louder than the whole.

GRA.name: Promote Our Sovereignty
GRA.desc: Our chancery and our Clergy labor to remind every prince, every merchant, and every village that the realm stands as its own master. Patronage, public works, and the careful staging of ceremony all reinforce the dignity of our independent rule.

GRA.name: Qāḍī al-Jamā'a
GRA.desc: The Qāḍī al-Jamā'a is the chief judge of the community, who presides over the Mālikī courts and appoints the many local qāḍī of the realm. A respected judiciary system settles disputes by law recognized by all and lends the throne the legitimacy of justice, deepening the people's attachment to formal jurisprudence.

GRA.name: Wulāt al-Ṯuḡūr
GRA.desc: The Wulāt al-Ṯuḡūr are the wardens of the frontier marches. They garrison the border castles, watch the passes, and manage the truces and tribute that keep the larger Christian kingdoms at bay. A proper march bristles with defenders and buys the realm time through careful diplomacy, because if we neglect the frontier that emboldens our neighbors, who may smell weakness and press their claims harder.

GRA.name: Ṭā'ifa
GRA.desc: When the Caliphate of Córdoba fell, al-'Andalus broke apart into a mosaic of petty emirates, called the ṭawā'if, each a court unto itself. Brilliant in learning yet jealous of one another, they could never stand alone against the Christian north. Bound now to a restored power in Iberia, a Ṭā'ifa keeps its own character while bending to the authority of a single sovereign.

GRF.name: An Army for Bavaria
GRF.desc: Only with a formidable standing army will we have the military might necessary to match our ambitions. With careful focus, we can expand it without having a ruinous impact on our state's finances.

GRF.name: Bavaria Coin
GRF.desc: Our realm needs a new standardized coin to serve as our national unified currency. Establishing a state-owned mint in our capital would ensure our total control over this new coinage.

GRF.name: Bavarian Cultural Institutions
GRF.desc: With our homeland at the feet of the beautiful Alps, we are a destination for artists from all over Europe, who seek inspiration in our incredible landscape. If we were to construct and support the appropriate cultural institutions, we could refine our court into a center of refinement and elegance, one that could rival even the most prestigious powers of Europe.

GRF.name: Bavarian Dukedom
GRF.desc: We have been granted the rulership of Bavaria directly by the Emperor! By embellishing ourselves as the divinely-appointed protectors of Bavaria, we will ensure our legitimacy cannot be questioned.

GRF.name: Bavarian Hofkriegsrat
GRF.desc: Establishing a council with the sole duty of advising our ruler during times of conflict will help us develop a more capable fighting force.

GRF.name: Bavarian Imperial Knights
GRF.desc: Our nobles have distinguished themselves as formidable knights in the service of the Holy Roman Empire. We should nurture and scrupulously maintain these troops to ensure the survival of our ducal integrity.

GRF.name: Bavarian Purity Law
GRF.desc: The excellent quality of our beer has been celebrated for centuries, but for our brews to achieve legendary status, we must ensure their continued prestige and superiority for all time. Several rulers in the past have created regulations and standards for the brewing of this wonderful substance; and we could use this fact as a stamp of our breweries' quality.

GRF.name: Dreams of Unification
GRF.desc: We once were ruled by Bavaria, unified in culture and allied under a single banner. We must ensure that the new Bavarian state is equally mighty, a home worthy of its strong and proud people.

GRF.name: One Faith for Bavaria
GRF.desc: We must ensure our people remain united in their faith, and that they will not be divided by heretical thoughts.

GRF.name: Practical Diplomacy
GRF.desc: No matter if we are answering to an Imperial overlord or cozying up to a potential foreign ally, our diplomats must be prepared for everything. But only if they keep Bavarian interests first and foremost in their efforts will we be able to claim true success in our diplomatic maneuverings.

GRF.name: Skilled Brewers
GRF.desc: Our lands are rich in the crops and fresh water required to brew beer, and our people readily enjoy this abundance. Many small breweries could grow into successful businesses, with the right support.

GRF.name: Trading Hubs of Bavaria
GRF.desc: Our lands are frequently crossed by merchants wishing to trade Salt, Silver, and Livestock in the rich lands to our south. We would be foolish not to take advantage of their presence, and therefore will establish bustling trade hubs in our own lands to attract their business.

GRL.name: Charts of the North
GRL.desc: Generations of Greenlandic navigators have mapped every current, ice shelf, and hidden passage in the waters around our shores. This knowledge, compiled into charts of unmatched precision, makes Greenland an indispensable partner for any expedition venturing into the northern seas.

GRL.name: Ivory of the North
GRL.desc: The tusks of the walrus and the pelts of the arctic fox are among the finest goods that Greenland can offer the world. Our merchants brave the cold waters to bring these treasures to the markets of Europe, and in doing so keep our colony alive and prosperous.

GRL.name: Masters of the Hunt
GRL.desc: The Greenlandic waters teem with whales, seals, and fish. Our hunters have perfected the art of reading the ice and the tides, and their mastery of the sea keeps our people fed and our ships manned. There is no finer school for a sailor than the waters of the north.

GRL.name: Memory of Vinland
GRL.desc: Our forefathers sailed westward from these icy shores and discovered Vinland, a land of plenty far across the ocean. The memory of those voyages lives on in our sagas, and we know the route our ancestors took. Let us sail west once more and reclaim what was once ours.

GRL.name: Royal Charter
GRL.desc: The crowns of Europe have recognized Greenland as a land worth investing in. A formal charter organizes our trade under royal authority, attracting merchants from across Europe and ensuring that the wealth of the north flows through Greenlandic ports rather than around them.

GRL.name: Western Outpost
GRL.desc: The shores of Vinland are within our reach. We have the knowledge of the route, the ships to sail it, and the will to endure the crossing. Let us establish a permanent presence in the west and use Greenland as the launchpad for a new era of settlement.

HAB.name: Archduchy of Austria
HAB.desc: We have been granted the Privilegium Maius, which grants us an elevated position among the princes of the Holy Roman Empire. This shows our status and prestige even outside of Imperial lands, and elevates us to a higher position than that of a mere duke.

HAB.name: Geheime Kabinettskanzlei
HAB.desc: Established by the state to clandestinely intercept and examine all correspondence, this Black Chamber will provide us with intelligence about the postal activity within our country. Our agents' expertise in stealthily opening, copying, and resealing official documents will become renowned throughout the world.

HAB.name: Reichshofrat
HAB.desc: The Reichshofrat serves as the highest legal institution for Austria and Holy Roman Empire both, giving us stronger control over the legal processes of both our direct and imperial subjects.

HAB.name: Grenzer Infantry
HAB.desc: Recruited from our Carpathian and Balkan lands, these light troops are well equipped to guard the peace in our border regions. Their knowledge of their homeland will make them a formidable opponent for any invader.

HAB.name: Grenzhussar
HAB.desc: Stationed in border garrisons, these regiments of hussars will be able to patrol and secure the far reaches of our country, while keeping the strain on our treasury light.

HAB.name: 'Tu Felix Austria Nube'
HAB.desc: 'Let others wage war; you, happy Austria, marry! For what Mars gives to others, Venus gives to you — kingdoms.'

HAB.name: A House of Glory
HAB.desc: Our rise to power has made us the target of much envy, and the rival houses of the Holy Roman Empire vie for our position as the protectors of the south-eastern border. Despite these circumstances, we pride ourselves on executing diplomatic maneuvers unrivaled by any others.

HAB.name: Austrian Court
HAB.desc: Maintaining our diplomatic relations requires time and effort, and committing too many people to diplomatic missions could negatively affect our efficiency and damage our reputation. The Austrian Court's streamlined approach ensures we deploy the right envoys at the right times and still gather the information we need without overextending our diplomatic resources.

HAB.name: Austrian Diplomatic Expertise
HAB.desc: Given our location at the center of all Europe, we must adopt a highly flexible attitude towards external diplomacy. Alliances and rivals can shatter as easily as they are formed, and our diplomats must be trained to cover every possible position.

HAB.name: Edict of Restitution
HAB.desc: A bit of bookkeeping will help us to weather any religious strife that could befall our realm. This harmless edict will surely not spark any further conflict.

HAB.name: Enlightenment Through Education
HAB.desc: Our rulers must receive the best education possible to live up to the ideal of the enlightened monarch.

HAB.name: Geheimer Rat
HAB.desc: The Geheimer Rat is an elite advisory body composed of high-ranking nobles and officials, serving as the central institution for guiding our political, military, and administrative decisions.

HAB.name: Grenzer Infantry
HAB.desc: Recruited from our Carpathian and Balkan lands, these light troops are well equipped to guard the peace in our border regions. Their knowledge of their homeland will make them a formidable opponent for any invader.

HAB.name: Grenzhussar
HAB.desc: Stationed in border garrisons, these regiments of hussars will be able to patrol and secure the far reaches of our country, while keeping the strain on our treasury light.

HAB.name: Hofkriegsrat
HAB.desc: Our war council can only function with a proper bureaucratic structure. Only when we know every detail about our troops and logistics can we defend our realm from hostile intruders.

HAB.name: Imperial Artillery
HAB.desc: The rapidly changing nature of warfare urges us to modernize our troops and tactics. In order to stay ahead of our foes, we shall make our artillery the pride of the Imperial army.

HAB.name: Land of Mountains and Rivers
HAB.desc: Our people are highly adapted to traverse the obstacles of our country, from the high peaks and passes of our mountains to the wide rivers of our valleys.

HAB.name: Landsknecht Tactics
HAB.desc: Only well-rounded tactics of artillery shock, cavalry charges, and unyielding infantry recruited from the can lead us to victory.

HAB.name: Legacy of Rudolf I
