They excel on close combat where the karambit's curved blade is extremely efficient at slashing, hooking, and gutting opponents. The adoption and proliferation of new formations and combat maneuvers has turned these warriors into a fabled armed force, feared throughout the archipelago.

MAJ.name: Madurese Ghali
MAJ.desc: The people that populate the Madura Strait have come to serve in our navy. Their naval prowess and great shipbuilding skills have given rise to a new kind of vessel, the Madurese Ghali. A large ship, it is used for offensive and voyager-adjacent tasks, as it will soon comprise the backbone of our fleet.

MAJ.name: Maritime Silk Road
MAJ.desc: Our geographical position, complemented by our growing influence, has led to us presiding over the extensive and profitable trade network that carries Silk and from East to West.

MAJ.name: Preservation of Javanese History
MAJ.desc: The history of the Javanese people is an integral part of our cultural identity. To protect this identity, we must preserve the traditions upon which we built our great country.

MAJ.name: Restore Candi Shrines
MAJ.desc: Scattered throughout Nusantara are a series of temples known as candi. We should restore these temples wherever we find them to renew our people's faith.

MAJ.name: Sumpah Palapa
MAJ.desc: The head of our military directly answers to our ruler, and holds enough influence and power to shape the future of our realm. To ensure they understand what an important role they have been given, they are required to swear a special oath, one that underlines our dreams of conquest and bolsters our spirits.

MAJ.name: The Bajang Ratu Gate
MAJ.desc: A ceremonious gate of magnificent proportions, the Bajang Ratu follows the architectural design of a candi bentar, or split gateway. Using high quality red brick, the gateway is to be one of the tallest constructs across the Majapahit domain. Its usage is vital, as the structure is used for grand ceremonies of religious and political nature.

MAJ.name: The Magic Arrow
MAJ.desc: One of the most prominent muzzle-loaded cannons of our era is the Cetbang. Armed with a cylindrical short barrel, it delivers a devastating blow with tremendous power. Such is its popularity, that it finds use in many aspects of our conduct of warfare, from protecting our ports to being the main armament of our warships and armies.

MAL.name: Manden Kurufa
MAL.desc: The Manden Kurufa, also known as the Manden Federation, is the government of the. Originally started as the 'Twelve Doors' which were the personal possessions of the Mansa, this network of alliances and conquered lands has become the core government of the state.

MAL.name: Office of the Farima-Soura
MAL.desc: Charged with guarding the northern border, the Farima-Soura monitors traffic across the Saharan border, and oversees the safety and swift passage of all mercantile traffic in and out of our borders.

MAL.name: Office of the Sankar-Zouma
MAL.desc: The Sankar-Zouma is a prestigious office granted to the Nobility by the highest authority in the land. Its role, much like the Farima-Soura, revolves around exercising authority along all trade routes across the southern border.

MAL.name: Gbara
MAL.desc: The Gbara is the deliberative assembly of Mali and is defined in the constitution, the Kouroukan Fouga. The Nobility represent the many clans in our state, and check the power of the ruling ruler.

MAL.name: Ton-ta-jon-ta-ni-woro
MAL.desc: In the early days of our empire, our army was made up of sixteen clans whose leaders promised to protect the great Mansa and the State. Translated as 'the Sixteen Slaves that carry the Bow', the Ton-ta-jon-ta-ni-woro are the high Nobility of the country and serve as commanders of the cavalry.

MAL.name: Farari Cavalry
MAL.desc: The Farari are the elite corps of the Malian military. Appointed from privileged and common people alike, the Farari are known for their bravery and military experience.

MAL.name: Farari Infantry
MAL.desc: The Farari are the elite corps of the Malian military. Appointed from privileged and common people alike, the Farari are known for their bravery and military experience.

MAL.name: Jonow Auxiliary
MAL.desc: The Jonow are slaves who accompany the Kèlè-Koun and their soldiers as carriers of their military equipment.

MAL.name: Mandekalu Horsemen
MAL.desc:
The Mandekalu Horsemen are the additional support of the Malian military. These Horon - the free people of Mali - received their mount and equipment from the Ton-tigi and the Mansa. Charging into the battle with lances and long swords, the Mandekalu Horsemen projected the power of the Mansa even in the furthest corners of the empire.

Can gain Experience in order to be promoted to Farari Infantry and Farari Cavalry after the advance Farari Corps has been researched. Experience is shared by all Mandekalu units. Won battles grant +15, lost battles grant +5 Experience per participating Mandekalu unit.

MAL.name: Mandekalu Infantry
MAL.desc:
The Mandekalu Infantry are the backbone of the Malian military, and are made of the Horon - the free people of Mali. Equipped with javelins, bows and poisoned arrows, they are a formidable force to be reckoned with.

Can gain Experience in order to be promoted to Farari Infantry and Farari Cavalry after the advance Farari Corps has been researched. Experience is shared by all Mandekalu units. Won battles grant +15, lost battles grant +5 Experience per participating Mandekalu unit.

MAL.name: Sofa Infantrymen
MAL.desc: Slaves who were trained in the arts of war so they can serve the state as soldiers. Although they receive their weapons from the Horon (the free men of Mali), it is them who risk their lives in combat.

MAL.name: Accounts of the Atlantic Voyage
MAL.desc: According to the legendary Mansa Mūsā, his predecessor started a journey across the Atlantic Ocean in hopes of discovering the furthest limits of the ocean. While some among the ruling class consider this endeavor a shameful abdication of duty, others see this as inspiration to explore corners of the world previously unknown to man.

MAL.name: Epic of Sundiata
MAL.desc: The Epic of Sundiata tells of the legendary campaign of Sundiata Keita, the founder of the Malian Empire and hero of our people. His story has passed from generation to generation, and has always been a great source of inspiration to our people.

MAL.name: Farari Corps
MAL.desc: The Farari Corps are the elite of the Malian military. Commanders in their own right, they are highly respected for their experience and bravery.

MAL.name: Gold of Bure
MAL.desc: The twin gold fields at Bambuk and Bure are renowned as the largest gold deposits anyone has ever heard of, and they belong to us! Bure's gold mines in particular produced fantastic wealth that famously destabilized the entire Egyptian economy through inflation when Mansa Mūsā visited there. Our economy, though, is used to a constant influx of gold, and is more difficult to inflate.

MAL.name: Kouroukan Fouga
MAL.desc: The Kouroukan Fouga is the basic constitution of Mali. It covers every aspect of living, from simple family life in the villages all the way to the sovereignty of the Mansa.

MAL.name: Mandekalu Levies
MAL.desc: The Mandekalu Levies are the backbone of the Malian military. Freemen of the Empire are called to arms in times of war, and it is a great honor for them to participate in these battles with their own weapons.

MAL.name: Mandinka Warrior Spirit
MAL.desc: Whether pagan or Muslim, Mandinka men have been the greatest fighters the Sahel has ever seen. The courage of our troops is admirable, as is their pride. When the Mansa raises an army, not only is it the largest in all the Sahel, it is the best!

MAL.name: Markets for Salt
MAL.desc: In our kingdom, Salt is worth its cost in gold. But south of us, in the great forests of the Ashanti and the Yoruba, salt is worth considerably more than gold. Luckily for us, we have our own supply of Salt, and enough gold to obtain as much as we could ever want. Perhaps we could find yet more markets of people for whom Salt is more valuable than gold?

MAL.name: Reclamation of Land
MAL.desc: The Sahara is not static. It can wax and wane depending on rainfall, and the habitable belt known as the Sahel, where we reside, can grow or shrink accordingly. A major drought could render much of our kingdom useless desert, an addition to the Sahara where no one reigns but death. However, in good years, we might reclaim some of the marginal lands from the Sahara and make it productive again.

MAL.name: Sofa Levies
MAL.desc: Originally, all soldiers in the Kèlè-Bolo levies are horon, or 'freemen', but the latest developments in Mali have forced the inclusion of jonow, 'slaves', to serve in the army as fighters instead of weapon-bearers. These slave warriors would thereafter be known as 'Sofa', protecting fortifications as part of garrison forces.

MAL.name: The Kèlè-Koun
MAL.desc: The Kèlè-Koun, or 'war-head', are the commanders of infantry fighting for Empire, called the Kèlè-Bolo, or 'war-arm'. Unlike the Ton-Tigi, the feudal lords of Mali, the Kèlè-Koun are not necessarily part of the Nobility. The Kèlè-Koun have jonow, 'slaves', serving as carriers of the weapons and equipment until their inclusion in the Sofa battalions.

MAL.name: West African Slave Trade
MAL.desc: Even before our Empire existed, the great Wagadou, the Ghana Empire that preceded us, sold Slaves across the desert to the Arabs. We have followed suit all these years, supplying the Arab world with a vast number of Slaves. Now the Europeans clamor for even more Slaves to work their holdings in the so-called New World. We have had little report, but the amount of Slaves they demand is truly stunning, and they keep coming back, sometimes even raiding our shores and abducting our subjects. The time has come to impose order on this trade and restrict the Europeans to select commercial ports where they will purchase, not steal, Slaves.

MAM.name: Mamlūk Government
MAM.desc: The Sultanate's rule over the vastness of Egypt depends greatly on maintaining a powerful standing army. Its upper class consists of factions of these powerful slave soldiers, who often ascend to the throne themselves, and can be the deciding factor between a long and short reign.

MAM.name: Refined Furūsiyya
MAM.desc: Through centuries of martial tradition, we have refined Furūsiyya, the Muslim code of chivalry and military practice, blending horsemanship, archery, and warfare tactics with intellectual and ethical training.

MAM.name: Early Mamālīk
MAM.desc: Well-trained elite troops, these men have been honed to represent the best our people have to offer. Raised as slaves purchased from foreign masters, they are disciplined and taught our religious and military doctrines as they are expected to form the core of our standing army. Oftentimes, they come equipped with heavy armor and sturdy spears. Their unique helmets and presence in the battlefield is a terrifying sight for our foes.

MAM.name: Mamālīk Horsemen
MAM.desc: The mounted arm of the Mamlūk military, these elite slave-soldier cavalry form the iconic shock force of our armies. Trained from youth in horsemanship, archery, and the lance, they complement the foot-based Early Mamālīk regiments and project the power of the sultanate across the battlefield.

MAM.name: Reformed Mamālīk
MAM.desc: The later Mamlūk troops are categorized by a renewed attention to detail and discipline. A series of military reforms are set in place, to restore the old standards and retrain our standing armies.

MAM.name: Reformed Mamālīk Horsemen
MAM.desc: Like their foot brethren, the mounted Mamālīk undergo renewed training and discipline reforms. The mounted core of our standing army remains the elite shock cavalry of the sultanate.

MAM.name: Ḥalqah
MAM.desc: Auxiliary units that often accompanied their Mamlūk counterparts, these light and quick troops will offer great support to their parent forces on the battlefield.

MAM.name: Early Mamālīk
MAM.desc: Well-trained elite troops, these men have been honed to represent the best our people have to offer. Raised as slaves purchased from foreign masters, they are disciplined and taught our religious and military doctrines as they are expected to form the core of our standing army. Oftentimes, they come equipped with heavy armor and sturdy spears. Their unique helmets and presence in the battlefield is a terrifying sight for our foes.

MAM.name: Foreign Gunpowder
MAM.desc: The great empires of Europe and the East have made groundbreaking advances in the use of gunpowder and its military applications. To study their ways and make the according improvements to our own armaments would greatly strengthen our own military.

MAM.name: Indian Networks
MAM.desc: Our merchants deal in goods from the markets of Alexandria, to the shores of Aden, and as far away as India itself. These extensive networks of contacts, business, and capital have positioned us at the forefront of maritime commerce.

MAM.name: Kārimī Merchants
MAM.desc: Formidable traders that primarily deal in spices, these mercantile giants have profited greatly from the flow of exotic goods that trail their origin as far as the shores of India and beyond.

MAM.name: Kāshif
MAM.desc: Our Sultanate is enormous, and therefore we must make wise, careful choices about its administration. To employ particularly learned individuals as local governors is a brilliant move, one that should eventually tip the geopolitical scales in our favor.

MAM.name: Mamluk Barīd
MAM.desc: Under Baybars, our barīd reached a sophistication unmatched in the Islamic world: relay stations with fresh mounts at fixed stages, carrier pigeons for the most urgent dispatches, and intelligence agents posted along every route. Word of a frontier raid can reach the capital in a matter of days, and our orders return just as swiftly.
mods: Reduces Barīd bureaucracy negative effect by 50%

MAM.name: Masters of the Nile
MAM.desc: The heart-vein of our Sultanate is the river Nile. Traversing our nation, its touch creates our most fertile lands, and its life-bringing waters of the river channel prosperity and ample wealth throughout our domain.

MAM.name: Port Customs
MAM.desc: Designating our ports as official merchant zones for incoming cargo is a move that will certainly increase the mercantile significance of our territory, albeit at the expense of our neighbors and foes alike.

MAM.name: Red Sea Trade
MAM.desc: The spice trade flowing through the Red Sea is a key source of our wealth, and we must seize full control of it. By threatening to burn down any Red Sea ports outside our authority that accept spice traders, we can capture the lion's share of this lucrative commerce. We may not win many friendships with our aggression, but we shall have gold enough to comfort us.

MAM.name: Reformed Mamālīk
MAM.desc: The later Mamlūk troops are categorized by a renewed attention to detail and discipline. A series of military reforms are set in place, to restore the old standards and retrain our standing armies.

MAM.name: Secure Mediterranean Ports
MAM.desc: Our ports across the Mediterranean Sea are some of the most affluent in the entire region. Merchants from every corner of the known world travel to Alexandria and Cairo to deal in spices, Silk, and precious stones. The creation of a merchant navy to facilitate and protect our maritime avenues would therefore be a wise idea.

MAM.name: The Royal Mamluks
MAM.desc: The Royal Mamluks are the elite core of the Mamluk army, serving as the Sultan's personal guard. Handpicked and rigorously trained, they are renowned for their loyalty, exceptional combat skills, and unwavering dedication.

MAM.name: Ḥalqah
MAM.desc: Auxiliary units that often accompanied their Mamlūk counterparts, these light and quick troops will offer great support to their parent forces on the battlefield.

MAN.name: Gonzaga Patronage of the Arts
MAN.desc: Our court has become one of the great magnets of artistic talent in the peninsula: painters, sculptors, and architects arrive already knowing that Mantua rewards ambition and that the work produced here will reach the eyes of every prince who sends an envoy to our door. We formalize this tradition of patronage into a deliberate policy, maintaining stipends and workshops that keep multiple artists resident at once and ensuring that the work they produce reflects the standing we intend to project. This culture of Mecenatismo reduces the cost of maintaining artists and draws talent of the highest quality to settle permanently among us rather than passing through for a single commission.

MAN.name: Monteverdi's L'Orfeo
MAN.desc: When Claudio Monteverdi staged L'Orfeo in our Palazzo Ducale for the Accademia degli Invaghiti, he gave the world its first fully realized opera: a work in which voices, instruments, and drama were fused into a form that audiences immediately recognized as unlike anything they had heard before. Mantua was the city where this transformation happened, and its court was the institution that made it possible, providing Monteverdi with singers, players, and the sustained patronage without which neither the rehearsals nor the score could have materialized. This primacy in the birth of opera makes our court the acknowledged origin of Europe's most powerful new art form, and the artists trained in its shadow carry our reputation to every stage they subsequently inhabit.

MAN.name: Palazzo Te
MAN.desc: Federico II Gonzaga commissioned Giulio Romano to build a pleasure palace on an island at the edge of the city, and what emerged was the Palazzo Te, one of the most inventive buildings of the Renaissance, a work of architecture that quotes the classical tradition with such knowing wit that scholars have argued over its ironies ever since. The frescoed rooms, from the giants collapsing in painted ruin to the horses of Federico's stables rendered with life-size confidence, are the most daring decorative program in northern Italy. The extraordinary achievement deepens our cultural tradition and lends the works produced under our patronage a singular character, sought out by collectors and courts above the more conventional output of our rivals.

MAN.name: Po Valley Agriculture
MAN.desc: The lowland plain that surrounds Mantua on three sides is among the most fertile land in Italy, and we have made systematic investment in its management the foundation of our domestic economy, draining marshes, expanding irrigation channels, and regulating the reclamation of new land at the margins of the lakes that define our geography. The result is an agricultural capacity that grows reliably each generation, supplying our city with food surpluses that sustain a population larger than our politics alone would justify. This patient cultivation of the Pianüra Padâna (Pianura Padana in standard Italian: the Po Plain) ensures that our subjects eat well in difficult years and that our treasury collects the taxes of a prosperous countryside.

MAN.name: The House of Gonzaga
MAN.desc: For well over a century the Casa Gonzaga has ruled Mantua not as conquerors but as lords whose claim rests on a compact of mutual benefit with their subjects, a legitimacy that no merely military power can purchase and that we have maintained by never treating the city as a resource to be extracted. We sustain this standing through three interlocking channels: the church patronage that binds our subjects through shared devotion, the formal dynastic titles that give our rule a legal foundation that rivals cannot challenge, and our deliberate respect for the commune traditions that Mantua's citizens still recognize as their inherited right. Resting on faith, dynasty, and civic compact, our state holds a legitimacy that each subject feels in daily life, and our rule is steadier than any arrangement built on force alone.

MAN.name: The Studium Mantovano
MAN.desc: We establish a formal studium in Mantua, drawing teachers of law, philosophy, and the arts from the great universities of the region and providing the sons of our burghers and minor nobility with an education that was previously available only to those wealthy enough to travel to Bologna or Padua. The institution links Mantua to the network of European learning that flows through the great schools, bringing the latest ideas in jurisprudence, theology, and natural philosophy into our city rather than letting them arrive years late through correspondence. This Studium Mantovano raises the literacy of our governing class and ensures that new ideas take root among us as quickly as they spread anywhere in Italy.

MEI.name: A Mining Heritage
MEI.desc: For centuries, mining has shaped our landscape, economy, and culture. Significant Silver discoveries in the region have attracted miners and traders from diverse regions, fostering the Ore Mountains' growth and expanding our realm's significance and development.

MEI.name: A Resilient Soul
MEI.desc: Our people are truly resilient, embodying unwavering determination in the face of challenges. They weather adversity with unwavering spirit, finding strength in unity and a steadfast commitment to their shared values. Their indomitable resilience propels us forward, enabling us to overcome any obstacle that comes our way. We will always emerge stronger and more determined than ever before.

MEI.name: A Tolerant Society
MEI.desc: Religious infighting and intolerance plagues other lands, but we stand firm against allowing such strife to fester in our realm. Regardless of the diverse faiths our subjects hold, this nation shall be built on the strong pillars of tolerance and brotherhood, fostering a harmonious coexistence among all communities. United by a common vision, we will be forging a nation where respect and understanding flourish, paving the way for a prosperous future.

MEI.name: Bonded by Loyalty
MEI.desc: Our valiant armies never waver! They demonstrate exceptional morale and loyalty, standing firm whether defending our realm or supporting allies. With indomitable spirits, they will press forward even in desperate circumstances, refusing defeat until physically unable to continue.

MEI.name: Fürstenschule
MEI.desc: As the Reformation takes hold and the state assumes control over religious administration, a new responsibility arises for the emerging state: education, which was previously the duty of the Church. We will found princely schools at Pforta, Grimma, and Meissen using former monastic properties. Thus, the state will take on a significant role in shaping the educational landscape, fostering knowledge and intellectual growth for the future leaders of Saxony.

MEI.name: Meissner Porcelain
MEI.desc: Saxony is the first country in Europe to produce Porcelain, which will bring wealth and prestige to the Wettin court.

MEI.name: Meißner Groschen
MEI.desc: The Meißner groschen will serve as our national currency. This coin is based on the Prague groschen, which we will replace. This new large groschen will mark the beginning of a new era in the history of our coinage and will let us better control its influxes.

MEI.name: Rétablissement
MEI.desc:
After tumultuous wars, a new era dawns upon Saxony — the remarkable Saxon Rétablissement. Amidst the ruins of our past, our nation will rise like a phoenix, rebuilding its shattered economy and charting a path toward prosperity. Driven by a blend of visionary state reforms and disciplined spending, our nation will emerge as a commercial hub.

With unparalleled administrative prowess and a strategic focus on economic growth, this resolute transformation will mark a pivotal moment in history, shaping the destiny of Saxony well into the future.

MEI.name: Saxon Baroque
MEI.desc: Dresden and Leipzig, among other locales, have gained international recognition for being centers of Saxon Baroque culture. Magnificent architecture, like the Dresdner Hof, epitomize the grandeur of Saxony, while Johann Sebastian Bach's work has transformed Leipzig into a city of music and thriving highbrow culture. The region boasts unique expressions of culture, including handicrafts from the Ore Mountains and culinary traditions like the Dresdner Christstollen.

MEI.name: Saxon Industrialization
MEI.desc: Saxony's successful early industrialization is evident, with a highly developed industrial sector compared to other regions. The manufactory system, producing mainly for export, has flourished and will make Saxony a leading state in Germany's industrialization process. The emergence of smaller commercial landscapes and trade will be instrumental in promoting the region's economic growth and connections to other markets in Europe.

MEI.name: The Meißen Lion
MEI.desc: The Meißen Lion, also known as the Markmeißnische Löwe, holds a special place in heraldry. Representing the Wettin dynasty's symbol of power, an armored black lion with a red tongue gazes to the left on a golden field. Its image appears in various forms, including on painted tombstones, ensigns, helmets, coins, and seals, symbolizing the affiliation of the city of Meissen to the Mark Meißen and adorning the coats of arms of numerous towns and communities. Some link it to the recolored Thuringian lion.

MEI.name: The Saxon Court
MEI.desc: The Saxon Court is a pillar of Electoral Saxony's government, alongside civil and military administration. Court regulations define the responsibilities and daily routines of officials, while the court itself is composed of both nobles and peasants serving the ruling family in governance and administration. Traditionally, each adult member of the ruling family maintained their own household court, but we will now create a single, permanent court in our capital, attracting the finest minds in the realm.

MFA.name: Casale Monferrato
MFA.desc: We have made Casale Monferrato the heart of our state, a city that grows in commerce and craft under the shelter of our rule. The merchants and guilds of the city bring life to its streets and revenues to our treasury, and its position on the roads between great powers makes it a natural gathering place for trade. This city is our richest possession and the proof of what sound governance can build.

MFA.name: The Casale Citadel
MFA.desc: We have transformed Casale Monferrato into a fortress city whose walls and bastions are among the most formidable in the peninsula. The citadel's deep ditches and angled walls are designed to exhaust any siege and bleed any attacker who thinks to take it quickly. This fortification has made our seat of power into one of the great military prizes of the age, too costly to assault and too important to ignore.

MFA.name: The Court Culture
MFA.desc: Our court has become a gathering place for artists, scholars, and musicians drawn by the patronage and refined taste we offer. We prize the Arts of the Court as instruments of prestige, and the works produced under our roof reflect well on our name wherever they travel. This investment in culture returns in reputation what it costs in coin.

MFA.name: The Marquisate's Resilience
MFA.desc: We have survived between greater powers through the arts of flexibility and careful friendship, never placing our trust entirely in any single alliance. By maintaining a reputation for reasonableness and good faith, we have made ourselves useful to those who might otherwise simply absorb us. This Diplomatic Resilience is our oldest strategy and our most reliable one.

MFA.name: The Monferrato Agricoltura
MFA.desc: The rolling hills and fertile valleys of our marquisate yield harvests that sustain our people and support a growing population of farmers and rural craftsmen. Through careful management and investment in our lands, we have expanded the reach of our agriculture into slopes and terraces that once lay idle. This Agricultural Transformation brings new settlers to our countryside and new revenues to our state.

MFA.name: The Paleologue Dynasty
MFA.desc: The ancient blood of the Paleologue gives our marquisate a dignity and legitimacy that commands respect from the greatest courts of Europe. This lineage connects us to a world of ceremony and diplomacy that most smaller states can only admire from afar. We carry this heritage as a shield as much as an ornament, using it to open doors that our armies alone could never unlock.

MLK.name: Highland Fortresses
MLK.desc: Our fortresses are a brilliant emblem of our resilience and fortitude, built to endure not only the difficult local climate, but also any foreign invader foolish enough to mount an attack into our unforgiving territory.

MLL.name: Pearl of the Mediterranean
MLL.desc: Following careful maneuvering of past rulers, the Balearics have become one of the most important regions of trade throughout the Mediterranean Sea, with many merchants choosing the islands as a core stop.
