MLL.name: Universitat de Mallorca
MLL.desc: The Universitat de la Ciutat i Regne de Mallorca is the governing body of our island realm, administered by elected Jurats who oversee taxation, public works, and the interests of the burgher and merchant communities. Its long tradition of municipal self-governance has made the mercantile class the dominant force in Mallorcan affairs, ensuring that trade policy and port administration reflect the needs of those who profit from the sea. The Universitat's competent civic administration is the backbone of Mallorcan prosperity.

MLL.name: Leges Palatinae
MLL.desc: Leges Palatinae shall strengthen the power of our court along with legitimizing our right as a independent state.

MLL.name: Carta de Franquesa
MLL.desc: The Carta de Franquesa granted by King Jaume I in 1230, in the very year following the conquest of Mayūrqa, establishes the bedrock of Mallorcan liberty: the freedom of the new settlers from servile dues, the right of the universitat to elect its own jurats, and the exemption of our merchants from the harshest royal levies. Each of the foranes, the rural communities scattered across the island, receives these privileges alongside Palma's burghers, binding the entire repopulation under a single charter rather than a feudal patchwork. Under the founding charter every Mallorcan household has a direct stake in defending royal authority, and our envoys speak abroad with less strain of a kingdom under law.

MLL.name: Corsaris Mallorquins
MLL.desc: Royal patents de cors authorize our captains to arm fast galleys and brigantines at private expense for raids against Barbary and Genoese shipping, as well as any other commerce hostile to the Crown. The corsair fraternity at Palma maintains its own rolls of veteran helmsmen, gunners, and boatswains that the royal navy draws upon in time of war, blurring the line between privateer and naval reservist into a single pool of seafaring manpower. This deep reservoir of trained crews fills our fleets faster than any state-recruited navy can and lets our squadrons reach distant station before any peer Mediterranean force has cleared harbor.

MLL.name: Escola Cartogràfica Mallorquina
MLL.desc: Our Escola Cartogràfica Mallorquina gathers Jewish and Christian map makers around the Cresques family of Palma (Abraham and his son Jafudà) who produces dozens of working portolan charts for the courts of Aragon, France, and Castile. Their workshops standardize the conventions of compass roses, rhumb lines, and named ports that every Mediterranean and Atlantic captain will rely on for two centuries. This concentration of cartographic learning raises the prestige of our Crown across Christendom and seeds a printing tradition in our presses that nourishes scholarship well beyond cartography alone.

MLL.name: Escola Mallorquina
MLL.desc: The literary flowering of our islands through the Escola Mallorquina restores Mallorcan letters to the European mainstream after generations in which our tongue survived only in private devotion and folk song. We will sponsor the Pollença and Palma poetic circles whose clear, classicizing Catalan draws on both the Greco-Latin canon and the rugged landscape of the Serra de Tramuntana, carrying their journals and verses along every shipping route between the islands and the mainland. This literary revival deepens the islanders' identification with their own language and softens the assimilation of mainland migrants, who absorb the local idiom through the school's widely read pages.

MLL.name: Indústria Lapidària
MLL.desc: The pale marès limestone of Mallorca and the dark slate of Menorca feed an organized indústria lapidària that supplies Iberian construction sites from Palma's cathedrals and Catalan coastal forts to American colonial churches. Our quarrymen in Santanyí and Felanitx work seasonally under contract to royal arsenals, paying tribute in cut blocks rather than coin and earning a reputation for the precision of their dressed ashlar. This organized stonecutting industry makes every Mallorcan workshop more productive and speeds every royal building project across our realm.

MLL.name: Torres Costaneres
MLL.desc: A network of torres costaneres, squat circular watchtowers of marès stone, rings Mallorca, Menorca, Ibiza, and Formentera. The towers are within sight of one another, manned by parish levies who light signal fires the instant a Barbary sail appears on the horizon. Each tower is paired with a fortified parish church and a refuge cistern, so that no coastal community is more than an hour from defensible walls and stored water. This island-wide defensive lattice raises the cost of any amphibious assault on our shores and lets a smaller garrison defend a longer perimeter than the establishment of any peer realm could match.

MLL.name: A Hub of Mediterranean Sea Trade
MLL.desc: While many of the old trade routes were casualties of past and conflicts, the newfound independence of the creates an opportunity for these once-profitable trade routes to be restored. Furthermore, the prime location of the Balearics offers us a chance to be a leading contender in Mediterranean Sea trade.

MLL.name: Exchange of Montpellier
MLL.desc: Bequeathed to Mll Jacme Ii Mallorca in the will of Ara Jacme I Arago, Montpellier has ever since been a crucial mainland holding for the. However, with the growing hostilities between Aragon and Mallorca, Montpellier may provide strong leverage with the.

MLO.name: Council of Justice
MLO.desc: Originally an instrument for resolving local disputes between peasants, the Council of Justice has developed into the land's most prominent court, handling cases and operating as a shield for our people.

MLO.name: Secret Council
MLO.desc: The Secret Council is a body of nobly-born individuals. Its jurisdiction encompasses our entire domain, and often clashes against the ruler's agenda. The majority of critical decisions made by or on behalf of the ruler frequently fall under the Secret Council's review.

MLO.name: Milanese Cloth Guilds
MLO.desc: Our valuable cloth industry rests upon the shoulders of the finest craftsmen in all of Italy. By entrusting their regulations and production lines to our Burghers, we will attain record profits and productivity at the minor cost of granting our merchant guilds some influence.

MLO.name: Visconti City States
MLO.desc: The under the Visconti family is marked by a fractured and decentralized state. Different prominent members of the Visconti house, including Azzone, Gian Galeazzo, and Bernabò, vie for supremacy through various tactics such as alliances, betrayals, and military campaigns. This constant power struggle constantly weakens the central authority of the and contribute to a state of instability and fragmentation in the region.

MLO.name: Beccaria's Treatise
MLO.desc: Our city produced Cesare Beccaria, whose treatise on crimes and punishments has become the most-read legal text in Europe, arguing that laws should deter crime through certainty rather than cruelty. By reforming our criminal code along these lines (replacing torture and arbitrary sentencing with proportional penalties and open courts) we create a legal system that the urban population sees as fair rather than predatory. This makes our cities easier to govern and more appealing to merchants and investors who know their disputes will be resolved by law rather than by bribes.

MLO.name: Il Biscione
MLO.desc: The coiled serpent of the Visconti has become the most recognized symbol of power in Northern Italy, stamped on our coins, our seals, and the gates of every city that answers to us. By making the Biscione the official mark of the ducal state, we tie the region's loyalty to our dynasty rather than to any one noble faction. Such visual authority makes it far harder for rivals to question our rule, and the serpent on our ambassadors' credentials opens doors that stay shut to other Italian lords.

MLO.name: Teatro alla Scala
MLO.desc: We have raised a theater on the site of the old church of Santa Maria alla Scala, large enough to seat two thousand and fitted with stage machinery that no other house in Europe can match. The first night drew every ambassador, merchant prince, and noble family who could claim a connection to Milan, and within a season premieres here were being discussed from London to Saint Petersburg. This stage makes our court the cultural arbiter of the continent, and the artists who succeed at La Scala carry our city's name everywhere they travel.

MLO.name: The Borromean Reform
MLO.desc: Carlo Borromeo's administration of Milan became the most closely studied model of institutional reform of the age: rigorous reorganization of local hierarchies, standardized training for officials, and regular inspection visits that reached every village in our territory. We adopt his model wholesale, using every institution at our disposal to extend education and discipline throughout our realm. This reform builds a population that is both more literate and more tightly bound to the institutions of the realm, making civic order far easier to maintain.

MLO.name: The Fabbrica del Duomo
MLO.desc: The Veneranda Fabbrica del Duomo has maintained a permanent workforce of stonecutters, engineers, and master builders in continuous employ for generations, treating the Cathedral not as a project with an end but as an institution that trains craftsmen and refines technique for as long as the work demands. We have extended its remit and its funding, ensuring that the knowledge it preserves flows outward to every construction site in our territory. This institution turns Milan into a school of practical building, and the craftsmen it trains are sought across the whole of northern Italy.

MLO.name: The Milanese Armorers
MLO.desc: A breastplate made in our workshops commands a price that craftsmen in Cologne or Toledo cannot match, and our armories supply courts and captains from Portugal to Poland. We formalize the armorers' guilds under ducal oversight, setting standards that protect our reputation and keep the technical knowledge, and the profit, within our walls. This monopoly on premium military equipment brings us steady revenue and keeps our own troops better equipped than any enemy who has to import their plate from elsewhere.

MLO.name: Integrate Lombard Claims
MLO.desc: Our quest to unite the former lands of the Lombard Kingdom is but a noble and legitimate one.

MOR.name: Amīr al-Muslimīn
MOR.desc: The title Amīr al-Muslimīn — Commander of the Muslims — was carried by the Almoravid sultans who crossed the Sahara to rescue al-'Andalus from Christian encroachment and by our Marinid forebears who returned across the Strait again and again in the same cause. Winning the Strait from the fleets of Castile and Aragon has placed us in that lineage: protectors of the last western frontier of Islam, recognized in the khuṭba of every mosque from Fez to the Guadalquivir. This title binds the Andalusi communities to our throne, fills our banners with willing warriors of the faith, and carries our name to every Muslim court that watches the Iberian peninsula.
mods: Damage Done versus Heathens in Battle

MOR.name: Marinid Zenata Confederation
MOR.desc: The Banū Marīn rode out of Figuig as Zenati horse-lords and took Fez from the failing Almohad dynasty by tribal cohesion and a banner of Mālikī orthodoxy. Our Marinid dynasty still stands on both pillars: the Zenati clans ride when our summons them, the fuqahā' bless rule, and the jihād in al-'Andalus answers to each. A Marinid commands because tribesmen follow and scholars sanction, and must keep proving both with the sword.

MOR.name: Sharifian Sultanate
MOR.desc: The Sharifian sultans have transformed Morocco from a confederation beholden to its tribal levies into a centralized monarchy whose authority flows from both genealogical sanctity and military discipline. The jīš service-tribes settle on crown land, Andalusi gunners drill on Fez's artillery range, and the great maḵzan apparatus moves tax rolls and judicial writs across the realm with a regularity the Marinids never achieved. This is the state-form that turns our baraka — the sacred charisma of descent from the Prophet — from a legitimacy claim into a governing system: a sultanate that is simultaneously a dynasty, a bureaucracy, and a religious court.

MOR.name: Shurfā' Status
MOR.desc: Our sultans claim descent from the Prophet Muhammad through the Idrisid line of the eighth century, and the Saadi and Alaouite dynasties have institutionalized this lineage as the central legitimacy of the Moroccan throne. The shurfā' — accredited descendants of the Prophet — hold a recognized rank above all other social classes, with their own marriage registers, tax exemptions, and judicial standing supervised by the royal naqīb. This sacralization of the dynasty gives the Moroccan sultan a religious authority that no other Maghrebi ruler can claim and that no rebel can credibly challenge.

MOR.name: 'Abīd al-Buḵārī
MOR.desc: The 'abīd are an enslaved soldiery conscripted by the sultan and registered under the name of al-Buḵārī as a legal fiction that binds them to the crown rather than to any individual master. We have organized this corps into a standing professional force that answers directly to the throne, reducing our reliance on the fractious tribal confederations for military manpower. This centralization of arms in royal hands marks a decisive step toward a sovereign army independent of the great clan-levies.

MOR.name: Guich Tribes
MOR.desc: With the Maḵzan built and its authority pressed outward, the exchange of land for service can be made a standing institution rather than a bargain renewed each season. The jīš tribes — of usually Arab origin, farming in arḍ al-jayš plots handled to each warrior and held free of tax for as long as they ride — are soldiers of the crown first and cultivators second. A corps that feeds itself from its own allotments costs the treasury a fraction of what wages would, and answers to no lineage but ours. Withdraw the centralizing hand and the arrangement lapses: these tribes serve a Maḵzan that reaches them.

MOR.name: Jaysh Armies
MOR.desc: Organized by the local administration to perform garrison and auxiliary duties, these fighters were hired to suppress local revolts and ensure the constant flow of reinforcements into our army, while also suppressing rebellions in their home territories.

MOR.name: Marabout Patronage
MOR.desc: The marabouts are holy men of recognized spiritual descent whose shrines dot the Moroccan landscape and whose intercession the common people seek for healing, arbitration, and protection against misfortune. By patronizing these figures and their attached zāwiya, we bind a decentralized network of sacred authority to the Maḵzan, making the sultan the recognized protector of popular Moroccan Islam. This relationship provides us access to religious intermediaries capable of pacifying communities that neither governor nor army can easily reach.

MOR.name: Maḵzan Quwwād
MOR.desc: The quwwād are crown-appointed regional governors whom the sultan dispatches to assert central authority over the territories the throne administers directly, collecting taxes, administering justice, and maintaining order on behalf of the throne. By formalizing the appointment and oversight of these quwwād, we extend the reach of the Maḵzan apparatus across our realm and reduce the autonomy of the great tribal confederations that might otherwise govern by custom alone. This integration of crown-appointed officers with local influence is the administrative heart of the Moroccan state.

MOR.name: War Tribes of the Ḡarb
MOR.desc: The Ḵlūṭ, the Sufyān, the Ṭlīq and the Riyāḥ hold the plains of the Ḡarb, the Azġar and the Habṭ on the same terms their forebears took them: land to cultivate and freedom from the tax collector, in return for riding when the sultan calls. It is service we buy and not obedience, and the distinction is lost on neither party — these are tribes we treat with rather than tribes we govern. What the bargain gives us is numbers, for a summons carried to every tent of four confederations puts more men in the saddle than any muster of the towns.

MOR.name: Bay'a Succession
MOR.desc: The bay'a is the oath of allegiance by which the leading men of the realm — the nobles, scholars, and tribal chiefs who constitute the ahl al-ḥall wa'l-'aqd — affirm a new ruler's right to govern. This law frames the manner in which that affirmation is organized and whose voice carries the greatest weight in the succession council.

MOR.name: Bled el-Maḵzan and Bled es-Siba
MOR.desc: The Moroccan sultanate has never governed the full extent of its territory through direct administration. The bled el-maḵzan — the land of government — is the settled zone where royal officials collect taxes and enforce order, while the bled es-siba — the land of dissidence — is the tribal hinterland that accepts the sultan's spiritual authority but resists his fiscal reach. This law determines where the balance falls.

MOR.name: Centralized Maḵzan
MOR.desc: The sultan extends direct royal administration, deploying quwwād and tax collectors deep into the tribal hinterland and subordinating local custom to the authority of the throne. The treasury grows richer, but the tribal confederations chafe under impositions they regard as a violation of traditional autonomy.

MOR.name: Negotiated Authority
MOR.desc: The sultan governs through bargain and recognition rather than direct coercionm, acknowledging the autonomy of tribal confederations in exchange for nominal submission and informal military cooperation. Revenue flows more slowly to the throne, but the realm holds together without the constant friction of forced compliance.

MOR.name: Shūrā Council
MOR.desc: The bay'a is administered through a formal consultative council of jurists and nobles whose deliberative process lends the succession the weight of Islamic scholarly consensus. Their collective endorsement anchors the ruler's legitimacy in the religious and aristocratic traditions of the realm.

MOR.name: Tribal Assembly
MOR.desc: The bay'a is confirmed by a great assembly of tribal chiefs whose collective oath binds the leading clans to the new ruler's authority and ensures their cooperation across the distant reaches of the realm. This tribal affirmation distributes political legitimacy widely, though it also reinforces the power of the confederation over the central state.

MOR.name: Black Guard
MOR.desc: The Black Guard is an elite corps of slave soldiers: enslaved men, haratin, and free Muslims raised from childhood to a strict religious creed and drilled in archery, horsemanship, and musketry. They form the backbone of our army.

MOR.name: Guich Cavalry
MOR.desc: The Guich Cavalry are the standing cavalry of the Moroccan Maḵzan — jīš tribesmen, of usually Arab origin, settled on arḍ al-jayš and holding their plots free of tax for as long as they ride. They are soldier-cultivators and not nobles, with no lineage of their own to fall back on, and that is precisely why the sultan trusts them: a corps whose standing depends entirely upon the crown. Mounted and paid in land, they carry the sultan's writ into country where a tax collector alone would not be heeded, and they cost the treasury less than any force that must be paid in coin.

MOR.name: Salé Rover
MOR.desc: The Salé Rover is the light corsair sailing vessel of the Bou Regreg republic — the shallow-draft raider built in the shipyards of Salé and Rabat by the Hornachero and Morisco refugees who established their independent corsair city-state at the mouth of the river. Our captains sail these swift ships into the Atlantic lanes to intercept the coastal traffic of Iberia, the Canaries, and the western Mediterranean approaches, outrunning any heavy war-galleon sent in pursuit. This Salé Rover tradition gives our state a fleet of fast Atlantic raiders that no galley-based corsair navy can replicate in open-sea conditions.

MOR.name: Black Guard
MOR.desc: The Black Guard is an elite corps of slave soldiers: enslaved men, haratin, and free Muslims raised from childhood to a strict religious creed and drilled in archery, horsemanship, and musketry. They form the backbone of our army.

MOR.name: Chichaoua Sugar
MOR.desc: Our sugar plantations and refining mills at Chichaoua, the Sus valley, and the Tadla plain transform Moroccan agriculture into an industrial export complex that holds every stage under one hand: sultanic charters grant tax-exempt status to the cane plantations, royal mills process the cane into refined loaves, and the imperial treasury takes a share at every stage. Our sukkar al-Maghribī reaches European bookkeepers, druggists, and confectioners through the Atlantic ports, commanding premium prices over Madeiran and Brazilian competitors. This sugar industry, held in royal hands from cane to loaf, generates revenue our central treasury draws upon directly and gives the Moroccan crown a luxury export advantage no other Maghrebi state can match.

MOR.name: Dhahabī Golden Age
MOR.desc: Our court under great sultans of the imperial heyday, the era subsequent generations remember as the dhahabī or golden age, accumulates wealth on a scale no later Maghrebi state can equal. Gold flows in from the Saharan termini at Sijilmasa, Walata, and Timbuktu; refined sugar departs the Atlantic ports for European confectioners; ambassadors arrive from courts across Christendom and the Sublime Porte seeking alliance or commerce. Sustained prosperity fills the treasury, and subsequent reigns draw upon it to fund military campaigns, religious endowments, and dynastic ceremonies that lesser states cannot afford.

MOR.name: First Fleet of the Mediterranean
MOR.desc: The fleet of the al-Muwaḥḥidūn caliphs at Marrakesh, sustained by tribute payments from the Italian maritime republics under Ya'qūb al-Manṣūr and command-coordinated from the imperial capital, established Moroccan naval supremacy in the western Mediterranean for two centuries. Our sultans inherit not only the docks at Salé, Asilah, and Larache but the doctrine of strategic centralization: fleets dispatched against single objectives at the order of Marrakesh, rather than the dispersed privateering that any coastal corsair captain could mount on his own. An imperial command tradition lets our navy operate as a coherent strategic instrument, which fragmented coastal corsair fleets could never be.

MOR.name: Foreign Politics
MOR.desc: Morocco's strategic position controlling the western Mediterranean gateway and the Atlantic re-supply route makes us the indispensable diplomatic counterweight for any European power seeking advantage against another. Our envoys at foreign courts negotiate as equals; the Sublime Door of Marrakesh receives ambassadors, signs commerce treaties, and arbitrates disputes between Christian princes who would never accept such mediation from any other Muslim sovereign. This unique diplomatic standing gives the Moroccan throne influence in European affairs that no other Maghrebi or sub-Saharan state can match.

MOR.name: Imperial Modernization
MOR.desc: Successive nineteenth-century sultans pursue a continuous program of administrative, fiscal, and military modernization: recruiting foreign technical advisors, restructuring the makhzen chancery, modernizing the imperial arsenals, and standardizing tax collection across the realm. Each reform faces resistance from entrenched tribal and ulema interests, but a slow habit of reform and adjustment gradually emerges and persists across changing sultans. This sustained adaptation lets our crown promote technicians, engineers, and modern administrators into positions of state authority while every source of revenue yields more to the treasury.

MOR.name: Jaysh Armies
MOR.desc: Our sultans have granted military estates to the jaysh tribes, chiefly the Banū Ma'qil and Banū Ḥassān, in exchange for permanent cavalry service to the throne. These warrior clans hold their lands tax-free and answer the sultan's call with their full mounted strength, providing the mobile striking force that the makhzen deploys against rebellious cities and Sahel raids. This integration of pastoral Arab tribes into a feudal military system gives Morocco a standing cavalry reserve at no fiscal cost to the central treasury.

MOR.name: Makhzen Taxation Reform
MOR.desc: The traditional patchwork of kharāj, 'ushūr, zakāt, and city guild gharāma taxes is repeatedly reorganized into more efficient consolidated forms: the unified per capita tertib on the rural plain, the standardized urban tax, and the regularized Atlantic-port customs assessments. Our merchants come to know what they will owe, our Jewish-Andalusi banking houses at Tetouan and Mogador refine their lending terms accordingly, and our treasury captures revenue that previously leaked through the cracks of overlapping exemptions. Continuous fiscal modernization gives our crown the wealth to fund modern armies and public works, beyond what purely traditional tax regimes can bear.

MOR.name: Marinid Madrasas
MOR.desc: Marinid sultans endow a network of imperial madrasas across Fez and the surrounding cities (the Bū 'Ināniyya, the 'Aṭṭārīn, the Bū 'Ināniyya of Meknes, the Ṣahrīj, and the Miṣbāḥiyya), each with mosque, library, hospice, teaching staff, and student stipends paid from the sultanic treasury. The graduates staff the qāḍī benches, the chancery scribes, and the sermon givers of the kingdom, binding the religious establishment to the imperial throne through shared training. This sultan-funded scholarship makes our state more learned and draws reformist scholars from across the Muslim world to our court.

MOR.name: Marinid Takeover
MOR.desc: The Banū Marīn, Zenata Berbers from the eastern plateaus, supplant the failing Almohads at Marrakesh and rebuild the imperial state around a reformed makhzen chancery at Fez al-Jadid, a streamlined dīwān of provincial governors, and a court ceremonial purged of Almohad religious and doctrinal overreach. The dynastic transition consolidates a leaner, administratively coherent imperial throne than the sprawling caliphate it replaces. The Marinid reorganization gives our court a centralized government that works, as the Almohad inheritance alone could not have provided.

MOR.name: Marrakesh–Fez Axis
MOR.desc: Our imperial throne rests on two capitals: Marrakesh holds the ceremonial prestige inherited from Almohad caliphal claims, while Fez al-Jadid serves as the administrative and religious heart of the realm. Each capital governs its own half of our territory through its own dīwāns and military command, while the sultan circulates between them on a yearly ceremonial circuit asserting central authority across the kingdom. This arrangement of two capitals carries our reach further across our territory than any single-seat Maghrebi state can hope to match.

MOR.name: Sa'dī Sharifian Emergence
MOR.desc: The Banū Sa'd, descended from the Prophet Muḥammad through Ḥasan ibn 'Alī and long settled in the Drâa Valley as a family of sharifian local notables, emerge in the early sixteenth century as claimants to the sultanate against the failing Waṭṭāsids. Their dynastic mission, to restore unified Moroccan-Arab imperial authority under a sharifian crown, wins them swift support from the ulema of Fez and Marrakesh, the trans-Saharan caravan masters, and the urban Andalusi exile communities. This dynastic emergence lets our envoys claim the prestige of prophetic descent across the courts of the Muslim Mediterranean and the Saharan trade world.

MOR.name: Sharifian Inviolability
MOR.desc: The constitutional doctrine of sharifian inviolability holds that our sultan, descended from the Prophet through Ḥasan ibn 'Alī, cannot be challenged on the same footing as a mere governor or qā'id. Provincial revolts may topple individual ummāl, urban risings may unseat hated tax collectors, and tribal confederations may resist particular royal commands, but the sharifian crown itself remains constitutionally sacrosanct in the eyes of the ulema and the bay'a-bound notables. This deep dynastic legitimacy lets our state weather provincial unrest that would topple monarchies dependent on purely secular authority.

MOR.name: Strongholds of the Atlas
MOR.desc: The mountain ranges that crown our territory (the High Atlas, the Middle Atlas, the Anti-Atlas, and the Rif) are the reason no foreign empire has ever held Morocco in lasting submission. Our Amazigh mountain clans have garrisoned the passes since the Roman attempts of Pliny's day, and our network of qaṣbah fortresses at Telouet, Aït Benhaddou, and the high valleys lets us hold defensible ground against any invader. This fortified geography makes Morocco the only kingdom whose interior cannot be conquered by sea or by Saharan crossing.

MOR.name: The Maḵzan
MOR.desc: The loose authority of the early sultanate must give way to a true maḵzan, a standing apparatus of tax-gatherers, secretaries, and appointed governors that carries the will of the throne from the obedient heartland into the lands of dissidence. With it, the central state ceases to be a matter of the ruler as an individual and becomes an institution that endures.

MOR.name: Ṭā'ifa
MOR.desc: When the Caliphate of Córdoba fell, al-'Andalus broke apart into a mosaic of petty emirates, called the ṭawā'if, each a court unto itself. Brilliant in learning yet jealous of one another, they could never stand alone against the Christian north. Bound now to a restored power in Iberia, a Ṭā'ifa keeps its own character while bending to the authority of a single sovereign.

MOR.name: Ahl al-Ḥall wa-l-'Aqd
MOR.desc: The Ahl al-Ḥall wa-l-'Aqd — those who loosen and bind — are the body of jurists, scholars, and senior notables whose collective consensus has traditionally conferred legitimacy upon Islamic rulers, their opinion standing as the community's endorsement of sovereignty. We convene this council as the formal deliberative institution of our realm, giving the 'ulamā' and the leading houses a structured voice in the affairs of state. A well-supported council translates scholarly authority into durable legitimacy; without the resources to maintain it, its rulings carry less weight, and the consensus that sustains our authority becomes harder to summon.

MOR.name: Al-Maḵzan
MOR.desc: Al-Maḵzan is the central apparatus of the sultan's authority, its tax-gatherers and governors extending the writ of the throne. A strong maḵzan tightens the crown's grip over distant tribes and towns, but when its administration falters the country truly becomes a bilād as-sība, the land of dissidence, and outlying provinces slip toward rebellion and autonomy.

MOR.name: Cultivate Andalusi Influence
MOR.desc: Our envoys and our scholars cross the Strait week after week, pressing our case at the of the ruler. The slow weight of patronage, marriage offers, and frontier garrisons binds the elites of the realm tighter to our side with every passing month.

MOR.name: Dār al-Ṭirāz
MOR.desc: The ostentous embroided clothes originating from Persia have long been used in the Islamic world as robes of honor the sovereign bestows upon those he favors. A well-funded royal Dār al-Ṭirāz workshop that weaves silk, brocade, and embroidery will clothe the court in splendor and send prized fabrics to every market.

MOR.name: Dīwān al-Qawāfil
MOR.desc: The Dīwān al-Qawāfil oversees the great caravans of the trans-Saharan trade, the routes through Sijilmāsa that carry gold and slaves north and salt and cloth south. A well-run office protects the merchants and their beasts and swells the wealth that crosses the desert, lest the caravans get prey to raiders, and the tribes of the sand grow hostile to a power that no longer secures the road.

MOR.name: Dīwān al-Ḡarb
MOR.desc: Dīwān al-Ḡarb — the Bureau of the West — is the administrative organ we plant in our Andalusi provinces to govern a population that speaks Arabized Romance as readily as Arabic and whose parish churches still outnumber our mosques. Its scribes collect the sultan's revenues, appoint qāḍīs over the mixed courts, and press the assimilation that turns conquest into province. A well-run bureau binds these western lands to our law; a neglected one hands the frontier to whatever clan can enforce its own.

MOR.name: Qāḍī al-Jamā'a
MOR.desc: The Qāḍī al-Jamā'a is the chief judge of the community, who presides over the Mālikī courts and appoints the many local qāḍī of the realm. A respected judiciary system settles disputes by law recognized by all and lends the throne the legitimacy of justice, deepening the people's attachment to formal jurisprudence.

MOR.name: Ri'āyat al-Madāris
MOR.desc: The Ri'āyat al-Madāris is the crown's patronage of the madrasas, the colleges that train the jurists, scribes, and officials on whom the state depends. Endowed generously, they fill the cabinet with learned and loyal servants and entrench the formal law of the schools.

MOR.name: Salé Arsenal
MOR.desc: The royal dār al-ṣināʿa of Salé stands at the mouth of the Bou Regreg, where Marinid shipwrights lay keels and fit out the vessels that carry our flag onto the Atlantic. The yards keep a standing body of caulkers and seasoned pilots close at hand, so a crew is found quickly whenever a hull is ready for the water. No other harbor on this coast arms a fleet with such ease.

MOR.name: The Gold Caravan
MOR.desc: Send a caravan south across the Sahara to the golden markets of the Bilād as-Sūdān, trading salt and cloth for the wealth of the Sahel. The road is long and the desert perilous, but a caravan that returns home will pour the gold of the Sahel into your capital's market.

MOR.name: Ṭā'ifa
MOR.desc: When the Caliphate of Córdoba fell, al-'Andalus broke apart into a mosaic of petty emirates, called the ṭawā'if, each a court unto itself. Brilliant in learning yet jealous of one another, they could never stand alone against the Christian north. Bound now to a restored power in Iberia, a Ṭā'ifa keeps its own character while bending to the authority of a single sovereign.

MOS.name: Chosen Rada
MOS.desc: The Chosen Rada creates a powerful council loyal to the ruler, with sweeping authority to suppress the power of the elites. The council's influence extends to matters of governance, policy, and decision-making.

MOS.name: Collegium
MOS.desc: The Collegium is an overhaul of the administrative structure used for government bureaucracy. It establishes several collegiums as government departments, with a systematic separation of responsibilities to avoid possible overlapping of duties. The collegiums are also tasked with case resolutions, with the help of advisory guidelines.

MOS.name: Court Ceremonies
MOS.desc: The introduction of the Court Ceremonies ensures grand ceremonies are carried out in accordance with traditions. Meticulous court etiquette is upheld, thereby elevating the prestige and splendor of the ruling elite.

MOS.name: Nakaz
MOS.desc: The Nakaz is an overhaul of the legal code concerning equality, justice, and humanitarianism. Heavily influenced by the Enlightenment, it aims to emulate the progressive reforms that are taking place across Europe, whilst simultaneously simplifying the code of law.

MOS.name: Prikazi
MOS.desc: The Prikazi is an overhaul of the administrative structure used for government bureaucracy. It establishes several bureaus that are responsible for various aspects of governance, such as taxation, justice, military affairs, and trade, which facilitates more rapid implementation of the policies and decisions made by the Tsar.

MOS.name: Razriadnyi Prikaz
MOS.desc: The Razriadnyi Prikaz introduces a census, which is used to maintain records of the country's population, property, and taxation. It is updated at regular intervals, assesses the military obligations of the estates, and maintains a record of land and property ownership, ensuring that what is due is paid.

MOS.name: Gatherers of Tribute
MOS.desc: Our position as the collector of tribute for the Golden Horde has given us many years of experience in gathering tribute... and in retaining some of the profits for ourselves.

MOS.name: Hurricane Hardy
MOS.desc: The designs of Feodor Apraksin are robust and resilient, enabling ships to weather most storms that Mother Nature is able to conjure. The innovative construction greatly contributes to any burgeoning maritime ambitions.

MOS.name: Organized Levies
MOS.desc: Governing the vast expanse of Russia is no easy task. We should establish local recruitment centers to make drafting levies into our armies easier.

MOS.name: Pomestnoe Voisko
MOS.desc: By redistributing plots of confiscated lands to noble cavalrymen, we can build a new class of soldiers to defend our principality.

MOS.name: Preobrazhensky Semyonovsky Imperial Guard
MOS.desc: The 'Toy Army' is organized into elite companies, forming the Imperial Guard which protects the interests of the monarchy. They are frequently involved in court ceremonies, parades, and other significant events, showcasing their importance beyond their military duties.

MOS.name: Rule through Dynastic Ties
MOS.desc: The lands of Russia have been ruled by one dynasty since time immemorial. We should utilize our position among our peers and our blood ties to take a leading role.

MOS.name: Seat of the Metropolitan Bishop
MOS.desc: The Russian people need firm religious guidance. We have historically cooperated well with the Church, and expanding this relationship would benefit us all. If we can move the seat of the Metropolitan Bishop to Moscow, we will be able to strengthen the bonds between our faith and our state.

MOS.name: Strength of the Boyars
MOS.desc: The Boyar class is in many ways the foundation of Russia, but just as we need to strengthen the Boyars, we also need to control them. We must protect seats for the Boyars in the Duma, but also to make sure that they are dependent on us to further their influence.

MOS.name: Zasechnaya Cherta
MOS.desc: In order to withstand the constant threat of Tatar raids, our ancestors have built a line of tightly positioned and well-defended forts. As our state grows larger, we should keep expanding this 'Abatis Line' to ensure our people are always protected from foreign attacks.

MTR.name: Marshland Guerillas
MTR.desc: We specifically train our levies to lure enemy units into the deep bogs where their armor becomes a liability. In these environments, our light, unarmored infantry reigns supreme through ambush tactics, turning the very earth into a weapon. Our ability to adapt to any terrain and move fast in the worst conditions makes us a dangerous foe.

MTR.name: Reclamation Engineering
MTR.desc: We have begun the process of draining parts of the Myzeqe marshes to create even more fertile farmland. This engineering feat not only increases our tax base but allows us to construct permanent roads through what was once impassable bog.

MTR.name: The Lagoon Fisheries
MTR.desc: The biological wealth of our coastal waters provides a stable food supply that supports a larger standing militia even during regional famines. By monopolizing the harvest of the lagoons, we ensure that our population remains healthy and our granaries full, fueling our state's survival.

MTR.name: The Masters of the Karavasta
MTR.desc: Our domain is protected by the labyrinthine Karavasta Lagoon, where our people have mastered navigation through mudflats and hidden channels. This watery landscape serves as a natural fortress that is nearly impossible for heavy foreign armies to map or conquer, providing a sanctuary that no cavalry charge can reach.

MTR.name: The Mataranga Port Authority
MTR.desc: We have unified all coastal harbors under a single administrative authority, streamlining the collection of dues and customs. This centralization has made us the most efficient trade administrators in the Adriatic, drawing the gold of foreign merchants.

MTR.name: The Trade Monopolies
MTR.desc: By controlling the river mouths and coasts, we can successfully dictate the flow of timber and grain from the interior to Venetian galleys. We have positioned ourselves as the indispensable middlemen of the Adriatic trade, ensuring no merchant can bypass our tolls.

MZB.name: Djemaa Governance
MZB.desc: Each Mzab city is governed by its own djemaa (an assembly of family head representatives) which meets in the city mosque courtyard to debate civic affairs, settle disputes, and elect the council of 'azzāba who exercise ultimate moral authority. The djemaa system has no inherited offices or noble privileges; every adult male of the founding families holds an equal vote, and the assembly's collective rulings bind even the wealthiest merchant houses. Proto-republican consensus governance steadies our pentapolis, resting on a religious and communal solidarity that no autocratic sultanate can command.

MZB.name: Ibadi Codification
MZB.desc: Our scholars at Beni Isguen and Ghardaïa compile the great Ibadi-Wahbī jurisprudence, the Kitāb an-Nīl of Sheikh 'Abd al-'Azīz ath-Thamīnī, the legal commentaries of Atfayyash and Bābū, codifying centuries of fiqh al-'ibādiyya into a written reference corpus. We send our promising young students from each pentapolis city to the others to learn from the senior 'azzāba councils, and our scholarly graduates serve as judges, scribes, and missionaries across the broader Ibadi world from Oman to Zanzibar. Codification gives our religious establishment a depth and coherence within our sect that no Sunni-Maghrebi madrasa tradition can offer.

MZB.name: Ibadi Modernism
MZB.desc: Our late-nineteenth-century intellectuals (Sheikh Muḥammad ben Yūsuf Atfayyash, the Pole of the Wahbiyya; Sheikh Ibrāhīm Bayyūḍ; and the younger generation of Salafiyya reformers) open the Mzab to dialogue with the wider Islamic reformist movements of Cairo, Damascus, and the Indian Ocean. We send our students to Tunis and Cairo, our journals from Ghardaïa engage with the Salafi press of Algiers and Constantine, and our pentapolis scholarly tradition meets the wider Ibadi world of Zanzibar and Oman on equal footing. The modernist intellectual revival binds the scattered Ibadi world into a shared modern community that a centralizing foreign administration will struggle to break up.

MZB.name: Ibadi Seclusion
MZB.desc: Our communities practice the doctrine of taqiyya (precautionary dissimulation) when interacting with Sunni-majority neighbors, professing common Sunni forms in public while maintaining strict Ibadi orthodoxy within the pentapolis walls. Our women are veiled and confined to the home courtyards, our markets segregate visitors from the inner sacred spaces, and our jurists publicly defer to the Mālikī fatwās of Algiers and Tunis while privately following their own al-Madhhab al-Wahbī line. This doctrine of religious and cultural seclusion preserves our distinct Ibadi identity through centuries of Sunni political pressure that have erased every other Khārijī community.

MZB.name: Mozabite Diaspora
MZB.desc: The first Mozabite merchant families (the Bayyūḍs, the Atfayyashes, the Bā Ḥaqqs) begin establishing trading houses in Algiers, Constantine, Tunis, and the smaller Algerian coastal towns, sending their sons north to learn commerce while their daughters remain at home in the pentapolis. Our diaspora merchants serve as a financial information network for the Ibadi community at home, extending Ibadi credit, sourcing grain in lean years, and channeling profits back into pentapolis endowments. Our emerging diaspora carries our financial reach across the Maghreb, farther than any Saharan community of comparable size has ever managed.

MZB.name: Pentapolis of the Mzab
MZB.desc: The five fortified Ibadi cities of the M'zab valley (Ghardaïa, Beni Isguen, Bou Noura, Melika, and El Atteuf) rise above the Wādī M'zab as a refuge for the Ibadi survivors of the Rustamid kingdom destroyed at Tāhart in 909. Each city is built as a fortified qṣar with its mosque tower serving as both minaret and watchtower, governed by the consensus of its founding families and bound to its sisters by intermarriage and a shared halqa al-'azzāba religious council. The pentapolis leaves our Ibadi community an urban heritage of walls and towers that no other Saharan settlement can claim.

MZK.name: Agricultural Wealth of the Devoll
MZK.desc: The fertile valleys of our heartland allow us to fund a lavish court and a highly trained cavalry force through advanced irrigation. The Devoll's harvests feed our political ambitions and fill the ranks of a large professional retinue.

MZK.name: Literary Patronage
MZK.desc: We have turned our capital into a center of culture, preserving the wisdom of the East and the West for future generations. This intellectual prestige makes our court the destination for the finest minds of the Orthodox and Latin worlds alike.

MZK.name: Silk Road Waystations
MZK.desc: Our land sits on the primary trade routes from the interior; by taxing the silk caravans, we maintain a full and prosperous treasury. This revenue allows us to patronize the finest calligraphers and icon painters, turning our domain into the cultural capital of southern Albania.

MZK.name: The Despots of Berat
MZK.desc: Ruling from the Castle of Berat, the 'City of a Thousand Windows', we represent the peak of Albanian urban sophistication and Byzantine-style administration. Our court serves as a magnet for scholars and artisans, turning our capital into a beacon of culture that rivals the grand cities of the East.

MZK.name: The Muzaka Chronicle
MZK.desc: Our family keeps meticulous and grand records of our history and territorial rights, ensuring our ancient claims are never forgotten. This literary tradition preserves our high Byzantine titles, overawing local rivals with our imperial dignity and historical depth.

MZK.name: The Muzakan Industrialization
MZK.desc: We have introduced the large-scale cultivation of cash crops in our most fertile valleys, fueling a new domestic industry. By processing our own raw materials into high-value products, we have created an industrial base that supports a wealthy and loyal urban population.

NAP.name: Accademia Pontaniana
NAP.desc: For a long time, Naples has striven to be a center of modern learning, attracting the great minds of the age and spreading the light of the Renaissance. Under the leadership of Giovanni Pontano, these discussion circles have been given structure and organization. It is only fitting that we name the academy after its industrious leader.

NAP.name: Encouraged City Living
NAP.desc: We have inherited an exquisite city from our predecessors. We must continue to beautify and improve this metropolis of the Mediterranean so that it can continue to grow and prosper. No longer can we content ourselves with merely repairing and maintaining the port and buildings; we shall make holistic improvements that better sustain our people by also building aqueducts, draining wetlands, and paving more roads.
mods: Possible Burghers in Towns and Cities

NAP.name: Expanded Arsenale
NAP.desc: For centuries, the Arsenale of Naples has been the center of our ship production and our main naval installation. However, it needs to be expanded and modernized to remain effective against hostile Mediterranean fleets. Let us expand both the commercial and military strength of our port, building a greater Arsenale to maintain a larger, more powerful fleet.

NAP.name: Institutional Reorganization
NAP.desc: By abolishing the Collateral Council and establishing the Real Camera di Santa Chiara, we will implement important legal reforms in Naples. Ongoing projects will aim to reorganize the legislative complex, consolidate laws into the Codice Carolino, and implement the Onciario Cadastre for tax reform.

NAP.name: Neapolitan Industrialization
NAP.desc: Naples has witnessed a gradual industrialization process over the past decades. Key sectors such as textiles, shipbuilding, and ironworks have experienced significant growth, fueled by investments and technological advancements. This shift towards industrialization will play a significant role in transforming Naples into a major economic center.

NAP.name: The University of Naples
NAP.desc: Founded in 1224 by Emperor Frederick II, the University of Naples is one of Italy's oldest public institutions. Embracing a secular ethos, it has provided generations of students with a comprehensive education and contributed to intellectual advancements across various fields.

NAV.name: Navarrese Adaptability
NAV.desc: Being positioned between two larger nations has forced our nation to adapt or die. With a mixture of intelligent alliances and swift military actions, our realm has managed to survive despite its smaller size. This ability to quickly adjust our actions to suit our specific needs is an edge that we should never lose.

NAV.name: Belligerent Stance
NAV.desc: Only an aggressive attitude will keep us safe. We will use whatever tools we have to make it clear that whoever attacks us will pay a high cost.

NAV.name: Conciliatory Stance
NAV.desc: The time of fighting is over, and we must pivot towards employing more diplomacy. After all 'you catch more flies with honey than with vinegar'`.

NAV.name: Defensive Stance
NAV.desc: Our lands are rugged as our people. Let our enemies come and bleed in our soil; future harvests will grow stronger.

NAV.name: Navarrese Maritime Code
NAV.desc: Based on the original Fuero of San Sebastián, the oldest maritime law in Europe, this code applies to every port in our possession and details the rights and duties of their inhabitants.

NAV.name: Offensive Stance
NAV.desc: We fear nobody, and as the old saying goes 'the best defense is a good offense'. We will attack first, and be deadlier than those who threaten our existence!

NAV.name: Order of the White Greyhound
NAV.desc: The Order of the White Greyhound was established by Charles III the Noble as the highest chivalric distinction of the Navarre Crown, selecting from the most loyal and distinguished knights of the realm. Its members, bound by an oath of mutual brotherhood and fidelity, are expected to embody the swiftness and loyalty of the greyhound in all their deeds. The order stands as a mark of royal prestige and trust, binding the Crown's closest allies in perpetual service and honor.

NAX.name: Achipelagic Vigil
NAX.desc: The scattered islands of the Aegean demand constant vigilance from their Latin rulers, who maintain fleets of light galleys to patrol against pirates, raiders, and rival Italian maritime powers. The dukes of Naxos and their vassals have developed a sophisticated system of island garrisons, signal fires, and swift courier vessels that allow them to respond rapidly to threats across the archipelago, while the wealth extracted from trade protection and harbor dues enables the construction of sturdy coastal fortresses that make the Cyclades one of the most secure regions of the Frankokratia, a maritime bulwark.

NAX.name: Aegean Waystation Networks
NAX.desc: In an era of global trade, our islands have become the indispensable waystations of the Mediterranean, providing fresh water, ship timber, and salted meats to long-haul vessels. By standardizing the port facilities across our twenty-odd islands, we ensure that any merchant ship must pay for the privilege of our hospitality. This logistics network makes us the undisputed masters of the Aegean's internal economy.

NAX.name: Sanudo's Isles
NAX.desc: Marco I Sanudo, a Venetian noble who participated in the Fourth Crusade, seized the Cyclades archipelago in 1207 and founded the Duchy of Naxos, creating a maritime feudal state whose lords ruled from fortified island citadels and drew income from trade, piracy suppression, and the fertile valleys of Naxos, Paros, and Santorini. By blending Italian commercial instincts with Frankish feudal organization, the Sanudo dynasty has maintained a semi-independent duchy that serves as a vital link in the Latin trade network, protecting shipping lanes while extracting tolls and offering safe harbors to Crusader, Genoese, and Venetian vessels alike.

NAX.name: The Aegean Hydrographic Bureau
NAX.desc: In an age of global exploration and precision, the Dukes of Naxos have established the premier center for Mediterranean cartography and maritime science. By employing the finest astronomers and clockmakers to map every reef, current, and wind pattern of the Cyclades, we have made our navigational charts the most sought-after tools in the world. This scientific mastery ensures that Naxiot captains can navigate the treacherous Aegean at night or in storm, granting our merchant and war fleets a decisive advantage in speed and safety over any foreign interloper.

NAX.name: The Marble Trade of Paros
NAX.desc: As the demand for fine art rises, the demand for high-quality Parian marble has returned to levels not seen since the days of Augustus. By reopening the ancient quarries and employing modern engineering techniques, we have turned a geologic quirk into a fountain of wealth that funds our Aegean hegemony. The palaces of Rome and Paris are increasingly built with stone hewn from our sovereign islands.

NAX.name: The Naxian Sea-Knights
NAX.desc: Our nobility is unique in the Western world; they are knights who have traded the horse for the galley and the lance for the boarding pike. These 'Sea-Knights' roam the Eastern Mediterranean under the Ducal banner, enforcing a 'Latin Peace'. This aggressive stance keeps our sailors sharp and our rivals' trade in constant peril.

NEG.name: Bridgehead of the Euripus
NEG.desc: The narrow channel separating our island from the mainland is the most strategic chokepoint in Central Greece, controlled by our massive swing bridge and fortified towers. By taxing the flow of goods between Boeotia and the Aegean, we have transformed a geographic oddity into a permanent source of toll revenue. We hold the key to the movement of armies in the Balkans, and we charge a heavy price for its use.

NEG.name: The Eubean Tidal Mills
NEG.desc: The unique, reversing tides of the Euripus Strait have been harnessed by our engineers to power a series of massive tidal mills. These machines provide consistent energy for milling grain, sawing ship timber, and powering forge bellows regardless of the wind. This technological advantage makes Euboea the most industrially advanced island in the Mediterranean, capable of out-producing its maritime rivals.

NEG.name: The Glassworks of Chalkis
NEG.desc: Using the high-quality silica sands of our beaches and the soda ash from our coastal plants, we have established a glassmaking industry that rivals Murano. Our mirrors and stained glass are exported to the great palaces of the Latin Empire and the West, bringing immense wealth to the island. The taxes on this luxury trade pay for the upkeep of our massive coastal walls in an age of gunpowder.

NEG.name: The Negropontine Navarchy
NEG.desc: The triarchs of Negroponte divided the lordship of the long island among three families, yet managed to maintain a unified naval policy that dominates the narrow Euripos channel and extracts tolls from every vessel passing between the Aegean and the northern ports. Their galleys, crewed by a mixture of Frankish knights, Greek mariners, and Italian mercenaries, patrol the straits with ruthless efficiency, ensuring that Negroponte remains one of the wealthiest and most strategically vital outposts of the Frankokratia.

NEG.name: The Three Fold-Defense
NEG.desc: The island of Euboea is divided among three Terzieri, or Triarchs, creating a competitive yet unified defensive structure that prevents any single lord from becoming weak. This tripartite system ensures that if one fortress falls, the other two mobilize instantly, creating a military administration that cannot easily be broken. This internal rivalry keeps our garrisons at peak readiness, as no Triarch wishes to be outdone by his peers.

NEG.name: The Triarchic Naval Academy
NEG.desc: To ensure the quality of our fleet, the three lords of the island have co-founded an academy for the training of naval officers and navigators. Students are taught the latest in astronomical navigation and maritime law, ensuring that every Euboean captain is a professional of the highest caliber. This focus on naval education keeps our fleet at the cutting edge of maritime warfare and exploration.

NEO.name: Neopatras Fortresses
NEO.desc: In the mountainous frontier of southern Thessaly, the lords of Neopatras, first Brienne and later Aragonese, constructed and repeatedly strengthened one of the most formidable castle complexes in Frankish Greece, turning the ancient city into a virtually impregnable stronghold that withstood repeated sieges by their enemies. These towering walls, deep ditches, and cleverly situated outworks became a symbol of Latin tenacity, allowing a small but determined garrison to project influence deep into central Greece and delay the northward advance of hostile powers for generations.

NEO.name: The Academy of Administration
NEO.desc: Neopatras needs to replace its hereditary 'Captain-Governors' with graduates of a dedicated Administrative Lyceum. Candidates are tested on their knowledge of our civil law and the latest techniques, ensuring that the nation's officials are as comfortable with a quill as they are with a sword. This shift from 'Birthright to Merit' has turned Neopatras into the most efficiently governed territory in Central Greece, capable of precise census taking and rapid tax levying.

NEO.name: The Consulate of the Sea
NEO.desc: Using our connections to the Crown of Aragon and the merchants of Barcelona, Neopatras has become the primary entry point for Iberian goods into the Levant. We operate a Consulate of the Sea that provides legal protection and standardized weights for all Catalan and Spanish traders. This special relationship makes Neopatras the wealthiest outpost of the Western Mediterranean in the heart of Greece.

NEO.name: The Great Company's Code
NEO.desc: The nation remains governed by the democratic and military traditions of the Catalan Company, where officers are elected and the spoils of war are shared. This egalitarian structure creates an army with incredibly high morale, as every soldier feels they have a personal stake in the survival of the state. While the rest of Europe moves toward absolutism, our 'Soldier's Republic' remains a fiercely loyal and cohesive fighting force.

NEO.name: The Neopatras Horse-Breeding Program
NEO.desc: In the fertile Spercheios valley, the Dukes have established royal stables to breed a new strain of warhorse, crossing Catalan stallions with local Balkan mares. The resulting Neopatras Charger is famed for its endurance in mountainous terrain and its shock power in the charge. This cavalry advantage allows us to dominate the open plains of Thessaly and strike fear into our rivals.

NEO.name: The Ordinance of the Viles Noves
NEO.desc: The realm has moved to centralize its scattered mountain population into 'New Towns' (Viles Noves in the Catalan language) modeled after the planned fortified villages of Catalonia. The governance of these towns is handed to a 'Consul of the Hearth', an official tasked with managing communal wood fuel and grain storage for the harsh winters. By controlling the heat and the bread of the highlands, our rule effectively ends the age of independent mountain warlords, replacing them with a streamlined, urbanized bureaucracy.

NOR.name: Sailors
NOR.desc: Ever since the very foundation of our nation, our people have lived off the ocean and the coast. Fishing, raiding, sea battles - our sailors have more experience than those of any other maritime nation, and we shall promote this expertise even further.

NOR.name: Bountiful Seas
NOR.desc: The Norwegian land cannot provide our people with enough food to sustain themselves. We will look to the sea to feed our people instead. Fortunately, the waters of the North Sea provide us with plenty of fishing grounds.

NOR.name: Military Shipbuilding
NOR.desc: The expansion of our fishing industry has also led to an expansion in shipbuilding. We have a ready pool of trained shipwrights at hand to expand our own production process.

NOR.name: Natural Seamanship
NOR.desc: With the growth of our fishing industry, we have also seen a corresponding expansion in the number of sailors in our realm. We should take advantage of this and recruit some of them to our navy, as seamanship is just as important as the ship itself.

NOR.name: Norwegian Merchants
NOR.desc: The ports of Norway have long been a desirable destination for merchants from all around Europe. It is time that we not only host foreign merchants in our ports, but benefit from the trades of northern Europe ourselves.

NOR.name: Pioneer Spirit
NOR.desc: In days gone by, our people would brave the high seas to establish colonies on distant shores. Let us rekindle this adventurous spirit in our people so that they sail forth again!

NOR.name: Seaborn Country
NOR.desc: The Norwegian people have always chosen to traverse the country by boat, whenever it is convenient. This makes our people adept sailors, ready to man our navy whenever necessary.

NOR.name: The Call of our Forefathers
NOR.desc: Long ago, our illustrious forefathers sailed forth and established colonies in the North. Our sagas even tell us that they reached a new world and established Vinland. We must follow in their footsteps.

NOR.name: Write New Sagas
NOR.desc:
Keen minds preserve knowledge
Known from ages past
Sung in the sundown
Sagas are our inheritance
Encouraged by the establishment
Each country will have its own

NOR.name: Kjøpstad Rights
NOR.desc: Granting privileges to the merchants of this location and giving them preferential treatment will bolster our own trading routes, while disfavoring foreign merchants.

NOV.name: Expanded Posadnichestvo
NOV.desc: The office of the Posadnik is a highly influential position. In order to avoid a one-person power monopoly, the office must be expanded, so that multiple members of the Nobility can assume this position at the same time and keep each other in check.

NOV.name: Ivan's Hundred
NOV.desc: The heads of the Ivan's Hundred, our local merchant guild, are permanent members of the commerce court of Novgorod and the ruling council of the Novgorod Republic. With their political presence and the agreements they have made with the Nobility, our nation will surely enjoy continued, successful trade.
mods: Crown Power (via Ivan's Hundred Merchant Association decision)
Trade Capacity % (via Ivan's Hundred Merchant Association decision)
Export Efficiency (via Ivan's Hundred Requests Monopoly on Beeswax decision)
Beeswax Output (via Ivan's Hundred Requests Monopoly on Beeswax decision)

NOV.name: Tysiatskii Office
NOV.desc: The Tysiatskii are military leaders selected from the Boyars. While in other states their responsibilities lie mostly in commanding our soldiers, our Tysiatskii Office serves additional functions as the representative of the Commoners, as acting judges in the commercial court, and as supervisors of our fortifications.
