NOV.name: Pyatina Division
NOV.desc: The Pyatina is the highest administrative division in Novgorod's government. The republic is divided into five Pyatinas, four of which border the city of Novgorod directly, while the fifth encompasses more distant territories.

NOV.name: Baltic Shipyard
NOV.desc: We shall build a grand shipyard on the eastern coast of the Baltic Sea, and dominate overseas trade!

NOV.name: Birchbark Manuscripts
NOV.desc: Writing and reading are fundamental pillars of our society. Religious texts, as well the details of our history, need to be written down so that future generations can learn of our cultural achievements. We have an abundant supply of birch trees in this nation, and their papery white bark will become our parchment.

NOV.name: City of Churches
NOV.desc: There are over eighty Orthodox churches in Novgorod, and some are the largest landholders in the principality. Their wealth and religious prestige allows the Church to significantly influence the population in many areas, and our citizens are more pious as a result — in a good way.

NOV.name: Defenses of Velikiy Novgorod
NOV.desc: The Republic of Velikiy Novgorod is the target of many external threats. But be it the western heretics from Scandinavia, the rampaging Germans to our southwest, or even other Russian powers to our south; they all shall all crumble at the feet of our unbreakable fortifications.

NOV.name: Grand Duke's Army
NOV.desc: Leading troops is the most important duty for the Grand Duke, who is appointed to rule over the Veche Republic. Under such strong and experienced leadership, our armies will become far more deadly in battle.

NOV.name: Northern Center of Arts
NOV.desc: Novgorod is an important cultural center in Europe. Epic tales are told of our's literate and intellectual population, intricate religious art, and grand architecture, increasing the prestige of our flourishing city and indeed the whole nation.

NOV.name: Novgorodian Fur Trade
NOV.desc: Fur, the silken gold of Russia! While other states gain their wealth from trading in Gold and other rare metals, our source of income comes from the high-quality Fur the motherland provides us with.

NOV.name: Reforms of the Posadnichestvo
NOV.desc: The Posadnik is the highest administrative position in our towns and cities, and is a more significant role than that of a mayor. As their city grows, so do the responsibilities, influence, and number of Posadniks in the administration.

NOV.name: The Ushkuyniks
NOV.desc: The Viking-like Ushkuynik pirates were once a useful tool to suppress our competitors. Unfortunately, we were forced to stop using them due to foreign intervention, mainly from Moscow. We should begin funding them again, and send these pirates to plunder farther shores — that will show everyone who the true masters of the North are!

NOV.name: Velikiy Novgorod First Chronicle
NOV.desc: The Novgorod First Chronicle details the history of our country, from the days of the legendary Varangian chieftain Rurik up to the present. It is a cultural heirloom that is proudly handed down from one generation to another.

NRM.name: Coutume de Normandie
NRM.desc: The codified customs of the emphasize feudal land rights, noble privilege, and local autonomy. While favoring a decentralized and traditional society, these laws form a robust legal framework that ensures the power of the nobility and preserves the distinct identity of the realm.

NRM.name: Channel Trade Ports
NRM.desc: Our position along the English Channel allows us to flourish as a commercial gateway. By investing in our port towns and merchant infrastructure, we can dominate regional trade while minimizing the cost of overseas operations.

NRM.name: Frontline of the Caroline War
NRM.desc: During the long conflicts between France and England, we stood as a strategic battleground. The pressures of war forged a hardened officer corps and traditions of battlefield excellence that endure to this day.

NRM.name: Heirs of Rollo
NRM.desc: The legacy of Rollo, the Viking founder of Normandy, continues to define our ruling house. Such a prestigious line has led to strengthened legitimacy and respect from our peers.

NRM.name: Norman Law
NRM.desc: Our state is governed by its own customary legal code, the Coutume de Normandie. By enshrining noble privilege, decentralized power, and property rights, this legal tradition ensures local stability while asserting our distinct identity.

NRM.name: The Exchequer
NRM.desc: Our legislative body must remain distinct from any outside influences, in an effort to preserve our cultural identity and independence. Inspired by Anglo-Norman fiscal institutions, our parliamentary procedures will surely bolster crown revenue and improve administrative oversight.

NSH.name: Society with the Lion
NSH.desc: Founded in the woes of the Western Schism, the Löwenbund is sworn to protect our lands from heretical revolts. We should grant them our official sponsorship and incorporate them into our court to further our cause.

NSH.name: Society with the Lion
NSH.desc: Founded in the woes of the Western Schism, the Löwenbund is sworn to protect our lands from heretical revolts. We should grant them our official sponsorship and incorporate them into our court to further our cause.

NSI.name: Society with the Lion
NSI.desc: Founded in the woes of the Western Schism, the Löwenbund is sworn to protect our lands from heretical revolts. We should grant them our official sponsorship and incorporate them into our court to further our cause.

NSI.name: Society with the Lion
NSI.desc: Founded in the woes of the Western Schism, the Löwenbund is sworn to protect our lands from heretical revolts. We should grant them our official sponsorship and incorporate them into our court to further our cause.

NSS.name: Society with the Lion
NSS.desc: Founded in the woes of the Western Schism, the Löwenbund is sworn to protect our lands from heretical revolts. We should grant them our official sponsorship and incorporate them into our court to further our cause.

NSS.name: Society with the Lion
NSS.desc: Founded in the woes of the Western Schism, the Löwenbund is sworn to protect our lands from heretical revolts. We should grant them our official sponsorship and incorporate them into our court to further our cause.

NSW.name: Society with the Lion
NSW.desc: Founded in the woes of the Western Schism, the Löwenbund is sworn to protect our lands from heretical revolts. We should grant them our official sponsorship and incorporate them into our court to further our cause.

NSW.name: Society with the Lion
NSW.desc: Founded in the woes of the Western Schism, the Löwenbund is sworn to protect our lands from heretical revolts. We should grant them our official sponsorship and incorporate them into our court to further our cause.

OBW.name: Eternal Alliance of the Forest Cantons
OBW.desc: We have forged an eternal alliance with our friends in the neighboring Cantons. Had it not been for this treaty, we would have surely succumbed to the Habsburg invaders and fallen under the rule of foreign tyrants yet again. These alliances will ensure our survival for centuries to come.

OGL.name: Camel Caravan Corps
OGL.desc: Our caravan protection auxiliary corps, the mehārist companies of mounted camel cavalry recruited from the Banū Wargla and the desert edge Berber tribes, patrol the southern approaches to our oasis, escorting incoming caravans through the Tassili and Tademaït plateaus where Tuareg raiders are most active. They serve under our crown on a contractual basis, paid through caravan toll revenues rather than the central treasury, and our officers integrate them as auxiliaries to the regular oasis garrisons during inter-state campaigns. The camel corps is a flexible Saharan striking force, able to range over long distances of desert where settled cavalry would founder.

OGL.name: Caravan Dominance
OGL.desc: We have established unrivalled dominance over the central Saharan trade. The Algerian-Regency caravans, the Tunisian-Hafsid merchant convoys, the Tafilalt-bound western traffic, and the deep Sahara Tuareg routes all pay tolls at our gates. Our caravan officers maintain registers of every animal passing through, our scribes record the goods and their values, and our crown takes a share of every transaction that the more decentralized oasis confederations cannot match. Our dominance of the trade route brings a steady flow of revenue, which other Saharan powers can only attempt to challenge through banditry.

OGL.name: In Salah Route
OGL.desc: Our caravan masters establish the Ouargla to Niger Bend route as the dominant central Saharan trade route, supplanting the older route from Sijilmasa through the western Sahara as the preferred path for our merchants. We maintain the In Salah staging post jointly with Tuareg confederations, each side providing guards, water rights guarantees, and warehouse space, and our jurists formalize the customs and toll schedules at every staging post. This ordered route, with its guards, wells, and fixed tolls, carries our merchants across the Sahara farther than any other oasis state can reach.

OGL.name: Saharan Terminus
OGL.desc: Our oasis sits at the northern terminus of the great trans-Saharan caravan routes coming up from Gao, Timbuktu, and the Niger bend. Every Soninke, Songhay, and Tuareg merchant arriving from the south must clear customs at our gates before pushing on to the Mediterranean. Our caravanserais (Sidi Lakhdar, Sidi Boumendil, the fanādiq of the central market) host the caravan crews and their pack animals for the months between expeditions, and our brokers arrange onward shipment to Algiers, Tunis, and Tripoli. At the terminus, our state takes a commanding share of the trans-Saharan trade revenues, which no maritime power can dispute.

OGL.name: Sharif of Ouargla
OGL.desc: Our local sharīf, Sīdī Muḥammad ben 'Abd Allāh claiming Idrīsid prophetic descent, proclaims a unified Saharan rising under a single banner of dynastic and religious resistance, gathering desert tribes, Tijāniyya brotherhoods, and disaffected oasis notables to his standard. His campaigns mobilize the deep Sahara confederations, the Tijānī lodges, and the Tafilalti caravan houses into an armed coalition that holds the southern Algerian frontier for years against any centralizing court that seeks to bring it under direct rule. The protracted Saharan rising wins our state the prestige of armed defiance and the power to rally many confederations at once, as the more rapidly subdued northern oases never did.

OGL.name: Southern Market
OGL.desc: Our central market becomes the dominant clearinghouse for the trans-Saharan trade in gold and slaves reaching the Maghreb. Bambara, Songhay, and Hausa captives are sold here to Mediterranean buyers, while the Wangara gold from Bambuk and Buré is assayed and forwarded under our seal to the mint houses of Algiers and Tunis. Our merchant houses extend credit to caravan masters waiting for season, our shrines accept votive offerings from grateful caravan survivors, and our cisterns serve every passing trader who pays the standardized water tax. Our primacy in trade fills the state's treasury from the commerce of a whole continent, a cushion no purely agricultural oasis economy could have.

OMA.name: Overseas Ambitions
OMA.desc: While the concepts of overseas expansion and colonialism have existed since antiquity, we have observed the modern ways of colonialism and have employed them ourselves. This will allow us to adopt their methods of overseas administration and create our own colonial empire.

OMA.name: Association With Unbelievers
OMA.desc: There are those who feel that we should not associate with unbelievers at all. We have done much to quash this, as only through association with heathen nations will we be able to trade with them.

OMA.name: Control of the Gulf
OMA.desc: Our sailors are used to navigating far and wide upon the seas, but control of the gulf surrounding us is what allows such travels. We must always stand ready to defend our waters against any foreign threat.

OMA.name: End of the Shipbuilding Guilds
OMA.desc: As long as ships have been built in Arabia, there have been guilds who control the production. Although they may have performed a valuable service in keeping shipbuilding traditions alive, they now stand in the way of progress. We must open up the shipbuilding industry to all with talent.

OMA.name: Expansion of Trade Contacts
OMA.desc: We must ensure that our merchants are always welcome wherever they go. Thus, we will use any means possible to make sure that all rulers we know about welcome our merchants.

OMA.name: Gulf of Oman
OMA.desc: Our nation is at the back of the ample and hostile deserts of Arabia, but the sea to our east allows us to circumvent them. It is by sea, not by land, that we will need to perform our diplomacy, trade, and expansion.

OMA.name: Land Isolation
OMA.desc: Despite not being an island, our land is factually isolated from the rest of Arabia due to the surrounding deserts. As such, we have learned how crucial it is to have access to the sea, and how useful it will be for us if we take that option away from our enemies.

OMA.name: Local Merchant Preference
OMA.desc: Theoretically a merchant can be a citizen of the world, sailing to and from whichever port he pleases. We are going to give advantages to home merchants, for example, priority for loading and unloading of cargo, to ensure that our merchants have every incentive to bring their products home.

OMA.name: Port Security Improvements
OMA.desc: To reap the full financial potential from trade, we need ships and any cargo they carry to be safe when docked in our ports. We must ensure that any areas that merchants consort in are free from petty crime.

OMA.name: Skilled Captains
OMA.desc: We must ensure that our captains meet the highest standards of seamanship and nautical knowledge, ensuring that they will be able to use every advantage in all situations.

ORI.name: Orissan Elephant Cavalry
ORI.desc: The elephant is a massive animal with far-reaching tusks and a thick hide. Its ability to traverse any kind of jungle gives the elephant a significant advantage in a very present niche of India. Atop of that, the Orissan War Elephant is capable of withstanding more physical punishment during combat compared to other elephants used for war due to their superior armor and training.

ORI.name: Anka Year System
ORI.desc: The Anka system is our method of documenting the regnal years of our rulers. Years ending in 6 or 0 are skipped, except for year 10, which is retained. The count begins at year 2, not year 1, and always starts on the Sunia, our fiscal new year.

ORI.name: Bulwark of the Hinduism
ORI.desc: The Muslim faithful have invaded India and subjugated many Hindu residents under their gruesome rule. Yet, Orissa stands unflinching against the warriors of Islam. We are the bulwark of Hinduism, and we shall defend our traditions and culture against any foreign invader!

ORI.name: Expansion of Infrastructure
ORI.desc: As technology advances, so does the number of people in our realm. Industrialization has driven significant population growth, and as such, we must expand our infrastructure to accommodate these growing communities.

ORI.name: Gajapati
ORI.desc: Horses are not native to Orissa, and the lands here are unsuitable for raising them. Our jungles are, however, famously teeming with elephants. In the dense jungles of Eastern India, well-executed tactical cooperation between elephants and infantry can be just as deadly as a cavalry. Let us further increase the size of our elephant corps and refine their tactics, so that we will be known as a true Gajapati, 'Lord of the Elephants'.

ORI.name: Odia Militarization
ORI.desc: The Muslim threat never ceases, nor does it ever rest. We must ensure our military is ready to face and combat invaders at any and all times.

ORI.name: Parikshas
ORI.desc: Orissa has long been divided among many different princes, but their time is over! We will take control of these lands, and appoint regional governors — parikshas — instead of allowing these petty princelings to dilute our imperial authority.

ORI.name: Patronized Temple Construction
ORI.desc: The glory of past dynasties is reflected by the grandeur of the temples they left behind. We should improve our many magnificent temple complexes, and construct new ones to further the development of Kalinga architecture.

ORI.name: Refined Cloth Production
ORI.desc: Orissa has been famous for its high-quality textiles since ancient times. Let us further encourage the textile guilds of Orissa to refine their methods of producing their fine Kalinga Cloth.

ORI.name: Salt Trade
ORI.desc: The high-quality Salt of Orissa is in demand all over India. Let us do whatever we can to encourage the Salt trade so that we may grow rich from it.

ORI.name: Servitor of Jagannath
ORI.desc: Worship of Jagannath, the Lord of the Universe, is what unites our people. Previous rulers of Orissa were even considered to be the scions of Jagannath. Our current ruler might not be one of his descendants, but we must imprint on all that our leader is the servitor of Jagannath, and that any disobedience to them equals treason against Lord Jagannath himself.

ORM.name: A Vast Emporium
ORM.desc: It has been said that Ormus is 'a vast emporium where there were peoples and goods of every description from all parts of the world' or that 'If all the world were a golden ring, Ormus would be the jewel in it'. Our realm's identity is inseparable from commerce. Indeed, ships from Gujarat, Arabia, and even China anchor in our ports, exchanging spices, Gems, Silk, and stories.

ORM.name: Gate of the Persian Gulf
ORM.desc: Ormus controls the strait that links the Indian Ocean to the interior of Asia. Whoever holds this vital passage dictates the rhythm of maritime traffic. Our command of these waters must be absolute, lest our influence be diminished.

ORM.name: Institutionalize the Moqarrariya
ORM.desc: For generations, our realm maintained peace with the mainland through the ancient tribute system known as Moqarrariya. Rather than depending on custom and negotiation, let us codify these tributes into formal pacts — securing fresh water, overland safety, and long-term stability through reliable diplomacy.

ORM.name: Invest in Qeshm and Ormus
ORM.desc: Though dry and rocky, the islands of Qeshm and Ormus have sustained urban life thanks to careful provisioning and rich trade. With proper investment, their ports and workshops can flourish further, turning them from logistical hubs into centers of innovation and productivity.

ORM.name: Mint of the Gulf
ORM.desc: Ormuzi coinage circulates from Basra al-Hamra to Bengal, trusted for its purity and weight. By institutionalizing our mint and expanding our issuance, we reinforce our financial sovereignty — and claim fiscal supremacy over the Indian Ocean.

ORM.name: Ormus Toll
ORM.desc: At the narrowest point of the Persian Gulf stands Ormus, the gatekeeper of east-west maritime trade. No vessel passes without our knowledge — or without paying our fee. For centuries, this toll has not just made us richer, but shaped our diplomacy and how we project power across the vast seas.

ORM.name: The Ormuzi Navy
ORM.desc: The Persian Gulf is crossed daily by our fleets — be they traders, patrols, or armed escorts. But to match the ambitions of those who envy our position, we must expand and modernize. Let Ormus become more than just a trading post: a maritime arsenal.

PAD.name: The Accademia Patavina
PAD.desc: We establish the Accademia Patavina di Scienze Lettere ed Arti to gather the leading scholars, physicians, and men of letters of the city into a single institution with the formal backing of the state, a structure that turns the individual brilliance of the university's faculty into a sustained collective enterprise capable of undertaking projects no single professor could manage. The Accademia provides a forum where the results of the university's research meet the practical needs of administration and commerce, making learned expertise available to the state at a fraction of the cost of maintaining separate advisory bodies. Organized scholarship gives our court an unusual depth of technical and administrative counsel and keeps in our service talented men who might otherwise seek the grander stages of larger states.

PAD.name: The Carraresi Signoria
PAD.desc: The da Carrara family have governed Padua for over a century as lords whose authority rests on a combination of personal prestige, legal sanction from the empire, and a genuine investment in the prosperity of the city they rule. Our administration has maintained the civic institutions that the commune period established, channeling their energy into the service of seignorial government rather than displacing them, and the result is a city that functions with unusual smoothness. This tradition of Signoria that respects the civic fabric it inherits makes our urban government work better and more cheaply, keeping our subjects settled and loyal.

PAD.name: The Paduan Commune
PAD.desc: The oldest municipal institutions of our city (the elected councils, the written statutes, the tradition of citizen participation in public decisions) have never been fully extinguished, even through the decades of seignorial government that placed a single family above them. We revive and formalize these communal structures, giving our merchants and burghers a recognized role in civic governance and restoring the sense that the city belongs to all its citizens rather than its rulers alone. This Comùn Padovàn (Comune Padovano in standard Italian: Paduan Commune) channels the energy of our most active citizens into institutions that serve the state, increasing the tax revenue that flows from a population that believes in the legitimacy of what it pays into.

PAD.name: The Paduan School of Philosophy
PAD.desc: The philosophy faculty of Padua has developed a tradition of rational inquiry into the natural world that operates on Aristotelian premises while reaching conclusions that trouble the Church far more than open theology might have. In Padua, it is considered legitimate to argue that the soul is mortal, that intellect is collective rather than individual, and that natural causes could explain what elsewhere requires divine intervention. This culture of secular reasoning produces lawyers, physicians, and administrators of unusual intellectual independence, trained to analyze rather than simply to accept authority. The reputation of the Paduan School makes our state a gathering point for minds that produce more careful governance, and draw scholars who enrich our city's intellectual life.

PAD.name: The School of Medicine
PAD.desc: The medical faculty of Padua has been recognized across Europe as the most rigorous training ground for physicians since the university was founded, combining systematic anatomical study with clinical observation in a way that the great Arab compilations alone could never provide. The students who pass through its dissection theater carry an understanding of the body more detailed and more precise than any other school in the Christian world could offer, and the physicians they become have changed how illness is understood and treated in every city they subsequently serve. Because our doctors trust what they observe, plague passes more lightly through our people than through those who rely on superstition, and the university deepens the literacy of every educated class it touches.

PAD.name: The University of Padua
PAD.desc: Founded in 1222, the Bò, named for the inn where its first students gathered, has never ceased to be one of the great centers of European learning, and Padua's willingness to teach subjects that more cautious universities declined has made it a destination for the curious minds of every generation. Vesalius performed his anatomical demonstrations here, Galileo lectured from its chair of mathematics, and the law faculty has trained judges and administrators across the continent. This unbroken tradition of free inquiry raises the literacy and skill of the burgher class that relies on the university and attracts scholars whose presence keeps the city's intellectual life in motion.

PAL.name: Humanist Court
PAL.desc: Our court and our ruler must strive towards humanist ideals. We must become a prime destination for aspiring artists and philosophers.

PAL.name: A Mild and Calm Ruler
PAL.desc: The only effect of bloodshed is to cause further bloodshed. Therefore, we need to be a forgiving ruler, and reconcile with our enemies to establish a lasting peace in our territories.

PAL.name: Castles on the Rhine
PAL.desc: By erecting multiple castles in key positions along the Rhine, we will be able to exert and expand our control over both the river and the trade flowing through it.

PAL.name: Consolidate the Territories
PAL.desc: Our administration is skilled in handling multiple disconnected territories without losing our grasp on them. With that, we can build a strong bureaucracy capable of handling even the most difficult tasks.

PAL.name: Forgiveness for Peasants
PAL.desc: When our peasantry rises up against our nobility, they unmistakably rise up against our own rule. However, we should not excessively punish those who revolt. With mild consequences, everyone will be more in alignment with our authority.

PAL.name: Heidelberg Catechism
PAL.desc: The Reformation has created many discussions around the nature of our faith. We should invest into a comprehensive catechism, to which our people will be able to adhere.

PAL.name: Humanist Education
PAL.desc: To govern well, our rulers must receive a comprehensive education in humanist ideas. To this effect, we must hire renowned humanists for the education of our rulers and heirs, while also focusing our court on these principles.

PAL.name: Local Fortification
PAL.desc: By virtue of having our territories disperse, we are vunerable to attacks from several foreign powers. Constructing many fortified outposts within our lands will buy us time to raise an army and repel any attempt to take over one of our many disconnected territories.

PAL.name: Palatinate Tolerance
PAL.desc: No matter their denominations, all Christian people must be welcomed in the towns and cities of our lands. While others may decide to suppress their religious minorities, our tolerance will ensure a steady stream of immigrants into our territory, and we shall benefit from their presence.

PAL.name: Palatine Lion
PAL.desc: Originating from the dynastic coat of arms of the Wittelsbach family, the Palatine Lion is the centerpiece of our legitimacy. Displayed with a red crown, it signifies our role as the Imperial Vicar and Arch-Steward of the Holy Roman Empire. As long as the Palatine Lion is proudly displayed on our crest, our legitimacy will not come into question.

PAL.name: Protect the Bibliotheca Palatina
PAL.desc: Rich in theological scriptures of several Christian denominations, the Bibliotheca Palatina is one of our most prized possessions. Protection of the knowledge and the cultural value contained within must be a high priority, so that we are able to keep relying on its documents.

PAL.name: Society with the Donkey
PAL.desc: Founded to protect knightly interests within the Empire, the Gesellschaft mit dem Esel has entrenched itself in the lands surrounding Heidelberg. Their expertise in governance, as well as their ability to sponsor tourneys, will improve our cultural standing.

PAL.name: Support the Romantic Movement
PAL.desc: A significant part of the Romantic movement is centered around Heidelberg. We should capitalize on this phenomenon, and support these and other artists in order to bolster our global recognition.

PAL.name: Vineyards and Orchards of the Rhine
PAL.desc: Although our territory is small, the sunny banks of the Rhine are perfectly suited to cultivate vineyards and orchards. With some effort, these could sustain our local economy by producing wine.

PAL.name: Society with the Donkey
PAL.desc: Founded to protect knightly interests within the Empire, the Gesellschaft mit dem Esel has entrenched itself in the lands surrounding Heidelberg. Their expertise in governance, as well as their ability to sponsor tourneys, will improve our cultural standing.

PAP.name: Holy See
PAP.desc: The Holy See is the jurisdiction of the Bishop of Rome, the Pontifex Maximus, head of the Catholic Church, known as The ruler.

PAP.name: French Cardinals
PAP.desc: Since the death of Pap Boniface Viii and the court's relocation to Avignon, most of the cardinals flocking to it are French and under the influence of the ruler of France, whose grip on the Rome will not allow a return to Rome.

PAP.name: Powerful Italian Families
PAP.desc: The anarchy and disobedience in the city of Rome and the other Italian estates greatly increased after the ruler moved the court to Avignon. Now those territories are under the control of powerful Italian families such as the Colonna and Orsini, who are almost completely independent of the ruler.

PAP.name: The Papacy
PAP.desc: A political structure where the nation is governed by a spiritual leader, the Pope, the highest-ranking office of the Catholic Church.

PAP.name: Centralize the States
PAP.desc: The Council of Trent has reformed doctrine and sharpened the institutional boundaries of the Church, but the Papal States themselves remain a patchwork of cities, lordships, and client territories whose local princes have long treated our authority as negotiable. We act now to close that gap, absorbing the revenues, appointments, and legal jurisdictions that local lords have quietly accumulated over generations, and placing them under direct administration from Rome in the manner that the reformed Curia demands. With crown authority consolidated over our territories, the Papacy has the financial and administrative foundation that the Counter-Reformation's ambitions require.

PAP.name: Ecclesiastical Primacy
PAP.desc: The Peace of Westphalia has excluded us from the diplomacy of princes, but it has not settled the question of who speaks for the Catholic Church within each Catholic kingdom, a question now pressed with dangerous urgency by those who would make the Church a department of the crown. We assert our primacy over the bishops of France, Germany, and Austria not as a formality but as a living doctrinal reality, condemning the propositions of Gallicanism and forcing clergy who have drifted toward national loyalties to account for the authority they owe to Rome. This reassertion of the Pope's exclusive right to define doctrine brings wavering churches back under the orthodoxy of the Holy See and restores the flow of tithes and ecclesiastical revenues that national rulers had begun to redirect toward themselves.

PAP.name: Glory of Rome
PAP.desc: The great popes of our age have transformed Roma from a city of medieval ruins into the most magnificent court in Christendom, commissioning artists, architects, and scholars to fill the Vatican with beauty that will outlast any dynasty and draw the eyes of Europe to the Apostolic See. We build on the bones of the ancient empire deliberately, wrapping our spiritual authority in the prestige of classical civilization and ensuring that every ambassador who enters our city understands he is visiting a power with roots older than any kingdom he serves. This investment in permanent magnificence means our prestige does not diminish with the passing of individual popes, because what we have built speaks for itself long after the man who commissioned it is gone.

PAP.name: Head of the Church
PAP.desc: The Bishop of Rome holds a position unlike any other in Christendom: not merely the highest-ranking prelate but the Vicarius Christi, whose pronouncements on matters of faith bind every Catholic ruler and kingdom whether they welcome them or not. We cultivate this authority as much through spiritual relationship as through institutional power, presenting ourselves as the father of all the faithful rather than simply their ecclesiastical superior, which gives rivals pause before they choose open confrontation with the See of Rome. This dual standing as institutional head and spiritual father generates a continuous religious influence across Europe and makes antagonizing us a costly act for any ruler who depends on the loyalty of Catholic subjects.

PAP.name: The Concordat System
PAP.desc: The political earthquakes of revolution and war have stripped away much of our temporal power, yet the fundamental need of states for religious legitimacy has not diminished, and it is precisely this need that we turn to our advantage in the formal treaties we call Concordats. We negotiate with each sovereign power separately, trading some degree of independence in administrative matters for legally binding recognition of Church rights, the security of our seminaries, and the formal standing of Catholic clergy within their borders. This system of bilateral agreements transforms every Catholic state from a potential adversary into a partner bound by treaty, giving us a diplomatic reach that no army could have preserved.

PAP.name: The Word of the Lord
PAP.desc: When the Papacy speaks in matters of faith and governance, it speaks with an authority that no secular ruler can claim: the force of divine mandate expressed through the Bulla Papalis, a formal pronouncement that carries the weight of scripture to every Catholic court in Europe. We reinforce this with a legal tradition that stretches back to the donation of imperial authority itself, giving us not only the prestige of God's representative but the documented right to intervene in worldly affairs, sanction wars, and call the powerful to account before a higher court than any king commands. This standing as both spiritual voice and legal arbiter means that when we recognize a cause as just, allies gather faster and rivals hesitate longer than they would for any purely secular power.

PAP.name: Papal Conclave
PAP.desc: When the Pope dies, the cardinals gather to debate who will be the new Pope. This can be quick, but sometimes it may take several years.

PAR.name: Prosciutto e Parmigiano
PAR.desc: The cured hams and aged wheels of cheese produced in the lowlands around our city have become luxury goods traded across the continent, arriving in courts and counting houses as emblems of the finest the Po plain can offer. We protect and formalize the production of these goods, regulating the standards that make them exceptional and ensuring their export enriches our treasury as much as it delights our customers. This reputation for culinary excellence turns a humble agricultural tradition into a lasting source of commercial and diplomatic prestige.

PAR.name: The Bishop of Parma
PAR.desc: The Bishop of Parma has long wielded an authority that rivals the secular power in this city, guiding its spiritual life through some of the most remarkable religious buildings in northern Italy. We choose to align ourselves with this institution rather than resist it, channeling its influence toward the stability and devotion of our people. This partnership between crown and church strengthens the faith of our subjects and gives our government a source of moral authority that no military force can easily replace.

PAR.name: The Commune of Parma
PAR.desc: Parma's tradition of self-governance runs deep, forged in the era of the Italian communes when the city fought alongside its neighbors to defend their liberties against imperial ambition. We draw on this inheritance to structure the relationship between the crown and our urban communities, offering protections and recognized rights in exchange for the taxes and soldiers that sustain the state. This compact roots our authority in consent as much as in force, making our government a more stable and cooperative partner for all who live under it.

PAR.name: The Enlightened Duchy
PAR.desc: A generation of reformers has convinced our court that the old machinery of government (its privileges, its exemptions, its slow customary procedures) is an obstacle to the welfare of our subjects rather than for their protection. We systematically replace custom with codified law, bringing reason to bear on taxation, education, and the management of public affairs. This commitment to rational governance makes our state more efficient, our laws more predictable, and our subjects more willing to trust that the government works in their interest.

PAR.name: The New Duchy
PAR.desc: The elevation of our city to the capital of an independent realm marks a new chapter for Parma, no longer a possession passed between greater powers, but the seat of a recognized territorial state with its own traditions and ambitions. We move quickly to establish the institutions and ceremonies of sovereignty, giving our subjects a clear identity and our neighbors a clear interlocutor. This consolidation of legitimate authority makes our state harder to absorb and easier to govern.

PAR.name: The Opera Obsession
PAR.desc: Parma will be transformed into a laboratory for theatrical wonder, culminating in the construction of the first permanent proscenium theater. By establishing the picture frame stage, Parma will create a literal and symbolic boundary between the audience and the divine artifice of performance. Our obsession with the scena, integrating complex hydraulics and ingenious pulley systems, will elevate opera from an academic experiment into a supreme spectacle of state power. This architectural breakthrough will turn us into a global magnet for scenographers, setting the technical standard for the modern opera house.

PAT.name: The Church-State of Saint Andrew
PAT.desc: As the spiritual heart of the Frankokratia, Patras has evolved into a sovereign ecclesiastical principality similar to the Prince-Bishoprics of the Holy Roman Empire. The Archbishop wields both the crozier and the sword, ruling his lands through a Synod of Defense that merges religious law with feudal military obligation. This unique status allows us to mobilize the peasantry through religious fervor, viewing every border skirmish as a localized Holy War.

PAT.name: The Patrine Mint
PAT.desc: Patras has secured the right to mint its own coinage, the Patrine Soldo, which is recognized for its stable value across the Aegean. By acting as the central bank for the Frankish Morea, the Archbishop exerts a powerful economic influence over secular lords. We control the pulse of trade through the purity of our silver.

PAT.name: The Pilgrimage Tolls
PAT.desc: The purported relics of Saint Andrew attract thousands of Catholic pilgrims who seek safety in the East, and we have established a network of fortified 'Hospices' to protect them. By charging a modest 'Protection Fee' for passage and lodging, the Archbishopric funds the maintenance of a standing army of Crusader-Monks. These funds are also used to beautify the city, making Patras the 'Rome of the East' and a beacon of Latin architecture.

PAT.name: The Port of Sanctuary
PAT.desc: Our ports have been declared 'Neutral Holy Ports', where merchants of all nations (Catholic, Orthodox, or otherwise) may trade in safety. This sanctuary status has turned our ports into the primary neutral ground for Mediterranean commerce. Even in times of total war, the trade of Patras continues to flow, protected by the Archbishop's ban.

PAT.name: The Seminary of Diplomats
PAT.desc: The Archbishop has established a school to train clergy in the art of international negotiation and secret correspondence. Our 'Black-Robed Diplomats' serve in the courts of Europe as the eyes and ears of the Latin East. Through these letters and whispers, Patras holds an influence over foreign courts that rival kingdoms envy.

PAT.name: Uniate Liturgical Printing
PAT.desc: To counter the influence of the Orthodox world, the Archbishop has established the first Greek-language Catholic printing press in the Peloponnese. We produce Bibles and liturgical texts that use the Greek language but adhere to Latin dogma, slowly winning the 'War of the Word' among the literate Greek classes. This cultural offensive reduces the risk of rebellion and integrates the Greek population into the Latin social hierarchy without stripping them of their linguistic heritage.

PEA.name: Fontana Maggiore
PEA.desc: Before we had painted our greatest canvases or trained our most celebrated condottieri, we had already declared our ambition in water and stone: the Fontana Maggiore, sculpted by Nicola and Giovanni Pisano and fed by a new aqueduct the whole commune funded, rising at the heart of Perugia as proof that no city in central Italy was richer, prouder, or more capable of collective ambition. The fountain gathered every saint, every trade good, and every classical virtue into a single monument and said with marble what no charter could say as well. This civic statement draws pilgrims and merchants to our center and tightens our hold over the streets they fill.

PEA.name: Guerra del Sale
PEA.desc: When the Pope imposed his salt monopoly, our people took up whatever weapons lay to hand; hence the papal mockery that named our uprising the Guerra delle Forche, the War of the Forks. We lost that war and were humiliated (the Baglioni expelled, the Rocca Paolina built directly over their palaces as a stone declaration of contempt) yet the defeat calcified into something more durable than pride. This bone-deep suspicion of outside authority makes every Perugian hill a natural fortress and every invader understand that whatever they take from us will cost more to hold than any strategic advantage can justify.

PEA.name: School of the Perugino
PEA.desc: Pietro Vannucci, the Perugino, built the most admired workshop in Umbria within our walls, and his students fanned across Italy carrying the grace of the Umbrian style wherever commissions took them. Raphael came here to learn at his feet before Rome claimed the greater man, and the city that taught the teacher of Raphael carries an artistic reputation no rival in our region can easily dismiss. This tradition of workshop teaching and intensive apprenticeship makes our city a magnet for painters, patrons, and the steady flow of commissions that follows wherever skilled hands gather.

PEA.name: The Griffin Companies
PEA.desc: Our city's emblem is the Griffin, and nowhere has it been carried further than on the banners of the Baglioni condottieri who sold their swords (and won wars) across the length of the peninsula. Perugia produces soldiers the way Florence produces painters: in quantity, at quality, with an instinct for command honed by centuries of factional street fighting and seasonal raiding. This martial tradition breeds officers who inspire loyalty and soldiers who hold their nerve when less experienced men break.

PEA.name: The Old University
PEA.desc: When revolution swept across Italy, our ancient university responded not by retreating into its medieval privileges but by opening its doors to the sons of merchants and artisans who would carry the new politics forward. The faculty of the Università degli Studi di Perugia produced the lawyers and pamphlet writers who made the Risorgimento possible in Umbria, turning a scholastic institution into an engine of civic transformation. With such a gift for turning learning into organization, no reform our government wishes to pursue will lack educated men who know how to carry it out.

PEA.name: Umbrian Academies
PEA.desc: Long after our political independence was absorbed into the Papal States, the Accademia del Disegno and the learned societies we maintained under papal patronage kept our intellectual and artistic culture alive, training the officials, theorists, and artists who staffed institutions far beyond our own borders. Every great power on the peninsula knew that Perugian training produced reliable men, and the steady demand for our graduates made our academies prosperous even as our influence diminished. This tradition of practical learned culture sharpens every instrument of governance we exercise and ensures our city punches above its political weight in the councils that matter.

PIE.name: The Citadel System
PIE.desc: A generation of engineers trained on the latest Italian treatises on fortification has surveyed every significant town in our domain and begun the work of converting the old circuit walls into a network of modern bastions, angled, low, and wide enough to mount artillery while denying the enemy any approach that our own guns cannot cover. We tie these citadels together by road and signal, so that a garrison threatened in one valley can expect support from the next. This Sistema delle Cittadelle transforms Piedmont into a country that cannot be overrun but must be taken fortress by fortress, a prospect that gives even the most determined aggressor pause before crossing our borders.

PIE.name: The Enlightened Court
PIE.desc: The generation of reformers who have gathered around our court have convinced us that the task of government is not merely to preserve what exists but to discover what works better and systematically replace the old with the new. We open our administration to men trained in the academies and experimental societies of the age, commission reports on everything from agricultural yields to judicial procedure, and fund the education of a class of administrators who can read a budget as readily as a treaty. This Còrt Ëluminà (Corte Illuminata in standard Italian: Enlightened Court) produces a state whose institutions are continuously improved by reason rather than paralyzed by custom, making our government faster, our research more productive, and our subjects more literate.

PIE.name: The Industrial Base
PIE.desc: The combination of water power from our mountain rivers, a growing population of skilled artisans in our cities, and the raw materials of the Alpine foothills has created the conditions for an early industrial transformation that no other region of Italy can yet match. We invest in the hydraulic mills, the standardized workshops, and the credit institutions that allow this productive base to expand systematically rather than grow by accident. This Base Industriale generates income from activities that were once invisible to the treasury and draws workers from the countryside into our towns, building the urban population and the taxable wealth of our state together.

PIE.name: The Piedmontese Cavalry
PIE.desc: The plains of the Po where they open onto our territory have long supported a class of lesser noble horsemen whose wealth depended on the quality of their horses and the reputation of their lance arm. We have organized these scattered men-at-arms into a formal cavalry, standardizing their equipment and training in coordinated maneuver rather than the individual charge that served in an earlier age. This Cavalleria Piemontese can screen our flanks, pursue a broken enemy, and fight in the loose formations that modern battlefield conditions demand, setting our armies free of the pace of infantry.

PIE.name: The Piedmontese Ordinance
PIE.desc: For generations, our mountain lords levied troops on custom and season, calling men to arms when the harvest was done and sending them home before the first snow. We have replaced this improvised tradition with a formal ordinance that fixes the size, equipment, and training standards of our infantry and binds our cities and rural lords to consistent obligations that can be called on at any time. This Ordinansa Piemontèisa (Ordinanza Piemontese in standard Italian: Piedmontese Ordinance) gives our army a professional core that holds its cohesion between campaigns, advancing the discipline and tradition of arms that lesser levies can never maintain.

PIE.name: The Via delle Gallie
PIE.desc: The ancient road descending from the Alpine passes into the Po plain once carried the legions of Rome; it has never ceased to carry merchants, envoys, and armies for whom the Piedmontese corridor is the most direct route between Italy and the north. We invest in the maintenance and security of these roads, building waypoints and toll stations that bring reliable revenue and ensure that goods in transit can move faster through our territory than through any rival route. This control over the Via d'le Gàlie (Via delle Gallie in standard Italian: Road of the Gauls) makes us an indispensable link in the chain of European commerce, enlarging our markets and giving our envoys natural openings at the courts that depend on the roads we manage.

PIS.name: Maritime Republic Legacy
PIS.desc: For three centuries, Pisa stood among the dominant sea powers of the western Mediterranean, its galleys reaching every harbor from Sardinia to the Levant and its naval victories over the Saracens earning the city privileged access to markets that lesser powers could not enter. The defeat at Meloria in 1284 diminished our fleet, but could not erase what those centuries of seaborne commerce built; our captains know these waters, our traders know their counterparts in every port, and the routes that made us great are still routes that we can sail. Our seafaring legacy gives our merchants an edge in the Western trade over any landlocked rival, and the memory of maritime greatness drives us to rebuild what was taken from us.

PIS.name: Pisan Academic Prestige
PIS.desc: Centuries of scholarly excellence have made the name of Pisa synonymous with learning and refined culture among the educated courts of Italy and beyond. Foreign students and wealthy patrons prize a Pisan education as a mark of distinction, and the artistic works produced in this atmosphere of cultured ambition command premium prices from discerning collectors who associate the city with quality. This reputation for scholarship elevates our standing in foreign courts and enriches those who produce and sell the works of art our academic tradition inspires.

PIS.name: Pisan Medical Tradition
PIS.desc: The medical faculty of the University of Pisa is anchored by the Orto Botanico, among the oldest university botanical gardens in the world, where students study the healing properties of plants and develop methods to treat epidemic disease more effectively. Physicians trained in Pisa carry this empirical tradition across the country, improving outcomes for the sick and reducing the toll that plague and pestilence exact on our population. Our commitment to medical learning makes our people hardier and spreads the literacy that comes naturally to those trained in the careful arts of diagnosis and recordkeeping.

PIS.name: Pisan Natural Philosophy
PIS.desc: The scholars of Pisa have pursued understanding through careful observation and measurement rather than received authority alone, building on a long tradition of inquiry in our Studio Pisano that spans mechanics, astronomy, and the natural arts. This empirical habit of mind has shaped not only our philosophers but our engineers and commanders, who approach problems with the same rigor that our scholars apply to the motion of the heavens. Natural philosophy disciplines our military thinking and sharpens the tactical precision of our forces.

PIS.name: The University of Pisa
PIS.desc: Founded in 1343 by imperial charter and rebuilt after each political upheaval that swept through Pisa, our university has trained jurists, physicians, and theologians whose careers carried the Pisan tradition of rigorous scholarship into the courts and churches of Italy and beyond. What distinguishes the Studio Pisano is not merely its age, but also its methods: the faculty has consistently attracted scholars who prefer questions to answers, building a lasting habit of inquiry that produces graduates capable of more than memorizing received doctrine. This tradition of active scholarship shapes the quality of every professional we train, raising the standard of learning across our institutions and ensuring that knowledge remains a living practice rather than a performed ceremony.

PLE.name: Old Viking Towns
PLE.desc: The ancient trading ports founded by the Ostmen are still bustling hives of mercantile activity where the canny can get rich.

PLE.name: Pale Works
PLE.desc: Our boundary is defined by light defensive works of dykes and palisades designed to deter our unruly neighbors from launching their irritating raids.

POL.name: Golden Liberty
POL.desc: The Golden Liberty, also known as Złota Wolność, represents the significant influence and privileges currently held by our Nobility, including the right to elect the ruler and shape national policy. It entailed that all Nobility, regardless of rank, economic status, or ethnic background, were considered equal in power to their peers.

POL.name: Liberum Veto
POL.desc: This introduces the requirement for unanimous voting in the Sejm. Any noble could stop any vote or legislation by standing up and shouting Sisto activitatem! ('I stop the activity!') in Latin, or Nie pozwalam! ('I do not allow!') in Polish.

POL.name: Merchant Seal
POL.desc: A seal bearing the insignia of our central authority, this document permits free, uninterrupted travel for our Burghers, allowing them more expedient passage between cities for themselves and their goods in exchange for a small supplemental tax.

POL.name: Council of Three Lands
POL.desc: A central body of Jewish Authority, this council is in charge of religious and judicial affairs with an aim of spreading religious tolerance and protect its people from persecution.

POL.name: Late Winged Hussars
POL.desc: Dressed in characteristic wings and donning illustrious armor, these cavalrymen are a force to be reckoned with when it comes to their powerful charges, dealing immense damage and shattering the enemy's morale.

POL.name: Winged Hussars
POL.desc: Dressed in characteristic wings and donning illustrious armor, these cavalrymen are a force to be reckoned with when it comes to their powerful charges, dealing immense damage and shattering the enemy's morale.

POL.name: Corona Regni Poloniae
POL.desc: This legislation establishes the kingdom as an indivisible, collective entity, owned not by any single dynasty or monarch but by the entire noble class. Rulers serve the realm, they do not own it. This concept of collectivity is deeply entrenched in our society.
mods: Poland is now referred to as the Crown of Poland

POL.name: Council of Three Lands
POL.desc: Our country has a long-standing history of accepting destitute, persecuted Jewish people. To that end, a council that will look after their needs and advocate for their rights will benefit the stability and spiritual strength of this realm.

POL.name: Folwark System
POL.desc: The Folwark System was a system of production that emphasized creating agricultural surpluses. Peasants were encouraged to work through either the use of rents or through compulsion. This system formed the bedrock of our economy.

POL.name: Granary of Europe
POL.desc: The fertile fields of our domain are home to Europe's richest grain crops, in part thanks to the Folwark System. Through our grace, we supply the markets beyond our borders, ensuring our people continue to prosper and never go hungry.

POL.name: Great Sejm Reforms
POL.desc: If we are to survive and continue to prosper, our governmental mechanism must run efficiently and be based on robust foundations. The parliament shall adopt modernized procedures and strengthen its authority. The goals of this evolution are to curtail the power of the nobility and mitigate the escalating abuses of serfdom.

POL.name: Grosz Krakowski
POL.desc: In an attempt to reform our monetary system, we will introduce a new currency, the Kraków Grosz. Minted from silver, these coins are destined to challenge the power of the Bohemian Prague Groschen and help establish our realm as pioneers of centralized taxation.

POL.name: Kasztelanowie
POL.desc: Castellans represent the voice of the monarch across our domain. They are in charge of gathering taxes and enforcing the rule of law, and may even execute justice in the name of the Crown.

POL.name: Komisja Edukacji Narodowej
POL.desc: Our government's need for capable administrators has led to systematic education reform. We will establish the first education ministry in Europe, devoted to spreading literacy throughout our population, which will hopefully lead to an increase in qualified candidates to staff our expanding administration.

POL.name: Land of Promise
POL.desc: The fertile lands of our domain are a coveted destination for many migrants, primarily those of lower status, seeking a better and more prosperous life.

POL.name: Late Winged Hussars
POL.desc: The evolution of Polish hussars entailed the adoption of heavier armor with red and white colors. They used a longer lance of around six meters, which made their charge incredibly devastating, often breaking the morale of their foes and causing them to rout.

POL.name: Polish Renaissance
POL.desc: Inspired by the ideals of the Italian Renaissance, we are experiencing a cultural golden age. Our literary achievements, architectural splendors, and cultivated atmosphere of religious tolerance have all led to a blossoming of culture across our land.

POL.name: Statute of Kalisz
POL.desc: Known as the General Charter of Jewish Liberties, this legislation contains articles that allow all Jews in our realm the freedom to worship, trade, and travel. The statute also attempts to reduce the number of blood libel accusations against Jews propagated by the Catholic Church.

POL.name: Stone and Brick
POL.desc: For centuries, we have used wood to build our towns and defenses, but we will now systematically upgrade our infrastructure by replacing more vulnerable wooden structures with stronger ones. We have inherited wooden towns, but we shall leave them fortified with stone and brick.

POL.name: Szkoła Rycerska
POL.desc: By establishing the 'Knight's School' to train noble youth in military science and their patriotic duty, we will forge generations of capable, dedicated military and civil personnel.

POL.name: Winged Hussars
POL.desc: The hussars were originally light cavalry troops used for scouting, but with the decline of the old feudal army, we have switched over to professional regiments, the core of which shall be made up of these heavier, armored hussars. The fear of these winged warriors shall make our enemies tremble in the night like children!

POL.name: Wojsko Komputowe
POL.desc: The 'Compute Army' was based around an annual budget calculated and approved by the Sejm. The idea behind this was to provide the Commonwealth with a stable standing army for defense.

POR.name: Casa da Índia
POR.desc: The Casa da Índia oversees all possessions in Africa and India, and controls all the rights to trade there.

POR.name: Estado da Índia
POR.desc: The Estado da Índia is the formal administrative framework through which Portugal governs its far-flung network of trading posts, fortresses, and colonies across Asia. Administered from the viceregal seat of Goa, it coordinates the fleets, garrisons, and revenue of a maritime empire spanning from the Persian Gulf to the South China Sea. By centralizing colonial governance under a single viceregal authority, the Estado allows the Crown to extract revenue and project power far beyond what any private trading venture alone could sustain.

POR.name: Marines
POR.desc: To establish a truly global empire, we must be skilled at launching assaults on enemy forts from the sea.

POR.name: Feitorias
POR.desc: The Feitorias (fortified trading factories established along the African and Asian littorals from the late fifteenth century) combine warehouse, garrison, customs house, and chapel under a single royal Feitor. Beginning with São Jorge da Mina and extending to Sofala, Hormuz, Goa, Malacca, and Macau, the network monopolizes choke points along the spice routes without requiring large inland conquests. Through this model of fortified trading posts Portugal controls a vast share of global commerce with remarkably few occupying troops, sustained by maritime supremacy alone.

POR.name: Monopólio das Especiarias
POR.desc: The Crown claims a monopólio over the pepper, cinnamon, and clove passing through ports, licensing which merchants may carry them and levying its fifth on every cargo that lands. By binding the spice trade to royal charter rather than to whichever captain returns first, the treasury turns the gamble of the sea into a steady and predictable source of revenue.

POR.name: Pursuing the Waves
POR.desc: Under Prince Henry the Navigator, the maritime school at Sagres gathers Genoese pilots, Catalan cartographers, and Portuguese shipwrights to systematize the navigation of the African Atlantic. Gil Eanes rounds Cape Bojador, the caravels reach Sierra Leone, and Bartolomeu Dias clears the Cape of Good Hope, each voyage extending our charts a hundred leagues further south. This sustained royal investment in exploration positions Portugal as the only kingdom in Europe with the patience to wait two generations for an oceanic reward.

POR.name: Restoration of Independence
POR.desc: The realm casts off the long union with Castile and acclaims a native dynasty, opening a generation of war along the Alentejo frontier. New bulwarked fortresses rise, fresh regiments are raised from every parish, and the alliances that guarantee its sovereignty are sealed. This restoration of independence rallies the whole nation behind the legitimate crown as no foreign or formed claimant ever could.

POR.name: Royal Academy of Fortification, Artillery, and Drawing
POR.desc: Queen Maria I establishes the Academia Real de Fortificação, Artilharia e Desenho at the Castle of São Jorge in Lisbon, succeeding the seventeenth-century military classes of Luís Serrão Pimentel. The curriculum unites Vauban-style fortification, Frézier descriptive geometry, and the modern artillery doctrines tested by French and Prussian engineers, taught by Manuel de Sousa Ramos and the royal engineer corps. A unified military academy trains the Portuguese army's officers to a continental European standard, preserving the kingdom's technical credibility through the wars of the coming century.

POR.name: The Battle of Ourique
POR.desc: At the Battle of Ourique in 1139, Count Afonso Henriques defeated a numerically superior Almoravid force in the contested borderlands of the Alentejo. The victory was sanctified by his troops' acclamation as king on the field, the rumored vision of Christ before the battle, and the eventual Manifestis Probatum of 1179 in which Pope Alexander III recognized Portugal as a kingdom. This founding triumph anchors Portuguese royal legitimacy in divine endorsement and battlefield achievement rather than dynastic descent, distinguishing our kingship from the rest of Iberia.

POR.name: Desembargo do Paço
POR.desc: The Desembargo do Paço is the supreme royal council of Portugal, entrusted with reviewing legislation, issuing pardons, and overseeing the judicial appointments that give the Crown its reach into every corner of the realm. Unlike the university-trained lawyers who staff the ordinary courts, the Desembargo draws on men of both legal expertise and royal confidence, combining professional jurisprudence with direct service to the monarch. A well-maintained Desembargo accelerates the administrative cycle and ensures that royal decisions are implemented with legal precision.

POR.name: Establish the Mesa da Consciência e Ordens
POR.desc: Our military orders hold vast commanderies and revenues beyond the reach of ordinary administration, their affairs settled piecemeal by whichever cleric or captain presses hardest for royal favor. Let us erect a standing tribunal — the Mesa da Consciência e Ordens — to examine their petitions, allocate their commanderies, and bind their spiritual authority ever more tightly to the Crown's purpose.

POR.name: Estado da Índia
POR.desc: The Casa da Índia answers for our trade, but our fortresses and factories from India to the South China Sea still answer to no single hand. It has been suggested that Goa be raised into the seat of a formal viceroyalty — an Estado — under which every garrison, fleet, and counting-house east of the Cape reports to one royal authority.

POR.name: Mesa da Consciência e Ordens
POR.desc: The Mesa da Consciência e Ordens was established to regulate the military orders of Portugal — the Order of Christ, the Order of Santiago, and the Order of Aviz — whose lands, revenues, and spiritual authority the Crown administers as Grand Master. The tribunal examines petitions for religious dispensations, manages the allocation of commanderies to royal clients, and arbitrates the interface between canonical law and royal patronage. Its establishment transformed the military orders from autonomous ecclesiastical corporations into instruments of Crown policy, tightly bound to the royal religious agenda.

POR.name: The Cape Route to India
POR.desc: Dispatch a fleet south along the African coast and around the great southern Cape, forging a sea road to the Spice Islands that bypasses every Ottoman toll and Venetian middleman. The route is brutal, two years of open ocean, unknown coasts, and storms that scatter ships, but the first nation to open it will command the spice trade of the world.

PRO.name: Angevin Heraldry
PRO.desc: The golden lilies and double-headed eagles of our banners speak to ancient rights and royal ambitions. Claims that stretch across Italy, reaching as far as Albania and Jerusalem, still echo in our hearts. Let the House of Valois-Anjou rise higher than ever before!

PRO.name: Capetian House of Anjou
PRO.desc: A potent mix of Capetian dignity and Angevin ambition courses through our blood. Though we no longer wear the crown of Jerusalem, we remain heirs to a legacy of kingship that once stretched from Anjou to Albania. With careful diplomacy and planning, we may yet revive the grandeur of our forefathers and claim what was unjustly taken from us.

PRO.name: Le Livre des Tournois
PRO.desc: Penned by royalty, the 'Book of Tournaments' is more than a manual; it is a statement of courtly pride and chivalric identity. Our nobility trains not only for war but for spectacle, and in doing so preserves martial discipline and prestige across the realm.

PRO.name: Lords of the Rhône Corridor
PRO.desc: The Rhône Valley has always been our artery of power, and our castles stand watch over it like sentinels of stone. These fortifications are some of the sturdiest in all of Europe, a steadfast sign of our military and engineering prowess, forever watching over our domain.

PRO.name: Piqûre de Marseille
PRO.desc: Across the workshops of Marseille, artisans stitch delicate boutis quilts in the Provencal style, treasured across Europe for their quality and charm. Much like our duchy, works of art created in our realm are composed of many parts stitched into a unified whole: a quilted land, rich in texture and culture.

PRO.name: Rade of Toulon
PRO.desc: Toulon's natural harbor offers the ideal staging ground for our naval ambitions. While Marseille thrives as our commercial jewel, Toulon shall be the armory of Provence, and the launching point of a future maritime power.

PRO.name: Statutes of Aix
PRO.desc: A series of loosely consolidated laws and statutes form the legal backbone of our governance. These statutes blend Roman jurisprudence with local customs and Angevin tradition, allowing us to manage a patchwork of regions as one cohesive domain: a true composite monarchy, where the parts are diverse, but the crown is indivisible.

PSK.name: Pskov Judicial Charter
PSK.desc: The Pskov Judicial Charter is the Old Russian legal code which was built on the Russkaya Pravda. It emcompasses many important features of the political, social, and economic life within Pskov.

PSS.name: An Army for Bavaria
PSS.desc: Only with a formidable standing army will we have the military might necessary to match our ambitions. With careful focus, we can expand it without having a ruinous impact on our state's finances.

PSS.name: Bavaria Coin
PSS.desc: Our realm needs a new standardized coin to serve as our national unified currency. Establishing a state-owned mint in our capital would ensure our total control over this new coinage.

PSS.name: Bavarian Cultural Institutions
PSS.desc: With our homeland at the feet of the beautiful Alps, we are a destination for artists from all over Europe, who seek inspiration in our incredible landscape. If we were to construct and support the appropriate cultural institutions, we could refine our court into a center of refinement and elegance, one that could rival even the most prestigious powers of Europe.

PSS.name: Bavarian Dukedom
PSS.desc: We have been granted the rulership of Bavaria directly by the Emperor! By embellishing ourselves as the divinely-appointed protectors of Bavaria, we will ensure our legitimacy cannot be questioned.

PSS.name: Bavarian Hofkriegsrat
PSS.desc: Establishing a council with the sole duty of advising our ruler during times of conflict will help us develop a more capable fighting force.

PSS.name: Bavarian Imperial Knights
PSS.desc: Our nobles have distinguished themselves as formidable knights in the service of the Holy Roman Empire. We should nurture and scrupulously maintain these troops to ensure the survival of our ducal integrity.

PSS.name: Bavarian Purity Law
PSS.desc: The excellent quality of our beer has been celebrated for centuries, but for our brews to achieve legendary status, we must ensure their continued prestige and superiority for all time. Several rulers in the past have created regulations and standards for the brewing of this wonderful substance; and we could use this fact as a stamp of our breweries' quality.

PSS.name: Dreams of Unification
PSS.desc: We once were ruled by Bavaria, unified in culture and allied under a single banner. We must ensure that the new Bavarian state is equally mighty, a home worthy of its strong and proud people.

PSS.name: One Faith for Bavaria
PSS.desc: We must ensure our people remain united in their faith, and that they will not be divided by heretical thoughts.

PSS.name: Practical Diplomacy
PSS.desc: No matter if we are answering to an Imperial overlord or cozying up to a potential foreign ally, our diplomats must be prepared for everything. But only if they keep Bavarian interests first and foremost in their efforts will we be able to claim true success in our diplomatic maneuverings.

PSS.name: Skilled Brewers
PSS.desc: Our lands are rich in the crops and fresh water required to brew beer, and our people readily enjoy this abundance. Many small breweries could grow into successful businesses, with the right support.

PSS.name: Trading Hubs of Bavaria
PSS.desc: Our lands are frequently crossed by merchants wishing to trade Salt, Silver, and Livestock in the rich lands to our south. We would be foolish not to take advantage of their presence, and therefore will establish bustling trade hubs in our own lands to attract their business.

RAG.name: The Arsenal Expansion
RAG.desc: Our shipyards have become famous for producing the argosy, massive carracks capable of surviving the Atlantic and the Indian Oceans. By standardizing our shipbuilding techniques and securing high-quality oak from the Bosnian forests, we ensure that the Ragusan merchant marine is the most technologically advanced in the Adriatic. These vessels carry vast cargoes and bristle with guns, allowing our merchants to dominate the spice and silk routes while flying the flag of Saint Blaise in every major port from London to Goa.

RAG.name: The Collegium Ragusinum
RAG.desc: To maintain our status as a center of refinement, we have established the Collegium Ragusinum, a Jesuit-led institution of higher learning that attracts the sons of Balkan and Italian nobility. By producing a class of highly educated diplomats, scientists, and poets, we ensure that Ragusa's leadership is never outmatched in the courtrooms of Europe. This intellectual investment turns our small city into a center of culture, where the fusion of Latin logic and Slavic spirit produces the scholars who will define the cultural awakening of the entire Adriatic littoral.

RAG.name: The Lazzaretto System
RAG.desc: Facing the recurring devastation of the Black Death, Ragusa has pioneered the world's first mandatory maritime quarantine system on the islands of Mrkan and Bobara. By isolating incoming crews and goods for forty days (quaranta), we protect our urban population while maintaining the functionality of our port when other Mediterranean hubs are paralyzed by plague. This scientific approach to public health ensures that the Republic remains a reliable and clean port of call, preserving our manpower and mercantile networks during even the most lethal periods of European history.

RAG.name: The Ragusan Maritime Insurance Code
RAG.desc: We have moved beyond mere shipping to the world of high finance by formalizing one of the first sophisticated systems of maritime insurance. By pooling the risks of our merchant families through the Monte di Pietà, we allow our captains to undertake daring new voyages to the Americas and the Far East with minimal personal risk. This financial innovation ensures that Ragusan capital is always in motion, creating a self-sustaining cycle of wealth that keeps our city wealthy and relevant even as the traditional Mediterranean trade routes begin to fade in importance.

RAG.name: The Ragusan Porto Franco
RAG.desc: As the wars between our neighbors intensify, we have declared our city a strictly neutral Porto Franco (Free Port). By refusing to host foreign warships while offering high-quality repairs and storage to all merchant vessels, we ensure that the conflict only serves to increase our profits. This 'Economic Non-Alignment' makes Ragusa the only safe harbor in a burning sea, allowing us to capture the trade routes that our rivals have abandoned in their pursuit of military glory.

RAG.name: The Statute of 1272
RAG.desc: To reassure the merchants who risk their fortunes in our ports, Ragusa has codified its laws into a comprehensive legal framework that defines property rights and maritime codes. By limiting the power of any single noble and establishing the Consilium Rogatorum, we create an orderly market that attracts the wealthiest traders of the Mediterranean. This legal clarity allows a small city-state to punch far above its weight, turning a rocky outcrop into a sanctuary of Libertas that no feudal lord can easily subvert or ignore.

RAV.name: The Battle of Ravenna
RAV.desc: Ravenna has long been a prize worth fighting for, and the fields outside our walls have witnessed battles of extraordinary ferocity that have made our name synonymous with the hardest kind of fighting in Italy. We harden the walls of the city and steel the soldiery against the shock of pitched battle, drawing on the lessons that only ground stained this often can teach. This martial tradition forges an army that is difficult to break and a city that is difficult to take.

RAV.name: The Byzantine Legacy
RAV.desc: Our city is a living archive of a civilization that has vanished almost everywhere else: the gold leaf apses, the intricate stonework, the iconographic traditions of the Byzantine world survive here in a concentration found nowhere else in the west. Artists and patrons who come to study these works carry their influence outward, raising the reputation of everything produced in our workshops. This custody of a unique heritage turns our past into a source of lasting cultural and commercial value.

RAV.name: The Mosaics of Ravenna
RAV.desc: No city in the Western world preserves the art of the Mosaic as we do; our basilicas and mausoleums are clad in tesserae that glow with gold and deep blue, images that have survived centuries of war and neglect without losing their impact. These works attract scholars, pilgrims, and artists who come to study what the ancient world looked like before it was lost. This tradition of extraordinary craftsmanship deepens our cultural heritage and lends our state a prestige that no contemporary rival can easily replicate.

RAV.name: The New Ravenna
RAV.desc: After generations of stagnation, we invest in our city's renewal, clearing old districts, building new roads and market squares, and offering incentives to artisans and merchants who settle within our walls. The city that results is more open, more prosperous, and more capable of absorbing the growth that comes with a reforming state. This reinvestment in our urban fabric makes Ravenna a place people want to come to rather than one they are merely stuck in.

RAV.name: The Pineda di Classe
RAV.desc: The vast coastal pine forests (the Pinedi) of the Adriatic coast are managed as strategic state assets. Our people have developed a culture of sylviculture and salt, harvesting timber for shipbuilding and managing the vast salt pans of Cervia. By reinforcing these traditions, our people will provide a non-agrarian source of wealth that is immune to crop failure, giving us the liquid capital necessary to face any challenges.

RAV.name: The Ravenna Reclamations
RAV.desc: The marshes and lagoons that surround our city are both our shield and our burden; they protect us from armies but flood our fields and breed disease. We commit to a systematic program of drainage and embankment, digging channels and raising dykes that push back the water and claim new agricultural land from the swamp. This transformation of the wetlands into productive territory feeds our growing population and expands the taxable estate of the state.
