SAL.name: The Alpine Crafts
SAL.desc: The highland villages of our marquisate have long sustained themselves through skilled craftsmanship, producing goods of quality that find their way into the markets of the plains below. The knowledge of our artisans is passed within families and guilds, ensuring that each generation inherits the Alpine Craft Traditions intact. This industry sustains the prosperity of our communities and earns our highland towns a reputation for quality that outlasts any political upheaval.

SAL.name: The Alpine Passages
SAL.desc: The mountain passes that cross through our lands connect the plains of Italy with the highlands beyond, and we have learned to profit from every traveler and merchant who must pass our gates. Control of the Alpine Routes gives us a leverage that no army alone can provide, and we use it to sustain friendships on both sides of the mountains. This geography is our greatest inheritance.

SAL.name: The Alpine Regiments
SAL.desc: Our soldiers have been forged in the hard school of mountain warfare, where endurance and discipline matter more than numbers and where every man knows the value of his comrades. The Highland Regiments of our marquisate have built a reputation for steadiness that makes them sought after even when our state is not at war. This tradition of arms is the shield behind which our people have always stood.

SAL.name: The Alpine Strongholds
SAL.desc: We have fortified the natural strongpoints of our mountains with walls and towers that make our land a nightmare for any invader who seeks to hold it by force. Every valley approach leads to a defended pass, and every pass to a Hilltop Citadel that must be taken before any advance can continue. Any army that enters our lands uninvited will find the mountains themselves arrayed against them.

SAL.name: The Mountain Routes
SAL.desc: The trails and roads that thread through our mountains are known to us as no outsider can know them, and this knowledge shapes how we move and supply our armies. Our soldiers march along paths that would leave foreign troops exhausted and disoriented, arriving fresh where others would arrive worn. This intimate mastery of the Alpine Terrain is a form of strength no fortress can replace.

SAL.name: The Saluzzo Chronicles
SAL.desc: Our court has fostered a distinctive literary tradition that weaves together the languages and voices of both sides of the mountains, producing chronicles and verse of surprising richness. The Occitan and Italian tongues mingle in our writings as they do among our people, creating something that belongs to neither tradition entirely. This chronicle of who we are preserves our identity in letters that outlast stone.

SAO.name: Salona's Stance
SAO.desc: The mountain lords of Salona, perched around the ancient site of Delphi and controlling the strategic passes into central Greece, maintain a fierce independence through a combination of rugged terrain, stout fortifications, and a martial tradition that draws fighting men from across the Frankokratia. Even as larger states collapse, the lords of Salona repeatedly defy their enemies, turning their highland fief into a safe refuge of Latin knighthood in Greece and a persistent irritant to every power that seeks to dominate the region between the Corinthian Gulf and the Spercheios valley.

SAO.name: The Asceticism of the Crissaean Crags
SAO.desc: The soil of Salona is a miserly host, offering little food besides mountain herbs to those who dwell in the shadow of the peaks. Life in this jagged landscape has bred a peasantry and knightly class alike who are famously indifferent to hunger and hardship. Our soldiers require half the rations of a Frankish man-at-arms, possessing a lean, wolf-like endurance that allows them to out-march and out-climb any adversary. In the high passes of Phocis, the belly is light, but the resolve is as unyielding as the mountain itself.

SAO.name: The Legacy of the Alpha Protector
SAO.desc: The 'Wolf-Pacts' have reached their logical conclusion: the Hegemony is the recognized 'Alpha' of the Eastern Mediterranean. We no longer justify aggression. We simply exercise our natural mandate to 'police' the Levant. This projection of power ensures that the Greek seas remain a private lake for the merchants of Salona.

SAO.name: The Parnassian Wolf-Pacts
SAO.desc: In the shifting power dynamics, Salona has moved beyond simple feudal oaths to a predatory legal doctrine known as the 'Wolf-Pacts'. By legally defining our neighbors as 'client-prey' that require Salona's 'alpha' protection to survive, we create a permanent diplomatic justification for intervention and annexation. This predatory diplomacy allows us to absorb smaller lordships and border fiefs under the guise of 'Defensive Consolidation', ensuring that the Latin presence in the Balkans is led by a single, sharp-toothed power rather than a scattered, vulnerable pack.

SAO.name: The Parnassus Mines
SAO.desc: Deep within the rugged mountains of our lordship lie veins of metals that have been forgotten since the days of the Delphic Oracle. By bringing in Saxon mining experts and applying Western smelting technology, we have turned the Mount of the Muses into a center of heavy industry. The wealth extracted from these mines allows the Lords of Salona to maintain a court that rivals the Dukes of Athens in elegance and power.

SAO.name: The Phocian Mule-Chancery
SAO.desc: Wheeled transport is pretty much impossible in most of our domain; thus, we have established a state-run Chancery to nationalize the logistics of the mountains. This allows us to move supply trains at a pace that leaves conventional imperial armies starving in the crags.

SAV.name: A Light in the Darkness
SAV.desc: We have embraced the teachings of the Waldensian movement and are dedicated to protecting this faith from the vicious Catholic Church, which seeks to eradicate its ideas.

SAV.name: A Unified House
SAV.desc: Savoy has been ruled by a stable line of dynastic counts ever since its creation. By ensuring the unity of our ruling family and maintaining a strong connection to local representatives, we keep our land from being fractured.

SAV.name: Control Over the Passes
SAV.desc: The passage over the Alps is troublesome at the best of times, and can be outright impossible with carriages or a larger entourage. By maintaining good pathways, shelters, and waystations, we will be able to dominate the difficult terrain and ensure a steady exchange of merchants throughout our territory.

SAV.name: Holy Shroud Pilgrimage
SAV.desc: Our realm is in the possession of a most holy artifact, a piece of cloth that bears the face of Jesus of Nazareth. Naturally, it has attracted numerous pilgrims, all clamoring to see and venerate this extraordinary relic. This constant stream of pilgrimage brings a great deal of wealth into our territory, which is all very much to our advantage.

SAV.name: Populate Alpine Valleys
SAV.desc: Many people in our realm leave the alpine valleys they were born into to settle in the urban areas on either side of the mountain range. This depopulation leaves the small villages of lesser valleys in a precarious, politically unstable position. We must ensure that the valley lands are sufficiently populated and can be adequately maintained.

SAV.name: Savoyard Alpine Identity
SAV.desc: Nestled in the high Alps, We are a mountain people before we anything. Their therrain and the passes crossing them are our inheritance, our livelihood, and the mountains themselves are our protectors. Generations of living inside the Alps have given our people an unmatched understanding of their heights and geography.

SAV.name: Stand against Heresy
SAV.desc: Our lands have long suffered under the heretical preaching of the Waldensians. By the force of our will and with the support of the divine, we have been able to contain their influence, and we shall continue to defend the one true faith from these dangerous ideas.

SBL.name: Shires of Scotland
SBL.desc: Introduced by Sco Malcolm Iii, the shire system divides Scotland into administrative counties, with each shire having its own structure.

SBL.name: Royal Burgh Commissioners
SBL.desc: The Royal Burgh Commissioners, representing the Crown-chartered burghs of Scotland, convene regularly to safeguard their privileges, regulate commerce, and advise the nation's ruler. Through their collective authority in the Convention of Royal Burghs, they ensure that Scotland's trading communities remain vital to governance, economy, and law, standing as a counterweight to the power of the Nobility and Clergy.

SBL.name: Distribution of Clan Holdings
SBL.desc: The inheritance of holdings is divided proportional to clan influence, with larger clans recieving more holdings. Clan holdings are passed directly to the heir, unless a title is revoked or goes extinct.

SBL.name: Direct Inheritance
SBL.desc: Holdings and titles are retained within a clan, only reverting back to the ruler when a clan lineage goes extinct.

SBL.name: Distributed by the Ruler
SBL.desc: Newly established holdings and titles are assigned by the ruler's preference. Larger clans are typically favored as allies by the ruler and receive the lionshare of new titles.

SBL.name: Dynastic Holdings
SBL.desc: New holdings and titles default to the ruling dynasty, only rarely being given by them to other clans.

SCO.desc: Introduced by Sco Malcolm Iii, the shire system divides Scotland into administrative counties, with each shire having its own structure.

SCO.name: Act of Revocation
SCO.desc: It has long been the custom to gift parts of the Royal Domain to our nobility as a reward for their services, but this system cannot be sustained if we want to ensure the integrity of our domain. From now on, we will insist on renting these lands instead of outright giving them away.

SCO.name: Assert the Royal Revenue
SCO.desc: If Scotland is to continue its independent existence, we must secure stable sources of income. By tightening our control over the obligations owed to us by royal estates and feudal properties, we can increase our rightfully received taxes. Through these methods, we can ensure the Crown has sufficient funds to enact their will without relying on other sources of money.

SCO.name: English Administrators
SCO.desc: Securing peace with our southern neighbor has led to a steady influx of English aristocrats entering our administration. This makes it possible to exert our control over our country more effectively.

SCO.name: Royal Scots Navy
SCO.desc: Since the Wars of Independence, we have been looking at reinforcing and updating our navy. Previously, we had used feudal obligations to bulk out our fleets with crew and ships, but we will now create a modern fleet, owned by the King and based in our port of Newhaven.

SCO.name: Tenacious Land
SCO.desc: War can be a long and tiring affair. If we are to defend our independence, we need to be prepared to endure hard times. Luckily, our people are as tenacious as the land they call their home, and resist foreign invaders to their last breaths.

SER.name: Baština Grants
SER.desc: The system of land grants for our elites is inspired by the Byzantine system of Pronoias. It grants them a grand array of privileges and obligations on behalf of their domains when it comes to administering the lands leased to them by the government.

SER.name: Gradozidanije and Gradobljudenije
SER.desc: Our domain is home to many fortifications and formidable strongholds. The maintenance expenses and garrisoning of these emplacements have been entrusted to the local population and townspeople.

SER.name: Krajiška Vlastela
SER.desc: Our borderlands must be safely guarded at all times. To that end, the system of krajine splits our frontiers into well-administered districts under the command of local lords, known as Krajiška Vlastela, who are in charge of maintaining and protecting the people of their provinces.

SER.name: Župa Districts
SER.desc: The compartmentalization and division of our society is detailed in the various legal frameworks that surround our administrative branch. The most important aspect of our society and bureaucracy is the division of our provinces into Župa districts, aimed at improving how local affairs are handled.

SER.name: Novo Brdo Code
SER.desc: The Novo Brdo Code provides detailed guidelines on property rights, safety measures, and economic practices, significantly influencing the development and prosperity of our mining communities.

SER.name: Zamanička Vojska
SER.desc: Meaning 'All Together', this system of universal military obligation demands that all able-bodied citizens, regardless of age or gender, are expected to defend the homeland when threatened. Unlike professional armies or feudal levies, this mobilizes the entire population to protect their independence, reflecting a communal commitment to defending their nation.

SER.name: Foreign Relations Bureau
SER.desc: Our realm has recognized the importance of fostering friendly relations and alliances with neighboring countries. To facilitate this, we will establish a specialized bureau dedicated to foreign affairs. By maintaining a dedicated focus on diplomacy, we are better positioned to navigate the complex web of international relations and secure our nation's prosperity.

SER.name: Keepers of the Gate
SER.desc: Serbia's rugged terrain has birthed a formidable network of defenses, epitomized by the imposing Smederevo Fortress. These enduring fortifications safeguard our nation, making invasion a daunting prospect. From the sprawling mountain ranges to the strategic river valleys, Serbia's defenses stand as a testament to our resilience and indomitable spirit.

SER.name: Military Modernization
SER.desc: Our people remember the birth of our nation: surrounded by formidable powers that pose permanent, looming threats to our security. This enduring vigilance has forged a culture of unwavering readiness, ensuring our armed forces stand as a shield against adversity. Fearless and respected, our soldiers have transformed us from potential prey to a mighty adversary, deterring any who dare encroach upon our sovereignty.

SER.name: Mimicking the Phoenix
SER.desc: We eagerly embrace the ways of Byzantium, aiming to mirror their laws and overall style. Drawing from the rich tapestry of Roman influences, we strive to infuse our governance and legal system with their essence, in a conscious effort to emulate the grace and sophistication of Byzantium within our realm.

SER.name: Rallying the Troops
SER.desc: Our realm has developed various methods for swiftly amassing troops, so no enemy can catch us unprepared. This edge has helped us stand tall, despite all odds being against us, and we are prepared for battle. United, we march forward, resolute in purpose and ready to defend our honor and homeland!

SER.name: Serbian National Militia
SER.desc: Drawing from the hard-won experience of our veteran units of the previous decades, we have established a permanent, professional standing National Militia. This force represents a decisive move away from the disorganized peasant levy, utilizing rigorous Western drill, uniform equipment, and a modernized chain of command while retaining the fierce, high-morale fighting style of our Balkan predecessors. This ensures that our independence is not a fragile diplomatic gift, but is instead backed by a credible, modern military machine that can defend our borders against any encroaching imperial power.

SER.name: The Morava Trade Guilds
SER.desc: We will issue royal charters to the guilds of the Morava Valley, and encourage the development of large-scale leather working, weaving, and metal finishing workshops along the river's transit points. By exempting these guilds from certain internal tolls in exchange for providing standardized equipment to the royal armies (such as saddlery for the cavalry and uniforms for the infantry) the state will create a self-sustaining domestic industry. This move will reduce the realm's dependence on expensive foreign imports from outside and create a prosperous, urban middle class that serves as a loyal counter-weight to the rural power of the nobility, significantly broadening the state's taxable economic base.

SER.name: The Rebirth of the Patriarchate
SER.desc: Through incredible savvy and political maneuvering within the complex imperial administrative systems of our neighbors, we have successfully negotiated the restoration of our national Patriarchate. This diplomatic victory grants us spiritual and legal jurisdiction over all Serbian populations stretching from the Adriatic coast to the middle Danube, effectively allowing the Church to act as a 'Guardian of all Serbs'. It enables the maintenance of a shadow administration that collects tithes, manages local education, and keeps the flame of our traditions alive among a population that remains unified by a single, powerful faith.

SER.name: The Saxon Mining Privileges
SER.desc: The deliberate invitation of Sasi miners from Upper Saxony and the Harz Mountains has fundamentally transformed our primitive surface pits into sophisticated industrial engines. By granting these Germanic experts their own autonomous courts, the right to follow their own mining codes, and religious freedom, we have successfully unlocked the vast, deep-seated silver and gold veins of Brskovo and Novo Brdo. This influx of technical expertise provide us with the immense quantities of hard bullion necessary to hire the finest Western mercenaries, build monumental stone endowments, and mint the high-quality silver Matapan imitations that have come to dominate Balkan trade and Mediterranean commerce.

SER.name: The Transcribers of Resava
SER.desc: In an era of conflict, the Serbian people turns to the pen to preserve what the sword can not. The Resava School of orthography will standardize the Serbian-Slavonic language, creating a cultural 'republic of letters'. This obsession with linguistic purity and the preservation of chronicles will ensure that our history is never lost to the fog of war. It creates a highly literate elite who acts as the memory of the nation, keeping the records of our dynasties alive in every monastery scriptorium from the Danube to the Adriatic.

SER.name: The Šumadija Agrarian Revolution
SER.desc: The Serbian peasantry has led its own cultural and economic revolution by adopting agrarian techniques learned from the West. This has turned the dense forests of Šumadija into a highly productive agricultural heartland. This surplus of food does not just feed the people; it fuels a demographic explosion. A well-fed Serbian population is a growing and ambitious one, providing a massive pool of young, healthy recruits for the army and a robust internal market that makes Serbia the dominant economic engine of the Central Balkans.

SER.name: Viteštvo
SER.desc: We will encourage Viteštvo, a unique Serbian chivalric code, that will blend the heavy-armored traditions of the West with the stoic warrior ethos of the East. This culture of knighthood will not be restricted to the highest nobility but trickle down into the lower classes of free soldiers. It will emphasize personal bravery, loyalty to the True Faith, and a specialized mastery of both the lance and the saber. This military culture will produce a population that is naturally predisposed to warfare, viewing military service as the highest form of social and spiritual achievement.

SIC.name: Constitutions of Melfi
SIC.desc: Emperor Frederick II, the Hohenstaufen King of Sicily, drafted a legal code for Sicily known as the Constitutions of Melfi, or Liber Augustalis. Still in use centuries later, it represents a solid foundation for the governance of our state, regulating public law, judicial procedure, and feudal, private, and penal law.

SIC.name: Licentia Populandi
SIC.desc: To increase harvests and tax revenue, the state granted Licenses to Populate to the nobility. This will allow lords to build brand-new towns in the desolate interior of the island, attracting peasants with promises of land and lower taxes. This internal colonization effort will transform the Sicilian landscape, turning wild hinterlands into a patchwork of profitable agricultural communities.

SIC.name: Sicilian Baroque
SIC.desc: Our island trembles often, causing many buildings to collapse. In order to replace these old structures, the state will orchestrate one of the most ambitious rebuilding programs in human history. Rather than simply repairing old ruins, the government will redesign entire cities using the theatrical, earthquake-resistant Sicilian Baroque style. This will demonstrate the state's incredible ability to mobilize labor and capital in the face of total disaster.

SIC.name: Studium Generale
SIC.desc: Founded by King Alfonso V of Aragon, the University of Catania was the oldest in Sicily and one of the few southern institutions granted full Studium Generale status. Unique for its royal charter and blend of scholastic and legal education, it produced jurists, theologians, and scientists who served both Church and Crown in a culturally diverse region.

SIC.name: The Court of the Royal Patrimony
SIC.desc: We will create this specialized court to manage the royal properties and the Secretias (customs offices). By professionalizing the collection of export duties on silk, tuna, and grain, the state will significantly reduce corruption and 'leakage' to local barons. This administrative rigor will turn our lands into the Crown's most reliable source of income, funding our wars across Italy and the Mediterranean.

SIC.name: The Marsala Wine Industry
SIC.desc: Thanks to foreign investors, Sicilian wine will be transformed from a local peasant drink into a fortified luxury good that can survive long sea voyages. The culture of the 'Vineyard Estate' (the Baglio) will be the new symbol of Sicilian wealth and sophistication. It links the island's ancient agricultural traditions to the modern, industrial world of global commerce.

SIE.name: Monte dei Paschi
SIE.desc: Our magistrates have established the Monte dei Paschi (a public lending institution secured against the revenues of the Maremma pastures) to provide affordable credit to merchants and the poor alike and to give Siena a stable foundation for commerce in an era of expanding trade. This innovation in public finance became a model of banking stability that outlasted empires, sustaining our commercial life through crises that bankrupted more reckless rivals. This institution accelerates the adoption of new economic practices across our lands while generating the steady fiscal revenue that a city of ambition requires.

SIE.name: Santa Caterina's Legacy
SIE.desc: Caterina di Giacomo di Benincasa (mystic, theologian, and doctor of the faith) remains the most celebrated soul that Siena has ever produced, and in the age of religious upheaval that followed the great disputes of the era her memory became a rallying point for a confident, devotional faith that answered challenge with piety rather than polemic. Sienese scholars and preachers placed themselves at the forefront of this spiritual renewal, drawing on the saint's writings to argue that reform must begin in the heart before it reaches the law. This legacy of sanctity and conviction deepens the faith of our people and draws together communities that might otherwise fracture under the pressures of religious conflict.

SIE.name: Sienese Civic Pride
SIE.desc: Even as the grand ambitions of the Sienese republic gave way to foreign pressure and Tuscan consolidation, the citizens of Siena maintained a fierce pride in their distinct identity (their dialect, their art, their tradition of communal self-governance) that made the city difficult to absorb without provocation. Those who sought to antagonize or diminish Siena found its people stubborn in their resistance, bound together by centuries of shared memory and an insistence that Sienese life meant something worth defending. This deep-rooted civic spirit discourages aggression against us and sustains the prosperity that flows from a population genuinely invested in the wellbeing of the city they call home.

SIE.name: Sienese School of Painting
SIE.desc: The art of painting has flourished in Italy since the beginning of the Renaissance, but no artists can match the elegance of those trained in Siena, where the Studium Senese, one of the oldest universities in Europe, ensures that painters and scholars alike are nurtured by the same tradition of civic patronage. Sienese art is otherworldly and refined, with a heavy focus on the miracles performed by Biblical figures and Saints. This unity of learning and artistry defines the Sienese school, securing its reputation for centuries to come.

SIE.name: The Council of Priori
SIE.desc: The Nine Priors of our republic, drawn exclusively from the merchant guilds of Siena and barred to the high nobility whose factional rivalries brought every previous government to ruin, have shaped the city's governance with an administrative diligence that our more aristocratic neighbors cannot match. Their terms are brief and their accountability public, making sustained corruption harder to conceal and factional manipulation harder to dress in the language of civic virtue. Merchant governance lends our institutions a practical competence and a legitimacy grounded in commerce and consent rather than an accident of birth.

SIE.name: The Palio of Siena
SIE.desc: Twice each year the contrade of Siena compete in the Palio: a bareback horse race around the Piazza del Campo that is as much a civic ritual as a contest, binding the neighborhoods of the city in a shared drama of rivalry, identity, and fierce communal pride. The elaborate pageantry of the event draws visitors from across Italy and broadcasts Sienese cultural vitality to all who witness it, reinforcing our reputation as a city that has not forgotten how to celebrate itself. This enduring tradition amplifies our influence across the region and wins us the admiration of courts that see in Siena a living testament to the power of civic culture.

SLZ.name: An Army for Bavaria
SLZ.desc: Only with a formidable standing army will we have the military might necessary to match our ambitions. With careful focus, we can expand it without having a ruinous impact on our state's finances.

SLZ.name: Bavaria Coin
SLZ.desc: Our realm needs a new standardized coin to serve as our national unified currency. Establishing a state-owned mint in our capital would ensure our total control over this new coinage.

SLZ.name: Bavarian Cultural Institutions
SLZ.desc: With our homeland at the feet of the beautiful Alps, we are a destination for artists from all over Europe, who seek inspiration in our incredible landscape. If we were to construct and support the appropriate cultural institutions, we could refine our court into a center of refinement and elegance, one that could rival even the most prestigious powers of Europe.

SLZ.name: Bavarian Dukedom
SLZ.desc: We have been granted the rulership of Bavaria directly by the Emperor! By embellishing ourselves as the divinely-appointed protectors of Bavaria, we will ensure our legitimacy cannot be questioned.

SLZ.name: Bavarian Hofkriegsrat
SLZ.desc: Establishing a council with the sole duty of advising our ruler during times of conflict will help us develop a more capable fighting force.

SLZ.name: Bavarian Imperial Knights
SLZ.desc: Our nobles have distinguished themselves as formidable knights in the service of the Holy Roman Empire. We should nurture and scrupulously maintain these troops to ensure the survival of our ducal integrity.

SLZ.name: Bavarian Purity Law
SLZ.desc: The excellent quality of our beer has been celebrated for centuries, but for our brews to achieve legendary status, we must ensure their continued prestige and superiority for all time. Several rulers in the past have created regulations and standards for the brewing of this wonderful substance; and we could use this fact as a stamp of our breweries' quality.

SLZ.name: Dreams of Unification
SLZ.desc: We once were ruled by Bavaria, unified in culture and allied under a single banner. We must ensure that the new Bavarian state is equally mighty, a home worthy of its strong and proud people.

SLZ.name: One Faith for Bavaria
SLZ.desc: We must ensure our people remain united in their faith, and that they will not be divided by heretical thoughts.

SLZ.name: Practical Diplomacy
SLZ.desc: No matter if we are answering to an Imperial overlord or cozying up to a potential foreign ally, our diplomats must be prepared for everything. But only if they keep Bavarian interests first and foremost in their efforts will we be able to claim true success in our diplomatic maneuverings.

SLZ.name: Skilled Brewers
SLZ.desc: Our lands are rich in the crops and fresh water required to brew beer, and our people readily enjoy this abundance. Many small breweries could grow into successful businesses, with the right support.

SLZ.name: Trading Hubs of Bavaria
SLZ.desc: Our lands are frequently crossed by merchants wishing to trade Salt, Silver, and Livestock in the rich lands to our south. We would be foolish not to take advantage of their presence, and therefore will establish bustling trade hubs in our own lands to attract their business.

SME.name: A Sacred Land
SME.desc: The lands of Samtskhe are home to places both sacred and revered among the Georgian people. The cave monastery of Vardzia, the ancient church of Atskuri with its miraculous icon of the Virgin Mary, and the Monastery of Ancha with its Anchiskhati icon, are some of the most significant holy places in our realm. By protecting and curating the Samtskhe church, setting it apart as distinct from that of Georgia, we ensure that our people stand united even in the face of adversity.

SME.name: Atabegs of Samtskhe
SME.desc: We are not just one part of the Kingdom of Georgia, as a long time ago we received royal recognition and, with it, the title of Atabeg. This title had previously been granted only to the Armenian vassals, and therefore its conveyance is a sign of distinction and of the respect that the Georgian monarch has for us.

SME.name: Bridge Between Worlds
SME.desc: Our country has always served as a bridge between the Christian and Muslim worlds. As such, people of both faiths within our borders have become accustomed to interacting with each other.

SME.name: Fortresses of Samtskhe
SME.desc: Our mountainous terrain has acted as a shield against foreign invaders many times. Because of this, we learned to build strong fortresses and to always be prepared for defensive warfare. This legacy of strength and readiness is one we must strive at all costs to uphold — the fortresses of Samtskhe must be perpetually well maintained, manned, and supplied, as foreign invaders are not a possibility but a certainty.

SME.name: Frontier Warriors
SME.desc: The Caucasus have been shaped by nomadic emperors since time immemorial, but the lush pastures of Samtskhe have convinced many tribesmen to settle. We must not let this affect the stability of our kingdom, but instead make arrangements with these settling tribes so that they contribute to our military ambitions in exchange for the lands they claim.

SME.name: Independent Ambitions
SME.desc: Samtskhe has often been obligated to bow to foreign rulers, be they Muslim or Christian; Georgian, Turkic, or Iranian. To build an enduring state that survives as an independent entity and can stand against covetous outsiders, we must establish independent institutions: issuing our own coinage, creating our own laws, and patronizing our own theologians and writers.

SME.name: Jaqeli Dynasty
SME.desc: Despite its humble origins, the Jaqeli dynasty has been able to establish many successful relationships, forging strong ties to the rulers of surrounding states. As such, we have a positive reputation in the diplomatic sphere.

SME.name: Proactive Diplomacy
SME.desc: While still a part of Georgia, Samtskhe operates with substantial independence. This privileged position requires constant diplomatic awareness and a policy of active diplomacy, ensuring that we always have a direct channel to those in power. We do all this while actively engaging in our internal politics, meddling with the succession and forging dynastic alliances as best benefits us. The survival of our relatively small state depends on upholding these diplomatic traditions. Let it never be said that we have done too little or acted without sufficient wisdom!

SME.name: Protect the Trade Routes
SME.desc: Our position at the crossroads of Georgia, Anatolia, Armenia, and Āzarbāijān also means that a great number of traders seek to cross our lands. However, the constant threat of being raided by nomadic tribesmen means that some have come to doubt the safety of traveling on our roads. We must properly defend all roads and merchant inns in our nation so that trade revenue can flow into our state treasury unhindered.

SMO.name: Diocese of Smolensk
SMO.desc: Once a spiritual stronghold of Orthodox Christianity and home to one of the oldest bishoprics in the region, the Diocese of Smolensk embodies our people's unshakable faith.

SMO.name: Hub of Militarism
SMO.desc: Long has war defined our fate, but now it shall define our strength. From the ruinous embrace of warfare and siege, Smolensk rises as a center of military production — cannons, firearms, powder and doctrine flow outward from our armories. Let the world see us not as a prize to be taken, but as a hammer to be feared, ready to strike the anvil of foreign conquerors.

SMO.name: Link the Steppes Trade
SMO.desc: Positioned between forest and steppe, Smolensk has long been a crossroads of war and commerce. By improving overland infrastructure and securing the arteries of caravan travel, we can reforge our role as the vital hinge between northern Rus', the Baltic, and the southern trade routes of the steppes.

SMO.name: Smolenskian Resolve
SMO.desc: For centuries, Smolensk has been a land carved up by outsiders — Lithuanian dukes, Polish kings, and Muscovite princes. To survive, we clung to what united us: our faith and our fortitude. If we are ever to rise again, we must cast off divisions and rally around the sacred idea that, above all, there is only Smolensk.

SMO.name: The Armories of Smolensk
SMO.desc: After decades of warfare on every border, we learned to fight with weapons of both east and west. Blending Muscovite grit with western precision, our armories now produce elite artillery and tactics unmatched by our rivals. From our forges comes firepower — and from firepower, domination and perseverance.

SON.name: Gold to Salt Trade
SON.desc: Some say that Salt is worth its weight in Gold... perhaps it would be more accurate to say that Gold is worth its weight in Salt. Either way, by exchanging these two commodities, we have established thriving trade networks.

SON.name: Independence from Mali
SON.desc: For many years, we were a subject of Mali. As Mali's power has weakened, ours has grown, and we can now claim to be fully independent of Malian overlordship. Let us take steps to make sure we remain so.

SON.name: Jihād Against the Pagans
SON.desc: Despite the best efforts of centuries of Sunni sultanates, Western Africa is still plagued by the menace of Animistic pagans. By lifting the banner of Jihād, we can cleanse our lands of the unbelievers and expand our frontiers at the same time.

SON.name: Malian Military Tactics
SON.desc: During our time as subjects of Mali, our people learned much from their military command and combat tactics. This knowledge shall help our own infantry in battles to come.

SON.name: Modernization of the Military
SON.desc: Our state lives and dies by the capabilities of our army. Our military not only ensures our survival, but is also what has set us on the path to greatness. We cannot allow ourselves to fall behind in progress!

SON.name: Sankoré Madrasah
SON.desc: We have been told that the Sankoré Mosque's school is the greatest center for learning in the entirety of Africa. Who could be surprised if this were true, given how many wise men from distant Arabia and the Maghreb are here right now, arguing the finer points of philosophy and religion?

SON.name: Sharī'ah
SON.desc: The Holy Law that the Prophet followed when ruling Madīna should be the unshakable foundation of the laws we use to run our society. By reforming our criminal code to reflect the teachings of the Prophet, we will bring harmony and justice to our people.

SON.name: Stories of the Gao Empire
SON.desc: Before the Malian Empire came to dominate Western Africa, the city of Gao was the capital of an empire in its own right. Although there are barely any written records of the Gao Empire, its legacy lives on in our oral traditions, inspiring all who want to achieve greatness one day.

SON.name: The Ḥajj
SON.desc: Like Mansa Mūsā of Mali once did, our rulers can travel to Mecca on pilgrimage, fulfilling the fifth pillar of Islam and bearing gold as a symbol of our wealth and power. Like the Malian pilgrims of old, the world will gasp in wonder at the wealth and grandeur of Songhai.
mods: Improves Dīwān al-Ḥajj bureaucracy positive effect by 50%

SON.name: Trans-Sahara Trade
SON.desc: Our traders frequently bring back fascinating things from the courts of North Africa. Perhaps they could find and bring back yet more fascinating trinkets?

SUK.name: Akson Sukhothai
SUK.desc: Although the Thai script is already common to all Thai people, it should not be forgotten that it was in our country and under our guidance that it was developed. As such, Thai script is not only a unifying force for our culture, but also proof of our individuality and distinctiveness.

SUK.name: Birthplace of a Culture
SUK.desc: We are called the first independent Thai kingdom, as we were the first ones to rebel against Khmer authority and establish ourselves as free from their influence. As such, all Thai people look at us in admiration.

SUK.name: Breaker of Chains
SUK.desc: It was not so long ago that we saw ourselves under the Khmer authority, but we have since gained our freedom, and have taken our rightful place as an independent power. We have earned the admiration of our peers, and their respect.

SUK.name: Military History
SUK.desc: Our armies have a long history of victory in combat. As a result, a position in our military is seen as a post of honor and prestige, and there are many willing to serve.

SUK.name: Ram Khamhaeng Stele
SUK.desc: Most of the history of the early Sukhothai kingdom comes from inscriptions on the Ram Khamhaeng Stele, commissioned by the great king to give a record of his glorious reign. The Ram Khamhaeng Stele is a sacred piece of heritage and one that surely proves our place in history.

SUK.name: Sukhothai Ceramics
SUK.desc: Ceramics have been created by the Thai people since antiquity, influenced by Chinese ceramics but always retaining their own distinct style. However, the ceramics produced in our country are most valued, and they are often traded at great distances overseas.

SUK.name: Unstoppable Army
SUK.desc: Many have tried in the past to stop our progress and expansion, but all have failed in the face of our army. It has proved to be an unstoppable force, one that readily crushes any obstacles in our way.

SUK.name: Wat Si Sawai
SUK.desc: We are known for our many gorgeous temples, such as the Wat Si Sawai, one of the oldest in Sukhothai. Built under the Khmer authority as a Hindu temple, its ensuing repurposing has turned it into a symbol of our identity. The faith of our people is strong.

SUN.name: Extend the Kampung-Kampung
SUN.desc: The foundation of Sundanese society lies in every kampung, rural communities that dot the landscape. Investing in the infrastructure of these villages ensures sustainable growth, strong local leadership, and resilience against both famine and invasion.

SUN.name: Pan-Asian Trade
SUN.desc: Sunda lies at the crossroads of great empires: India, China, and the Islamic world. By positioning ourselves as an indispensable node in this network, we secure access to goods, ideas, and partners across Asia turning our harbors into gateways of prosperity.

SUN.name: Pepper of the Parahyangan
SUN.desc: The fertile volcanic soil of the Sundanese highlands is perfect for growing the prized spice, black pepper. Traders from across the world seek our peppercorns for their potency and aroma. We must capitalize on this natural treasure to expand our influence through spice.

SUN.name: Sérén Taun
SUN.desc: Held after the harvest, the Sérén Taun festival is an annual thanksgiving ceremony celebrating agricultural abundance. Marked by rituals, offerings, and music, it strengthens the communal bonds of our kampung-kampung and reminds all of the sacred balance between people, rice, and nature.

SWE.name: Alsnö Stadga
SWE.desc: This set of rules was set up by Swe Magnus Ladulas in 1280 at Alsnö Hus to regulate and formalize the benefits of the Nobility, while also protecting the Peasants from their exploits. This is why he was nicknamed 'Ladulås', or 'Barn-Lock' in English by the commoners.

SWE.name: Frihetstiden
SWE.desc: We have entered an Age of Liberty, in which the Crown shall no longer hold absolute sway! The government of Sweden is now in the hands of the estates, and the monarch may do nothing without first gaining our approval.

SWE.name: Land-Owning Peasants
SWE.desc: peasants hold a uniquely strong position compared to their peers in much of feudal Europe. They own their land outright, pay taxes directly to the crown, and often have a voice in local assemblies, giving them a degree of autonomy and legal protection. These farmers were not serfs; many are armed and serve in levies. Their rights are rooted in ancient customary law, and their relative independence is a foundational element of Swedish rural society.

SWE.name: Swedish Copper Coins
SWE.desc: The abundance of copper in Sweden, primarily from the Stora Kopparberget mine in Falun, has prompted the country to use it as the main metal for minting a new national currency, the daler. This is issued as a large money plate, called plåtmynt, which can weigh up to 20 kilograms. Some argue that this might not be very practical and that the volume of money in circulation could exceed copper reserves, but they seem narrow-minded.

SWE.name: Caroleans
SWE.desc: The Caroleans are the Swedish and Finnish infantry of the Swedish Empire. Recruited from the peasantry, the Caroleans go under strict training and are renowned for invoking fear in the hearts of their enemies.

SWE.name: Hakkapeliitta
SWE.desc: The Hakkapeliitta were the fearsome Finnish cavalry known for their gruesome effectiveness on the battlefield. The name Hakkapeliitta is a Finnish modification of the names that the soldiers of the Holy Roman Empire gave them, stemming from their battle cry 'Hakkaa päälle!', or 'Hack on them!'/'Cut them down!'. The Hakkapeliitta were feared for their sudden and savage attacks that shocked the enemy into submission.

SWE.name: Always Attack
SWE.desc: Forming our marching troops into a Svinfylking and charging is enough force to shatter any opponent! Mounted troops are not superior; other than being ridden to the battle itself, horses have no place on the battlefield.

SWE.name: Caroleans
SWE.desc: The Caroleans are the Swedish and Finnish infantry of the Swedish Empire. Recruited from the peasantry, the Caroleans go under strict training and are renowned for invoking fear in the hearts of their enemies.

SWE.name: Free Farmers
SWE.desc: Swedish peasants have always made significant contributions to our country; the differences between a noble and a free farmer have never been big.

SWE.name: Hakkapeliitta
SWE.desc: Finland is considered a rather poor and backwards region, but service in the Swedish cavalry offers skilled Finnish horsemen ample opportunities for glory and plunder. Superior horsemanship and high-quality mounts allow us to raise the feared Hakkapeliitta — cavalry so effective in battle that our enemies whisper they must be protected by witchcraft.

SWE.name: Indelningsverket
SWE.desc: The Swedish allotment system divides the peasantry into groups of ten for recruitment purposes. This system made it easier to find people to serve in the army and organize them into units.

SWE.name: Kung och Riksdag
SWE.desc: Swedish rulers often depended on cooperation with the estates, especially with such a large peasant class compared to that of the nobility. During the reign of Gustavus Adolphus, however, a historic compromise was made with the aristocrats, who loyally pledged their resources to the disposal of the nation in return for new privileges.
mods: Estate Satisfaction from Destroying Estate Buildings

SWE.name: Kungliga Postverket
SWE.desc: The Kungliga Postverket, or Royal Postal Agency, was created to improve state administration and communication across the expanse of Sweden. It establishes a reliable network of couriers and waystations, and has become crucial for our military coordination, diplomacy, and governance.

SWE.name: Machina Nova
SWE.desc: Christopher Polhem, dubbed the 'father of Swedish engineering, has transformed Swedish industry with his Machina Nova, an innovative array of mechanical systems designed to streamline and boost production. Using intricate systems of gears, cams, and water power, Polhem has developed several machines capable of performing tasks previously done by hand, from ore-crushing in mines to textile weaving and sawmilling.

SWE.name: Mulltimmer Masugn
SWE.desc: Swedish Iron, prized for its purity and strength, supplies not only our domestic needs but also the foundries and armories of nations across the continent. The Mulltimmer Masugn was not built just with stone, but also with wood isolated with sand, gravel and dirt.

SWE.name: Produktplakatet
SWE.desc: The decree forbids foreign ships arriving in Sweden to bring goods from countries other than their own or their colonies.

SWE.name: Swedish Absolutism
SWE.desc: Absolutism is the theory that one person should be in charge, that this person is the monarch, and that said monarch shall run the government unfettered by the Privy Council.

SWE.name: Swedish Copper Coins
SWE.desc: The abundance of copper in Sweden, primarily from the Stora Kopparberget mine in Falun, has prompted the country to use it as the main metal for minting a new national currency, the daler. This is issued as a large money plate, called plåtmynt, which can weigh up to 20 kilograms. Some argue that this might not be very practical and that the volume of money in circulation could exceed copper reserves, but they seem narrow-minded.

SWE.name: Swedish Steel
SWE.desc: While other armies may be content to wildly fire inaccurate volleys at their enemies, we shall march at them in disciplined ranks, deliver a single volley at close range, and then feed them cold steel.

SWE.name: Stadsrättigheter
SWE.desc: The merchants of this location will receive extended privileges to conduct their trade free of foreign competition.

SWE.name: Support New Farms in North or East
SWE.desc: We are supporting Finnish and Swedish settlers in the north to colonize and populate the new lands.

SYZ.name: Eternal Alliance of the Forest Cantons
SYZ.desc: We have forged an eternal alliance with our friends in the neighboring Cantons. Had it not been for this treaty, we would have surely succumbed to the Habsburg invaders and fallen under the rule of foreign tyrants yet again. These alliances will ensure our survival for centuries to come.

TAT.name: Al-Maghīlī's Jurisprudence
TAT.desc: Muḥammad al-Maghīlī of Tuat, author of the Aḥkām Ahl adh-Dhimma and counselor to the askiyas of Songhai, exports our Mālikī jurisprudence across the western Sahara, the Hausa cities, and the Sahel kingdoms beyond. His rulings on dhimmī status, taxation, and ruler-subject obligations bind the courts of Songhai, Kano, and Katsina to Tuat's juridical authority. This concentrated scholarly authority extends our cultural influence well beyond our oasis frontiers and binds the southern Maghrebi-Sahelian clergy to our shayḵs.

TAT.name: Caravan Escort Corps
TAT.desc: The Tuat escort companies, armed and mounted on oasis-bred camels and Saharan horses, hire out their services to every major caravan transiting our territory between Sijilmāsa and the Niger bend. Our riders know every waterhole, every reliable forage track, and every raider's likely ambush point across two thousand kilometers of desert. Our light cavalry escorts caravans swiftly and reinforces our campaigns quickly, for no inland Maghrebi power has our local knowledge of the desert.

TAT.name: Caravan Oligopoly
TAT.desc: The Tuat caravan houses (Kawāsim, Bū Bakr, Kuntī) formalize their trans-Saharan monopoly through bonded warehouses at every relay post, fixed tariffs published at the oasis gates, and exclusive escort contracts that competitors cannot reproduce. Our agents at Walāta, Timbuktu, Sijilmāsa, and Touggourt clear every load through the same set of accounting books. A closely held monopoly brings our crown great merchant strength and steady tariff revenue, while the unorganized caravan broker towns of the wider Sahara go without.

TAT.name: Ibāḍī-Mālikī Coexistence
TAT.desc: Mālikī majority and Ibāḍī minority share the foggāra water rights, the caravan protection corps, and the ksar councils across the Tuat oases, a religious coexistence no urban Maghrebi capital can equal under its own jurists' rulings. Our shayḵs of both schools attend the same federation assembly, sit on the same trade arbitration tribunal, and recognize each other's marriage and inheritance contracts. A pluralistic settlement lends our court a wide tolerance and a broad religious legitimacy that single-school states struggle to keep.

TAT.name: Steamship-Era Pivot
TAT.desc: As Atlantic steamships divert the trade in gold and slaves away from the desert routes in the late nineteenth century, the Tuat houses pivot to dates, salt, and Saharan-tourist transit, adapting our towns to the smaller but durable commercial niche that survives the steam revolution. Our oases now host visiting foreign scholars, merchant agents, and curious travelers whose payments and gifts supplement the surviving caravan revenues, and our agents at Algiers and Oran open Mediterranean-sea connections to the coastal steamer lines. The pivot opens some trade by sea and draws settlers to our towns, which Saharan towns living on trade volume alone could never preserve.

TAT.name: Tuat Date Palmery
TAT.desc: Millions of date palms across the Tuat oases, sustained by the foggāra irrigation networks running tens of kilometers under the desert sand, feed our people, our caravans, and our export trade in equal measure. Our cultivators have selected the celebrated Deglet Nour and Aghras varieties for premium markets across the Mediterranean and the Sahel. Deep oasis cultivation brings our crown a great export of fruit and a steady prosperity that the rain-fed agriculture of the Maghrebi coast can never match.

TEU.name: Absolute Order
TEU.desc: All powers of the state are consolidated in our order. Every action taken and every decision made goes through the hierarchy of the Teutonic Order first before it gets executed. Of course, this bureaucracy is not in everyone's favor, but it ensures the absolute power of the Hochmeister.

TEU.name: Crusader Discipline
TEU.desc: Our grand order was forged in the flames and blood of the Third Crusade during the siege of Acre in 1191. While we originally nursed the sick and feeble, the order has transformed into a militarized group of knights of unbreakable devotion and discipline.

TEU.name: Expanded Marches
TEU.desc: Grant autonomy to the local governors of our border regions, and reform their holdings into marches. These special zones will pay fewer taxes to the state in return for an obligation to maintain the highest combat readiness during times of war as well as peace. This should provide us with substantial military flexibility at little cost.

TEU.name: Infantry Tactics
TEU.desc: Contemporary battles in Europe have proven that the age of infantry is about to begin. It is now time to develop new tactics, adopt use of the pike, and reform our medieval concept of auxiliary infantry into the main fighting force of our future armies.

TEU.name: One State, One Religion
TEU.desc: Reserve all state offices only for those who follow our religion. Heretics and heathens are no longer welcome in our realm.

TEU.name: Peasant Recruitment
TEU.desc: It has become clear to us that we can no longer rely on foreign volunteers to fill up our army ranks, no matter how experienced and valuable they might be. Instead, we will develop a system that would allow us to levy our subjects, both German and non-German folk alike.

TEU.name: Prussian Bishops
TEU.desc: We shall grant further rights and privileges to our Prussian bishops, ensuring their loyalty in all matters.

TEU.name: Reformed Order Army
TEU.desc: The German knights, and veterans of the Crusades and other wars are simply not numerous enough to remain the base of our armies. We must reorganize the army to incorporate domestic levies, regiments capable of replacing the knights on the battlefield.

TEU.name: Teutonic Heavy Cavalry
TEU.desc: There is no greater symbol of power and military prowess than the heavy cavalry. While for many states the cavalry is made of nobles, every Teutonic Knight is also a member of our heavy cavalry, and undergoes the strict training of a crusader.

TEU.name: Teutonic Religious Authority
TEU.desc: We will put an end to the loose religious autonomy local bishops hold within our realm. All religious matters, from taxation to converting the populace, will be state matters from now on.

TFL.name: Caravan Protection Tariffs
TFL.desc: The qā'ids of Tafilalt levy a regulated ṣadaqa al-qāfila (caravan protection tariff) on every load entering or departing the oasis at the published rates of our customs houses at Sijilmasa, Rissani, and the desert gates, in exchange for armed escort across the pre-Saharan frontier. The collection passes through bonded accountants of the qā'idal houses, with a fixed share routed directly to the central court and the remainder retained for the maintenance of the desert escort and the upkeep of the watering posts. This published rate tariff system stabilizes our exchange of caravan custom for state protection and routes the proceeds straight to the sultan's court, sparing our treasury the waste of provincial intermediaries.

TFL.name: Emirate of Mūlay 'Alī ash-Sharīf
TFL.desc: Mūlay 'Alī ash-Sharīf, eldest of the Alaouite sharifian house long established at Tafilalt, receives the bay'a of the assembled qā'ids, marabouts, and tribal chiefs of the oasis as the founding emir of an autonomous southern principality. Our administrative chamber of viziers, our reformed treasury, and our court ceremonial draw equally on the Saharan Idrīsid heritage of our forefathers and on the Marinid chancery practice of the northern Maghreb, forging an emirate whose internal coherence the lands of dissidence around us cannot easily match. This consolidation of the Tafilalt under a single sharifian throne gives our court the administrative reach, the legitimacy across confessional lines, and the dynastic continuity that the older Maghrebi sultanates spend decades trying to reproduce.

TFL.name: Oasis Levy Horsemen
TFL.desc: Each ksar of Tafilalt provides its share of the seasonal horse and mehari camel rider muster, a light cavalry of the Saharan school trained from boyhood to ride down raiders across the dunes, ambush caravans, and outpace any pursuing force across terrain no infantry can cover. Our oasis stables breed the dark-coated Berber horse on the date palm fodder of our gardens and on the brackish wells of the deep oasis, producing mounts of stamina that no Mediterranean-bred warhorse can match in the Saharan climate. Our oasis cavalry tradition fields a swift mobile force whose endurance and speed the standing forces of the centralizing northern courts will struggle to meet.

TFL.name: Oasis Tax Resilience
TFL.desc: The Tafilalt's irrigation register, the meticulous record of every seguia channel, every date palm parcel, and every household water share kept by the assembly of qā'ids, lets our fiscal officers assess and collect taxation with an accuracy and equity that the makhzen's roving inspectors cannot duplicate elsewhere. The Tafilalti caravan houses keep their accounts under the same registry, settling state contracts at fees so modest that no inland court can negotiate comparable rates from its own merchants. Deep-rooted oasis fiscal practice gives our treasury steady taxes and a thrifty discipline in keeping merchants, which the makhzen's central provinces struggle to match.

TFL.name: Sijilmasa Gold Terminus
TFL.desc: Every caravan from the Sahel terminates its journey at Sijilmāsa, the great trans-Saharan way station at the heart of Tafilalt where Wangara gold dust, Sudanic kola, and Saharan captives change hands for slab salt, Maghrebi textiles, and the silver of the Iberian Mediterranean. Our merchant clans operate the assay foundries, the gold dust scales, and the bonded warehouses through hereditary charters that secure the prosperity of the entire oasis. Our unbroken commercial primacy fills the Tafilalt with the wealth of the southern caravans, a prosperity that inland Maghrebi cities far from the desert termini cannot match.

TFL.name: Trans-Saharan Outposts
TFL.desc: The qā'ids of Tafilalt maintain a chain of garrisoned outposts at Tindouf, In-Salah, Wadi Saoura, and the desert waterposts between, through which our merchant houses, our scribes, and our diplomatic envoys project influence across the deep Sahara to the emirates of Adrar, Walata, and the Sahel beyond. Our resident garrisons at each funduq station combine watering rights, armed escort, and bonded warehousing, anchoring the trans-Saharan commercial system on Tafilalti capital and Tafilalti tariffs rather than on remote court directives. The outpost network multiplies the commercial reach of our oasis far beyond its formal frontiers and gives our merchant houses a chain of waystations that inland Maghrebi states cannot easily build.

TGT.name: Beni Djellab Sultanate
TGT.desc: The Beni Djellab family proclaim themselves Sultans of Touggourt, consolidating power over the Souf and Wādī Rīgh oasis complexes under a single dynastic line whose dynastic continuity outlasts every neighboring oasis confederation. They build the central Touggourt qaṣr as both ceremonial residence and administrative center, organize a makhzen-style chancery for fiscal records, and project authority across the surrounding ksūr through marriage alliances and military levies. The sultanate gives the Souf oasis region a centralized political form, which the consensus-governed neighboring oases never achieve.

TGT.name: Caravan Levies
TGT.desc: Our crown raises a permanent military garrison through caravan tax revenues. The zakāt al-'ushūr on incoming goods funds standing oasis guard companies and a tribal cavalry reserve drawn from the surrounding Berber confederations. Our tribesmen serve in rotation on the city walls and at the caravan staging waterholes, earning a share of caravan fees in lieu of regular pay, and our crown's permanent military establishment grows independent of either central Algerian or Tunisian tributary demands. Funded by the caravans, our levy system gives our state a standing garrison at no cost to the regular agricultural economy.

TGT.name: Qādiriyya Zwāyā Network
TGT.desc: Our central oasis hosts the principal Qādiriyya Sufi zwāyā of the southern Algerian Sahara (Tolga, Sidi Khaled, and the chain of lodges between), drawing pilgrims from every oasis between the Aurès and the Sahel, and binding the southern religious establishment to our court through shared ritual and endowed land. Our sultan funds the upkeep of the lodge mosques, the teaching circles of the Qādiriyya shayḵs, and the seasonal mawlid festivals that draw thousands of pilgrims to our city. Patronage of the Sufi network spreads our crown's religious and cultural influence across the south, beyond what any purely secular sultanate can do.

TGT.name: Saharan Crossroads
TGT.desc: Our oasis sits at the confluence of three trans-Saharan caravan routes (the western route to Tafilalt and Sijilmasa, the central route to Ouargla and the Niger, and the eastern route to Ghadāmis and Tripoli), making us the natural meeting point for caravans of every Maghrebi state. Our central market draws traders from Tunis, Algiers, Fez, Tripoli, and the deep Sahara every season, and the migrant families who follow the caravans settle in our growing urban quarters. Standing at the crossroads, our state reaches across the entire Saharan network and draws a steady stream of settlers to its towns, as no single-route oasis can.

TGT.name: Sultanate Administration
TGT.desc: Our Beni Djellab sultans refine the makhzen administration into a proper fiscal institution, registering palm groves and date yields, recording caravan transactions, paying salaried scribes and judges from a central treasury, and dispensing justice through a tiered court system from the village qāḍī up to the sultan's own dīwān. We hire trained administrators from Tunis, Algiers, and even Cairo as advisors, our court correspondence in formal Arabic flows out across the Ottoman world, and our archives preserve every fiscal record of the sultanate. Our administrative sophistication reaches into fiscal and judicial affairs as no other Saharan oasis state's does.

TGT.name: Sultanate Autonomy
TGT.desc: Our Sultan negotiates a careful autonomy from the Algerian Ottoman Regency, recognizing the Sublime Porte's nominal suzerainty, paying a modest annual tribute, and accepting periodic Janissary detachments from Algiers as garrison auxiliaries, while retaining full internal governance and an independent treasury. Our court hires Christian renegades, Andalusi exiles, and Ottoman Janissaries on contractual terms alongside our Berber tribal levies, giving our military a cosmopolitan officer corps no purely tribal sultanate can field. This negotiated autonomy preserves our independence through centuries of Algerian-Regency political turbulence.

THP.name: A Centralized Levy System
THP.desc: We have moved away from loose clan associations toward a semi-professional core of infantry based in our central cities. Where tribal levies gather slowly, ours answer a threat quickly and in good order.

THP.name: French Blood Claims
THP.desc: We assert a prestigious, albeit disputed, descent from the French Royalty, granting our diplomats a unique standing in the courts of Europe. This perceived noble pedigree allows us to negotiate as peers with the Italian city-states and the Papacy, securing alliances that would be denied to common Balkan warlords.

THP.name: Mecenas of the Arts
THP.desc: We have funded the construction of grand cathedrals and fortifications, blending Gothic and Byzantine styles to showcase our wealth and piety. This architectural splendor serves to legitimize our rule in the eyes of the Church and our subjects, turning our cities into symbols of permanence.

THP.name: Princeps Albaniae
THP.desc: Our name has become synonymous with the state itself, allowing us to integrate various ethnic groups under a single banner. By promoting the most talented individuals regardless of their origins, we have created a meritocratic bureaucracy that outshines our feudal rivals.

THP.name: The Lion of Thopia
THP.desc: Our house has risen to preeminence by masterfully navigating the clashes among the clans, positioning the Thopia family as the arbiters of Albanian sovereignty. By weaving together a complex web of alliances, we will secure the first true Princeps Albaniae title recognized by both the East and the West. With the lion of our crest flying over the ramparts of the coast, we have established a professionalized administrative core that outpaces the primitive feudalism of our rivals, ensuring our house remains the foremost power of the Adriatic shore.

THP.name: The Thopia Merchant Marine
THP.desc: We have expanded our commercial influence by offering state protection to all merchant vessels flying the Thopia banner. This naval security has turned our ports into the preferred hubs for Levant trade, siphoning wealth away from the decaying ports of our rivals.

TIB.name: Drokpa
TIB.desc: The Drokpa nomads often operate as herders and traders, porters that connect distant settlements. Through their traditions and unparalleled knowledge of the terrain, they traverse the high-altitude routes between Tibet, Bhutan, Ladakh, and Nepal. Their seasonal caravans carry Salt, Wool, and dried meat in exchange for grain and manufactured goods. These networks knit our mountains into a vibrant lattice of commerce and diplomacy.

TIB.name: Monastic Dominance
TIB.desc: A fusion of spiritual and temporal rule defines our political landscape. From the smallest village to the halls of power in Sakya, monastic institutions are central to every sphere of life. Their moral authority and organizational prowess ensure loyalty, unity, and cultural resilience.

TIB.name: Monastic Education System
TIB.desc: Our monastic institutions have long served as centers of learning, debate, and spiritual discipline. Through rigorous training and a structured approach to education, our clerics maintain a high standard of intellectual and moral integrity. These foundations will support wise governance and cultural flourishing across our enlightened realm.

TIB.name: Sakya Hegemony
TIB.desc: For the last century, the Sakya school has held temporal authority over Tibet, acting as spiritual and political stewards under Mongol patronage. Their dominance ushered in an age of centralized governance and scholastic consolidation. Though their rule has waned, their legacy continues to shape our approach to authority and order.

TIB.name: The Three Great Seats
TIB.desc: Sera, Ganden, and Drepung, these towering monastic universities form the intellectual heart of Tibet. Their scholars train one generation after another of monks, diplomats, and rulers. With their rise, our realm became not only a bastion of faith but a cradle of rigorous thought and institutional progress.

TIB.name: The Yak
TIB.desc: Domesticated for centuries, the yak is the backbone of Tibetan pastoral life. It provides meat, milk, wool, transport, and fuel — even its dried dung is a vital source of fuel on the treeless plateau. In times of need or celebration, yak butter fills our lamps and cups.

TIB.name: Tányuè Guānxì
TIB.desc: For centuries, our spiritual influence in China has formed the bedrock of our diplomatic relations. Imperial patronage, tribute exchanges, and sacred rituals like Tányuè secure both respect and material gain.

TIR.name: Archduchy of Austria
TIR.desc: We have been granted the Privilegium Maius, which grants us an elevated position among the princes of the Holy Roman Empire. This shows our status and prestige even outside of Imperial lands, and elevates us to a higher position than that of a mere duke.

TIR.name: Austrian Diplomatic Expertise
TIR.desc: Given our location at the center of all Europe, we must adopt a highly flexible attitude towards external diplomacy. Alliances and rivals can shatter as easily as they are formed, and our diplomats must be trained to cover every possible position.

TIR.name: Land of Mountains and Rivers
TIR.desc: Our people are highly adapted to traverse the obstacles of our country, from the high peaks and passes of our mountains to the wide rivers of our valleys.

TIR.name: Landsknecht Tactics
TIR.desc: Only well-rounded tactics of artillery shock, cavalry charges, and unyielding infantry recruited from the can lead us to victory.

TLE.name: Bānu 'Abd āl-Wād Investiture
TLE.desc: The ability to rule this state is largely dependent on the support of the Zenati Bānu 'Abd āl-Wād in the environs of Oran. Should our backing amongst those Tribes falter, so will our legitimacy and ability to govern effectively.
