TLE.name: Mashwar Court
TLE.desc: The mashwar is the inner audience court of the Tlemcen sultanate, where the sultan receives counsel from the great nobles and jurists of the realm in a ceremonial setting that binds them to the throne through formal recognition. Its deliberative character gives the Zayyanid state a consultative legitimacy that distinguishes it from purely coercive rule, lending the sultan's decisions the weight of collective noble endorsement. We formalize the proceedings of this court, making it the recognized channel through which policy is debated and the noble estate exercises its influence within the constitutional order.

TLE.name: Zayyanid Ghulām
TLE.desc: The Zayyanid Ghulām are the mamlūk-style slave retainers of the Zayyanid emirs of Tlemcen, bought from the Saharan caravan trade and Genoese factors at Oran, trained from boyhood, and sworn to the emir alone. They garrison the Mechouar fortress and form the emir's strike force when the tribes threaten the throne.

TLE.name: Entrepôt Connections
TLE.desc: Our roads link Tlemcen to its outport of Honein on the Mediterranean, to the Saharan staging post of Sijilmasa, and to the great Maghrebi trunk routes that cross our territory under royal escort. We charter our noble houses to maintain the carriage tracks and the funduq stations along these arteries in exchange for tax exemptions and grants of land along the route. This system of merchant convoys keeps the central Maghrebi trade flowing reliably even when factional warfare disrupts Fez or Tunis.

TLE.name: Mālikī High Council
TLE.desc: Our city's Mālikī jurists, the heirs of the great Tlemceni qādīs Ibn Marzūq and the long line of teachers at the Ya'qūbiyya madrasa, convene as the recognized synod of orthodox jurisprudence for the entire western Maghreb. Rulings of the Majlis Mālikī Tilimsān circulate through the Qādirī and Shādhilī Sufi networks, are cited at the courts of Fez, Marrakesh, and the trans-Saharan emirates, and bind even sultans who would prefer juridical authority of their own. This concentrated legal and scholarly authority extends our cultural influence well beyond our political frontiers and binds the western Maghrebi clergy to our court.

TLE.name: Origins of the Ṭarīqa Tijāniyya
TLE.desc: The Mālikī faqīh Aḥmad at-Tijānī founds his namesake Ṭarīqa Tijāniyya at the oasis of 'Ayn Māḍī at the southern edge of our territory, claiming an exclusive spiritual pact with the Prophet and a chain of authority bypassing all earlier Sufi orders. Tijānī missionaries fan out from our state across the western and southern Sahara, into Fez, the Senegalese marches, and as far as the Sudanic emirates, propagating both the order and the diplomatic prestige of its Tlemceni hearth. This new Sufi network extends our religious influence across every Muslim court of the Atlantic basin and the trans-Saharan world.

TLE.name: Qal'at al-Mashwār
TLE.desc: The Qal'at al-Mashwar at the heart of Tlemcen rises as both fortified royal residence and the seat of Zayyanid court ceremony, housing the dīwān that taxes the Saharan caravans from Sijilmasa and Ouargla, the Mediterranean shipping from Oran, and the overland passage between Fez and Tunis. Its triple-walled enclosure concentrates the offices of state, including administrative chambers, the mint, the markets of the Mechouar quarter, and the sultan's personal guard, within a single defensible compound. A stronghold at once palace and treasury lends the Zayyanid capital a fiscal weight beyond any purely territorial Maghrebi state, and the strength that comes from holding every organ of state behind the same walls.

TLE.name: Tlemceni Carpets
TLE.desc: Our urban looms, concentrated in the Bāb al-'Aqaba and Bāb Sīdī Bū Madyan quarters, weave the celebrated sajjādat Tilimsān, the dense-knotted pile carpets whose geometric medallions distinguish them from every other Maghrebi rug tradition. Andalusi master weavers who settled in our city add new vegetal patterns and indigo vermilion palettes that command premium prices from Genoese, Marseillais, and Venetian merchants at the Oran fairs. Our regulated carpet industry gives our crown a trade in luxury cloth and an urban class of artisans, far beyond what the wool and tent producers of the inland tribes can offer.

TLE.name: Tlemceni Nahḍa
TLE.desc: Our cultural revival, the Tlemceni Nahḍa, centers around the scholars Muḥammad as-Sa'īdī, Ibn Khūja, and the salons of the Old Mechouar, reclaiming the Zayyanid–Andalusi heritage that earlier interventions had let lapse. We restore the great madrasas, reprint the medieval Tlemceni manuscripts from the libraries of Fez and the Escorial, and publish bilingual periodicals that introduce European thought into the western Maghrebi conversation. This linguistic and intellectual renewal binds the scattered Zayyanid heritage into a shared modern identity that no foreign administration can easily fragment.

TLE.name: Zayyanid Ghulām
TLE.desc: The Zayyanid Ghulām are the mamlūk-style slave retainers of the Zayyanid emirs of Tlemcen, bought from the Saharan caravan trade and Genoese factors at Oran, trained from boyhood, and sworn to the emir alone. They garrison the Mechouar fortress and form the emir's strike force when the tribes threaten the throne.

TNC.name: Aztec Chargers
TNC.desc: The aggressive nature of our warriors is known — and feared — beyond our borders. When battle starts, our enemies shiver in fear at the sight of our combatants charging at them with frenzy, as if they were about to be run down by the heralds of Death itself.

TNC.name: Brave as a Hummingbird
TNC.desc: The hummingbird holds a crucial role in our mythology. Linked to the god of war, Huītzilōpōchtli, it embodies fallen warriors' reincarnation and is honored for its bravery. The hummingbird will be made a new symbol for our banners, one that will inspire our soldiers to fight unto their deaths!

TNC.name: Calpixcāyōtl
TNC.desc: Our tributary regions will receive appointed tribute collectors, called calpixqueh, who will be in charge of ensuring the flow of tribute never stops. There will be a calpixqui in the region, and another in the capital of our nation, for each tributary state.

TNC.name: Chinampas
TNC.desc: Proficient in terracing hills for cultivation and skilled in crafting arable land on shallow lake portions through ingenious chinampas, our populace's remarkable agricultural abilities will significantly benefit our society.

TNC.name: Nahua Domination
TNC.desc: The superiority of Nahua culture is very clear, as neighboring peoples increasingly adopt it as their own. This cultural diffusion and spread of influence creates opportunities for us to extend our political control well beyond our borders.

TNC.name: New Trade Opportunities
TNC.desc: The needs of our people have been adapting to the new markets that have opened to our traders, and we have been training our merchants in methods to maximize our earnings.

TNC.name: People of War
TNC.desc: Whether we take up arms on a search for prestige, to instill fear in our foes, to take captives for sacrifice, or simply to acquire wealth, our people are accustomed to a continuous state of warfare, enduring its hardships with more resilience than members of other nations.

TNC.name: Pōchtēcayōtl
TNC.desc: Traders travel far afield, to provinces well beyond the reach of our authority, and even to the territories of our rivals. If these traders were to, perhaps, also serve as our eyes and ears, what secrets might we learn?

TNC.name: Reformed Tēlpōchcalli
TNC.desc: As we face new enemies, new military tactics have to be developed or learned. This invaluable knowledge will be taught in our Tēlpōchcalli.

TNC.name: The Return of Quetzalcōātl
TNC.desc: Contact with foreigners from other continents has given us interesting new ideas about our gods. The Quetzalcōātl prophecy unveils a reality beyond myth — a glimpse of truth. Quetzalcōātl, 'the Feathered Serpent', will soon return and herald a transformative era, vanquishing darkness for enlightenment. Symbolizing cosmic fusion, he will bridge matter and spirit, restoring balance and elevating human consciousness.

TNC.name: Tlahtohcāyōtl
TNC.desc: We will create a system of provinces for the city-states that are integrated into our realm in an effort to centralize our power.

TNC.name: Warrior Societies
TNC.desc: Our society is remarkably dynamic, offering commoners, also known as mācēhualtin, the path to become pīpiltin, or noble, by exceptional military service through the tlahuiztli honor dress rank system. This unique opportunity for upward mobility grants our people a distinct advantage over those in neighboring societies.

TNK.name: Ancient Roots
TNK.desc: Our ancestors ruled the lands of Tamil Nadu for centuries. In these times when we are dominated by foreign invaders, we should rely on our ancient connections to this land to justify our rule.

TNK.name: Expert Resistance
TNK.desc: Our troubled history records both victories and crushing defeats. If we want to endure and dominate as a significant power once more, we must develop a thorough understanding of how to best utilize our native terrain to delay and stall hostile armies until we can mount a direct resistance.

TNK.name: Hardened by War
TNK.desc: Throughout our turbulent history, we never wavered in the face of conflict and insurmountable odds. We need to weaponize this determination, and use it to instill a sense of fervor into our people that will inspire them to fight harder than ever.

TNK.name: Imperial Pandyan Legacy
TNK.desc: The lands of southern India have long endured the incursions of foreign invaders and upstart warlords looking to establish their own domains. We must use the grand history of our ancient dynasty to lay claim to this land, as only we can bring stability and peace back to our rightful territory.

TNK.name: Pearl-Diving Expertise
TNK.desc: Our people have developed an outstanding skill for diving for and harvesting pearls along our coasts. While this has clear economic benefits, the natural affinity our people have for water makes them excellent and easily-trained sailors, granting us an edge against our seafaring foes.

TRE.name: Form Byzantium
TRE.desc: Lets TRE form Byzantium.

TRE.name: Form Rome
TRE.desc: Lets BYZ, TRE form Rome.

TRE.name: Byzantine Birthright
TRE.desc: The great Byzantine Empire, under the rule of our forefathers, was truly something to behold. Deceit and treachery may have toppled their regime, but Byzantium has risen like the phoenix to reclaim its former glory, and now no one shall doubt our authority!

TRE.name: Empire in Exile
TRE.desc: We inherit some of the bureaucracy of our former empire, allowing us to maintain order and governance despite our reduced circumstances.

TRE.name: Grand Komnenoi
TRE.desc: The Komnenos dynasty may have been expelled from the Byzantine throne long ago, but its glory never faded. Members of our lineage are still shown the appropriate deference, and this respect and admiration stretches far beyond our borders.

TRE.name: Greek Stronghold
TRE.desc: Since ancient times, Greek has been the language of education and science. When our ancestors came here, they not only brought their determination, but also their culture and native tongue. As such, the Greek tradition of learning is very much alive in our country.

TRE.name: Komnenoi Princesses
TRE.desc: Some remarkable women have emerged from along the Komnenos, and many among the rulers of Europe and even the infidels have sought their hands in matrimony. Our line is well-respected, and our princesses doubly so, for they are what allow foreign countries to claim legitimacy through our line, and us to maintain influence in foreign courts.

TRE.name: Komnenos Legacy
TRE.desc: Let nobody forget that we are the descendants of the Komnenos that ruled over the Byzantine Empire. Although we now rule a different state, the legacy and prestige of our dynasty remains undeniable.

TRE.name: Lessons of the Fourth Crusade
TRE.desc: Isaakios Angelos, who deposed our line centuries ago, was himself deposed and blinded. On the pretense of putting the blind old fool back on the throne, the Venetian troops then sacked Constantinople. If there is something to learn from this incident, it is that treason and deceit are ubiquitous in the struggle for power, but they can also safeguard victory.

TRE.name: Pontic Mountains
TRE.desc: Much as the Alps separate the French and Italian, the Pontic Mountains separate our last Greek holdout in Anatolia from the Turkic invaders who have seized the Anatolian Plateau. Pontus has always been more Greek than the rest of Anatolia; perhaps the legacy of the great Mithridates will inspire our warriors and strike as much fear into the Turks as he did the Romans?

TRE.name: Pontic Trail Mastery
TRE.desc: Our land is like our home; its forests, our garden. We know every bit of it better than anyone. Every path and every trail that crosses it is known to us, and we will make use of that knowledge if any dare to invade us.

TRE.name: Princes of the Laz
TRE.desc: The Laz have inhabited these lands for centuries. While our Empire was forged by Greek people, many Laz nonetheless remain within our borders. This has led to some of our enemies calling us Princes of the Laz in mockery, regarding us as inferiors. However, no matter what they say, it does not diminish our heritage, and we shall wear the title proudly.

TRE.name: Strategic Marriages
TRE.desc: Kingdoms are conquered not only by the sword. By forging marriage alliances with surrounding nations, we create opportunities to inherit their thrones — and, at the very least, extend stronger influence over them.

TRE.name: Terminus of the Silk Road
TRE.desc: Even when it was called Trapezous in the mists of antiquity, our nation was the point where the land route across Asia meets the sea route leading to the Mediterranean. We grew famous as the terminal point for the great Silk Road, the wealth of China and India passing through our lands on its way to Europe. Since our nation still lies in this crucial location, there is no reason for us not to continue and encourage this steady flow of intercontinental trade.

TRE.name: Trapezuntine Endurance
TRE.desc: Banished from our country, and yet our line survived. Forced to live in a mountainous wasteland surrounded by enemies, and yet our people thrived. We are a resourceful people, determined to make the most of what we have and to best whatever situation we encounter.

TRE.name: Trapezuntine Monasteries
TRE.desc: It is our faith that saves the souls of our people, and our clergy are the ones who ensure their salvation. What, then, are our monasteries, if not the source and origin of such salvation?

TRE.name: Allelengyon
TRE.desc: Originally conceived under Emperor Basil II (commonly known by his nickname the Bulgar-Slayer) and deriving from the Greek word allilengýi (solidarity), the Allelengyon was a tax obligation designed to redistribute fiscal burden. When smallholders fail to meet their dues, responsibility is legally transferred to wealthier landowners of the district, ensuring imperial revenue while preventing the ruin and absorption of peasant lands. In this way, fiscal solidarity becomes a lever of stability and control.

TRE.name: Books of the Basiliká
TRE.desc: Building upon Justinian's Corpus Juris Civilis, the Books of the Basiliká reorganize Roman law into a coherent Greek legal corpus. By clarifying, standardizing, and harmonizing centuries of jurisprudence, they render the Emperor's law undisputed, authoritative, and universal.

TRE.name: Court Eunuchs
TRE.desc: Educated, loyal, and excluded from dynastic ambition, court eunuchs form a trusted administrative cadre. Their proximity to the Emperor and insulation from familial power make them ideal stewards of palace governance, finance, and imperial correspondence.

TRE.name: Honorary Titles
TRE.desc:
From the Patrikios and Anthypatos to the Magistros and Kouropalatēs, our court governs ambition through dignity rather than command.

This intricate system, revolving around the bestowing of ranked honors, silks, and privileges, allows the Emperor to bind generals, senators, and provincial elites to the throne by rewarding loyalty, defusing rivalry, and turning prestige itself into an instrument of rule.

TRE.name: Imperial Senate
TRE.desc: Composed of senior dignitaries appointed by imperial authority, the Senate serves as a body of acclamation and counsel. Its assent legitimizes reigns, successions, and major acts, preserving Roman continuity while ensuring that sovereignty remains firmly imperial.

TRE.name: Kephalai
TRE.desc: The Kephalai are administrative and legal compendia designed to render imperial governance practicable. Replacing older regional arrangements such as the Katepaníkion, they distill law, taxation, and military obligations into standardized directives, ensuring uniform rule across the provinces.
mods: Monthly Prosperity in towns and cities

TRE.name: Nómos Émpsychos
TRE.desc: Deriving from the concept of living law (Nómos Émpsychos), the Emperor forms a fundamental cornerstone of our administration and embodies sovereign authority itself. First articulated under Justinian, this principle binds legislation, justice, and command to the imperial person, placing the ruler at the very core of the Roman state.

TRE.name: Ritualistic Court
TRE.desc: Ceremony is governance made visible. Through regulated ritual, precedence, and spectacle, the imperial court transforms authority into sacred theatre, ordering hierarchy at home while overwhelming foreign envoys with the majesty of our great capital, the perceived center of the civilized world.

TRE.name: Romanitas
TRE.desc: Romanitas affirms uninterrupted Roman statehood. The Emperor rules not by conquest or ethnicity, but as the lawful inheritor of authority, law, and tradition that dates back over a millennium. This identity binds empire and faith together, presenting Roman rule as divinely sanctioned and morally supreme.

TRE.name: Strategarchia
TRE.desc: The Strategarchia embodies the institutional command of the imperial army. Generals are appointed, rotated, and restrained by bureaucracy, ensuring that military power serves the state rather than personal ambition. Warfare is thus rendered an administrative function, governed by hierarchy rather than fealty, while ensuring only the best rise to the top.

TRE.name: Thémata
TRE.desc: Formed in response to existential pressure, the Thémata divide the empire into provincial military-administrative districts. Each of these divisions is governed by a Strategós who unites civil and military authority, enabling rapid local defense while remaining formally subordinate to the imperial hierarchy.

TRI.name: Balance the Landstände
TRI.desc: Our territory is both home to many urban areas and castles of many imperial knights. Balancing them and their often opposing interests is no easy task. Only if they cooperate with us and the cathedral chapter, we can ensure the functionality of our government.

TUN.name: Guardians of Ifrīqya
TUN.desc: Tunis carries the dynastic memory of Carthage's Punic dominion, Kairouan's Aghlabid amirate, and the Hafsid claim to the title of Khalīfa — caliph of the western Islamic world after the fall of Baghdad. Our sultans crown themselves in the Zaytuna mosque under regalia that links their throne to a thousand-year continuity of Ifrīqyan sovereignty, distinct from any Berber dynasty to the west or Mamluk power to the east. This composite imperial legacy gives Tunis a legitimacy that the surrounding Maghrebi states cannot match in either antiquity or doctrinal weight.

TUN.name: Husaynid Beylik
TUN.desc: Where the Ottoman framework installed rotating governors answerable to the Porte, the Husaynid bey transformed the beylik of Tunis into a hereditary dynasty in all but name, negotiating a constitutional fiction — nominal Ottoman sovereignty, effective dynastic rule — that lasted into the modern era. The Husaynids built a capable cabinet-based administration, preserved Ifrīqyan cultural continuity, and managed the balance between the increasingly nominal Ottoman connection and the practical demands of European diplomacy with more sophistication than most comparable polities. We have institutionalized this hybrid: a state that is dynastically governed, administratively modern in its cabinet apparatus, and prestigious enough to deal as a recognized sovereign while retaining the theological cover of Islamic suzerainty.

TUN.name: Hafsid Caliphal Claim
TUN.desc: The Hafsid sultans derive their claim to governance from descent and recognition as successors to the Almohad caliphate, presenting themselves to the Muslim world as the legitimate heirs to the universal authority of the Commander of the Faithful. We cultivate this caliphal dignity through ceremony, correspondence with distant Muslim rulers, and the patronage of scholars who articulate the theological basis of our claim. This spiritual authority elevates our prestige beyond that of a mere regional sultanate and secures the devotion of our Muslim subjects and allies.

TUN.name: Taifa of the Reïs
TUN.desc: The Tunisian tā'ifa of the reïs is a formally constituted corporation of corsair captains whose statutes govern the conduct of privateering operations, the distribution of prize shares, and the ransom of captives from the city's slave markets. We grant the taifa legal recognition as a chartered corporation of the burgher estate, binding the most capable maritime entrepreneurs of the realm to our cause in exchange for formal rights over the harbor. This arrangement gives Tunis one of the most organized corsair institutions in the western Mediterranean and a reliable source of sailors available for royal service in wartime.

TUN.name: Hafsid Ghulām
TUN.desc: The Hafsid Ghulām are the slave-soldier corps of Hafsid Tunis: Black African captives from the trans-Saharan markets, Iberian prisoners from corsair raids, and children of earlier ghulām born to the institution and bound to the throne. They are the disciplined counterweight to the restless Banū Hilāl tribal levies.

TUN.name: Admiralty Reform
TUN.desc: Our state shipyards at Bizerte and Porto Farina come under formal beylical admiralty command: replacing the personal charter corsair captain with a salaried fleet officer, organizing the conscription of sailors from the Sahel coastal towns through a registered ship roll, and substituting heavier classes of galley and galleon for the lighter raiding vessels that the previous century relied on. Our naval academy at La Goulette trains its officer cadre in the gunnery and navigation that the Mediterranean wars now demand, and our paymasters disburse fleet wages from the central treasury rather than through prize share. A state-organized naval administration leaves our successor regimes a fleet that no personal charter corsair tradition could sustain into the gunpowder era.

TUN.name: Caliphal Claim
TUN.desc: After the Mongol sack of Baghdad ends the 'Abbāsid line, our Hafsid sultans claim the khilāfa (the universal sovereignty over the Muslim community), invoking our Almohad-shayḵ descent and our role as protectors of Mālikī orthodoxy. Our Friday-sermons name our sultan as Commander of the Faithful, our coinage bears the caliphal titulature, and our diplomatic correspondence with the Mamluks, the Marinids, and the Ilkhanate insists on equal sovereign protocol. The caliphal pretension lends the original Tunis line a religious and political authority that no other Maghrebi dynasty matches, neither Marinid, nor Zayyanid, nor Waṭṭāsid.

TUN.name: Caliphal Revival
TUN.desc: Our reformist circles revive the Hafsid caliphal memory as an ideological resource, citing the centuries when Tunis was the western caliphal capital, the Ifrīqiyan hegemony that our forerunners maintained from Constantine to Tripoli, and the universal sovereignty claims that distinguished our ancestors from any contemporaneous Maghrebi dynasty. Our pamphleteers invoke the precedent against the encroaching foreign centers of authority, and official histories foreground the Hafsid caliphal era over the intervening centuries. Our modernist ulama trace our reform program's legitimacy through this restored caliphal lineage. The revival of dynastic memory gives the original Tunis line an ideological inheritance that purely modernist reform movements elsewhere lack.

TUN.name: Connections with the Christian World
TUN.desc: The Hafsid sultans have maintained continuous commercial and diplomatic relations with Pisa, Genoa, Venice, Aragon, and Provence since the thirteenth century, signing successive capitulations that grant European merchants resident factors at Tunis and La Goulette. Our court receives Christian envoys with the same protocol that we extend to fellow Muslim sovereigns, and our customs revenue from Italian trade alone funds a third of the central treasury. Pragmatic engagement with Christian Europe makes Tunis commercially and diplomatically flexible, as the more isolationist Maghrebi states are not.

TUN.name: Export Monopolies
TUN.desc: The bey holds Crown monopolies on the export of olive oil, woolen textiles from Sfax, henna and indigo Dyes, and the dried fish of the Tunisian banks, all staples that no Mediterranean market can fully replace from elsewhere. Our state warehouses concentrate these goods before they reach foreign factors, and our pricing committees set rates that Italian and Provençal buyers must accept or do without. Crown export monopolies fill the central treasury with a stable income in foreign coin, steadier than fluctuating caravan revenues.

TUN.name: Fundamental Pact
TUN.desc: The 'Ahd al-Amān (the security pact that our bey proclaims under reformist pressure) guarantees equality before the law for Muslims, Christians, and Jews, the inviolability of person and property under judicial process, and the formal codification of taxation and conscription procedures that the prior regimes left to discretionary practice. Our reformist drafters, drawing on Tanzimat and European precedents but framing the document in classical Arabic-Islamic legal terms, secure its endorsement from both the Zaytuna ulama and the Bardo court. Our bey now rules by written law, while the Maghrebi and Ottoman courts around us still govern by custom and decree.

TUN.name: Hafsid Continuity
TUN.desc: Our Husaynid beys claim direct dynastic legitimacy succession from the original Hafsid line, citing genealogical chains compiled by our court scholars, ceremonial titulature preserved across the Ottoman-regency interregnum, and the formal continuity of palace office that the Bardo administrators trace back through the deys to the last Hafsid sultans. Our investiture ceremonies, our diplomatic credentials, and our court historians' chronologies all affirm this Hafsid-Husaynid continuity as the foundation of our legitimacy. The line of Hafsid kings runs unbroken through us, and no rival regency can point to an older dynasty.

TUN.name: Hafsid Ghulām
TUN.desc: The Hafsid Ghulām are the slave-soldier corps of Hafsid Tunis: Black African captives from the trans-Saharan markets, Iberian prisoners from corsair raids, and children of earlier ghulām born to the institution and bound to the throne. They are the disciplined counterweight to the restless Banū Hilāl tribal levies.

TUN.name: Hafsid Imperial Axis
TUN.desc: Our hegemony stretches across the Ifrīqiyan lands (Tunis, Bougie, Constantine, Tripoli) administered through a network of governor cousins, tribute-paying Banū Hilāl tributaries, and resident Christian-merchant factor houses whose customs revenue funds the central treasury. Our distance administration relies on signal towers along the coast, paid couriers on inland routes, and a customary code that grants regional governors broad latitude in exchange for promptly remitted tribute. A chain of governors from Tunis to Tripoli carries the original Tunis line's imperial reach across Ifrīqiya, one that no successor government fully restores.

TUN.name: Husaynid Dynasty
TUN.desc: Our dynasty, founded by Ḥusayn ibn 'Alī (an officer of Cretan-Anatolian descent risen through the deylical hierarchy), consolidates the bey's authority over the Janissary corps, the dey, and the pasha, replacing the rotating officer governance of the prior generations with a hereditary line. Our successive beys appoint mamluk advisors trained from boyhood in the Bardo Palace. Administrative reforms centralize the tax farms under direct beylical control, and our diplomatic correspondence with Istanbul recognizes Ottoman sovereignty in form while exercising autonomous power in fact. Dynastic consolidation gives our state a coherent and continuous administration across generations, which no succession of rotating officers could supply.

TUN.name: Khaldunid Circle
TUN.desc: The Tunis court of our sultans patronizes 'Abd ar-Raḥmān ibn Khaldūn during his formative years (the philosopher-historian whose Muqaddima lays the foundations of social and historical analysis a century before any European parallel), alongside the wider circle of Andalusi refugee scholars, North African qadi-historians, and visiting Eastern ulama who pass through our capital. Our court librarians compile the genealogies, our administrative archives preserve the chancery records that later historians draw on, and our patronage of Ibn Khaldūn's contemporaries makes Tunis a magnet for scholarly correspondence across the Muslim world. The Khaldunid intellectual flowering leaves the original Tunis line a cultural inheritance that no other Maghrebi court can claim for the period.

TUN.name: La Goulette Defense
TUN.desc: Our state navy and our garrison at La Goulette resist the successive Habsburg-Ottoman intrusions that the gunpowder Mediterranean brings: Khayr ad-Dīn Barbarossa's first occupation, Emperor Charles V's restoration of our sultan, and the long war of attrition that follows. Our chief admirals and Tunis qasba commanders fortify the harbor's seaward approaches. Court diplomats play the rival empires against each other to preserve dynastic autonomy, while resident Andalusi engineers redesign our cannon batteries to the latest specifications. The Hafsid anti-imperial defense leaves the original Tunis line a defensive military inheritance that successor regimes can draw on.

TUN.name: Tunisian Corsairs
TUN.desc: The corsair captains of Tunis and La Goulette have hunted Christian shipping in the central Mediterranean since the late Hafsid century, operating under state charter alongside Christian renegades, Greek captains turned Muslim, and adventurers from every Mediterranean port who find refuge and employment in our service. Our shipyards at Bizerte and Porto Farina maintain the swift ṣḵīrah galleys that both native and foreign-recruited captains employ, and the slave markets at Tunis re-export captives across the Maghreb and into the Ottoman world. This state-sponsored privateering, drawing on both Tunisian-born and renegado talent, gives Tunis a fleet of effective war galleys and a sailor pool that no Maghrebi treasury could otherwise afford to maintain.

TUN.name: 'Ifrīqiya, Reunited
TUN.desc:
The decentralization of the has been addressed at its core. The era of the Hafsid Familial Governor is over, and all of 'Ifrīqiya stands reunited under the banners of the. No longer will the countryside be brutalized by rampant crime; no longer will the emirs be blackmailed by the Nobility; no longer will the state be dependent on the support of foreign actors.

It is a time of reckoning for the old order, and a great opportunity for us to usher in a new era.

TUN.name: Ahl al-Ḥall wa-l-'Aqd
TUN.desc: The Ahl al-Ḥall wa-l-'Aqd — those who loosen and bind — are the body of jurists, scholars, and senior notables whose collective consensus has traditionally conferred legitimacy upon Islamic rulers, their opinion standing as the community's endorsement of sovereignty. We convene this council as the formal deliberative institution of our realm, giving the 'ulamā' and the leading houses a structured voice in the affairs of state. A well-supported council translates scholarly authority into durable legitimacy; without the resources to maintain it, its rulings carry less weight, and the consensus that sustains our authority becomes harder to summon.

TUR.name: Coffee House Espionage
TUR.desc: Coffee houses and other urban meeting places are major hotspots for subversive activities. By seeding these places with our loyal spies and informants, we can better safeguard state security.

TUR.name: Enderûn
TUR.desc: The Interior Service is a complex branch of the household. Divided into the Privy Chamber, the Treasury, the Privy Larder, and the Great and Little Chambers, its ranks consist of a motley crew of eunuchs, slaves, and other little-noticed members of the royal household, who can sometimes wield remarkable influence over the inner workings of the state.

TUR.name: Eunuch Viziers
TUR.desc: Skilled eunuch servants can be granted powerful positions such as Black Chief Eunuch, Kızlar Ağası, and White Chief Eunuch, Kapı Ağası. In these roles, they are responsible for communications between the ruler and the, as well as administration of the harem and pages, supervision of waqf foundations, and the education of princes, among many other things. Considered more trustworthy than their intact peers, they can be relied on to always work for the benefit of the state.

TUR.name: Expanded Timar System
TUR.desc: The system with landed Sipâhi supplying the bulk of our cavalry has been expanded, assigning them vast tracts of conquered land on which to continue amassing cavalry.

TUR.name: Imperial Harem
TUR.desc: The Imperial Harem is much more than a collection of enslaved beauties at the ruler's beck and call - it is an institution parallel to the Interior Service, with its own organization, education, and protocols. Though those in the harem must work behind the scenes, they can sometimes wield great influence, turning the tides of state with merely a whisper in the right ear.

TUR.name: Legacy of Osman
TUR.desc: The Legacy of Osman is a tradition of divine right to expand under the central religious and political authority of our supreme leader. We invoke the Legacy to justify our continued conquests, maintain dynastic legitimacy across diverse holdings, and create an empire where our conquered peoples are not merely subjugated, but fully absorbed. Failure to uphold the Legacy can be seen as a betrayal to our people's traditions.

TUR.name: Malikâne
TUR.desc: A reform to the Muqāta'ah system, Malikâne allows tax farmers to purchase lifelong contracts for tax collection rights in the areas they farm. This provides them with more security and incentivizes long-term investment in their region's overall economic development. The drawback of this system is that maintaining rule of law over these lifetime grants will become more difficult.

TUR.name: Niẓām-i Jedīd
TUR.desc: A radical military reform, the New Order Army relies heavily on foreign instructors and Western tactics and weapons, as well as reorganizing the artillery corps. May it lead us to new victories, and further diminish the troublesome influence of the moribund Janissaries.

TUR.name: Sekban System
TUR.desc: Sekban soldiers are recruited in large numbers from the Burghers, and financed by a special tax called the Sekban Aqçesi. Typically fighting as infantry armed with muskets, they form the new core of the army, but are perpetually at odds with the Janissaries.

TUR.name: Timar System
TUR.desc: A system of feudal land holdings focused on building a formidable cavalry force. Our Sipâhi cavalrymen will be assigned land grants and obligated to provide cavalry forces proportional to the size of their holdings.

TUR.name: Autonomous Kadiluks
TUR.desc: Qāḍī should be given greater power within their alloted Kadiluk jurisdictions, to better utilize their wisdom for the benefit of the state.

TUR.name: Ayan Notables
TUR.desc: No one knows the complex power dynamics of far-flung provinces better than the elites who already reside there. Given status as Ayans, they are trusted to govern with only limited oversight from the state.

TUR.name: Ghazi Lords
TUR.desc: Warriors for the faith, these devoted fighters campaign across distant frontiers in pursuit of plunder, honor, and divine purpose. Comprised of zealous volunteers and tribal raiders, they guard our borders through relentless raids and conquests, spreading both influence and fear in equal measure.

TUR.name: kanun‐i Osmani
TUR.desc: A collection of legislations that together make up the laws of Ottomans, focused on providing internal stability for the numerous ethnicities rather than on conquering new lands.

TUR.name: Janissary Arquebusiers
TUR.desc: The Janissaries are the elite corps only loyal to the Sultan himself. Their ranks are made up through the Devşirme System of child levy and go through strict military training. As such, the Janissaries are the most disciplined forces of the Empire.

TUR.desc: The Janissaries are the elite corps only loyal to the Sultan himself. Their ranks are made up through the Devşirme System of child levy and go through strict military training. As such, the Janissaries are the most disciplined forces of the Empire.

TUR.name: Ahidnâme
TUR.desc: Also called capitulations, the Ahidnâme are contractual agreements with other nations, drawing upon both Muslim and secular law. Ahidnâme are most often used for guaranteeing the protection and rights of foreign merchants and clergy within our lands, ensuring that justice is upheld and trade can flow unhampered.

TUR.name: Autonomous Pashas
TUR.desc: Balancing local needs versus national interests is one of the most difficult aspects of government. Given the slow pace of communications, it can take a long time for the most basic directives to reach even relatively close provinces. We must encourage local governors towards more autonomy to ensure that local interests are served in a timely manner.

TUR.name: Azeb Irregulars
TUR.desc: Unmarried youths drafted from the poorest segments of society, the Azebs will not only function as soldiers and sailors, but also builders, sappers and armorers. Through a system of fortress garrisons, we will ensure that they always get paid.

TUR.name: Bashi-bazouks
TUR.desc: Unruly irregulars recruited from disenfranchised segments of the population, and sometimes outright vagabonds, the bashi-bazouks provide an affordable way of garrisoning forts and outposts. With their proclivity for brigandage and wanton killing, they can always be relied upon to disturb the enemy's frontier.

TUR.name: Birûn
TUR.desc: The Birûn, or the Exterior Service, comprises the group of administrators, military officers and religious scholars just outside the ruler's personal inner circle. Together, they make up an efficient bureaucracy inherited from Persia and the Great Seljuks, but adapted further by elements from Byzantium, making it uniquely Ottoman indeed.

TUR.name: Dragomans
TUR.desc: Interpreters, translators, and guides in one, the Dragomans are skilled officials who work to enhance our diplomatic and commercial efforts with different communities and countries. Most dragomans are of Greek ancestry, though some hail from Jewish, Armenian, or other multilingual backgrounds.

TUR.name: Ghazi
TUR.desc: In keeping with steppe traditions, our nobles are warriors of the frontier, and we shall be fearless in the fight to expand the Abode of Islam.

TUR.name: Imperial School of Naval Engineering
TUR.desc: This new school, Mühendishane-i Bahr-i Hümâyûn, will help us train shipwrights, naval officers, and sailors for both the navy and the merchant fleet.

TUR.name: Janissaries
TUR.desc: Janissaries are the elite units of our armies, trained since childhood and forged through discipline.

TUR.name: Janissary Arquebusiers

TUR.desc: The Janissaries are the elite corps only loyal to the Sultan himself. Their ranks are made up through the Devşirme System of child levy and go through strict military training. As such, the Janissaries are the most disciplined forces of the Empire.

TUR.name: Kafes
TUR.desc: By keeping our unruly princes confined to a special part of the harem, the Kafes, we can prevent wanton rebellions and the rivalry between brothers that used to plague our regime.

TUR.name: Kanunnames
TUR.desc: By establishing unique codes of law in each of our empire's provinces, we can ensure that our rule will be viewed as equitable and just. These law books, known as Kanunname, will take into consideration the local circumstances and traditions of each of our diverse and far-flung provinces.

TUR.name: Khedivates
TUR.desc: Large empires are usually formed around a core territory, and otherwise surrounded by subject nations of somewhat dubious loyalty. We should take the necessary measures to keep these nations under our surveillance.

TUR.name: Menzil
TUR.desc: A complex system of supply depots and lodgings for use by soldiers and officials, menzil waystations allow our armies to rely less on plunder, and remain well-supplied on every frontier.

TUR.name: Muqāta'ah
TUR.desc: A system of tax farming where nobles purchase the right to collect revenue from parcels of land owned by the state. Muqāta'ah balances the distribution of wealth across the empire, and turns the nobility away from corruption, giving them a vested interest in supporting the state.

TUR.name: Mālīye
TUR.desc: A vast, diverse, and highly organized bureaucracy staffed by the most skilled of scribes, the Mālīye aspires to be a fundamental and incorruptible institution of the state.

TUR.name: Seljuk Heritage
TUR.desc: To embrace the future, we must remember what we learned from Persia and the Great Seljuks, and build a state that can unite disparate peoples and beliefs into a greater whole.

TUR.name: The Legal Code of Suleiman
TUR.desc: Suleiman is remembered as one of the great rulers of history, a soldier, a lawmaker, and a reformer. In fact, while the West knows him as Suleiman the Magnificent, in his homeland, he is called 'The Lawgiver'. Central to his reforms was the re-examination of Ottoman dynastic law, Kanun, in order to bring it in line with Sharī'ah.

TUR.name: Timariots
TUR.desc: By offering Timar land grants to Sipâhi cavalrymen, they can use this new state-sponsored wealth to supply themselves and their retinue. This allows us to field more formidable cavalry forces.

TUR.name: Tulip Period
TUR.desc: We will reform old and stagnant traditions, plant tulips in all gardens, and usher in a new golden age of commerce and connection.

TUR.name: Turkic Traditions
TUR.desc: We hail from the steppes. The wind, the hardships, and the thrill of battle will always be in our blood, and we must never forget them.

TUR.name: Âyan
TUR.desc: Âyan are provincial magnates of diverse backgrounds that wield significant local autonomy, but still provide a ready source of tax farming income and military forces for the state.

UBV.name: Upper Bavarian Land Rights
UBV.desc: The 'Upper Bavarian Land Rights' is a collection of old Bavarian legal codes which codifies many common practices within Bavaria. It also sets and defines the role of the Nobility in Bavaria's court and covers administrative matters of the state.

UBV.name: An Army for Bavaria
UBV.desc: Only with a formidable standing army will we have the military might necessary to match our ambitions. With careful focus, we can expand it without having a ruinous impact on our state's finances.

UBV.name: Bavaria Coin
UBV.desc: Our realm needs a new standardized coin to serve as our national unified currency. Establishing a state-owned mint in our capital would ensure our total control over this new coinage.

UBV.name: Bavarian Cultural Institutions
UBV.desc: With our homeland at the feet of the beautiful Alps, we are a destination for artists from all over Europe, who seek inspiration in our incredible landscape. If we were to construct and support the appropriate cultural institutions, we could refine our court into a center of refinement and elegance, one that could rival even the most prestigious powers of Europe.

UBV.name: Bavarian Dukedom
UBV.desc: We have been granted the rulership of Bavaria directly by the Emperor! By embellishing ourselves as the divinely-appointed protectors of Bavaria, we will ensure our legitimacy cannot be questioned.

UBV.name: Bavarian Hofkriegsrat
UBV.desc: Establishing a council with the sole duty of advising our ruler during times of conflict will help us develop a more capable fighting force.

UBV.name: Bavarian Imperial Knights
UBV.desc: Our nobles have distinguished themselves as formidable knights in the service of the Holy Roman Empire. We should nurture and scrupulously maintain these troops to ensure the survival of our ducal integrity.

UBV.name: Bavarian Purity Law
UBV.desc: The excellent quality of our beer has been celebrated for centuries, but for our brews to achieve legendary status, we must ensure their continued prestige and superiority for all time. Several rulers in the past have created regulations and standards for the brewing of this wonderful substance; and we could use this fact as a stamp of our breweries' quality.

UBV.name: Dreams of Unification
UBV.desc: We once were ruled by Bavaria, unified in culture and allied under a single banner. We must ensure that the new Bavarian state is equally mighty, a home worthy of its strong and proud people.

UBV.name: One Faith for Bavaria
UBV.desc: We must ensure our people remain united in their faith, and that they will not be divided by heretical thoughts.

UBV.name: Practical Diplomacy
UBV.desc: No matter if we are answering to an Imperial overlord or cozying up to a potential foreign ally, our diplomats must be prepared for everything. But only if they keep Bavarian interests first and foremost in their efforts will we be able to claim true success in our diplomatic maneuverings.

UBV.name: Skilled Brewers
UBV.desc: Our lands are rich in the crops and fresh water required to brew beer, and our people readily enjoy this abundance. Many small breweries could grow into successful businesses, with the right support.

UBV.name: Trading Hubs of Bavaria
UBV.desc: Our lands are frequently crossed by merchants wishing to trade Salt, Silver, and Livestock in the rich lands to our south. We would be foolish not to take advantage of their presence, and therefore will establish bustling trade hubs in our own lands to attract their business.

URB.name: The Ceramics Guilds
URB.desc: The potters and painters of our city have developed a tradition of tin-glazed maiolica whose vivid colors and intricate scenes are sought by collectors and courts across the continent. Our ceramic guilds guard and transmit their techniques across generations, ensuring that the quality which made our name endures. This craft industry exports our culture in every painted dish and decorated vessel that leaves our workshops.

URB.name: The Enlightened University
URB.desc: Our university has endured through changes of government and the upheavals of the ages, continuing to draw students and scholars to our city by the reputation of its teaching. The long tradition of learning established in our most glorious days has become a living institution that carries that spirit forward into a new era. This continuity of scholarship is our gift to the future and our connection to the greatness of our past.

URB.name: The Hill Fortresses
URB.desc: The hilltops of our domain have been fortified over many generations, turning every elevated town into a position that would take a determined army weeks to reduce. Our soldiers learn their craft on these steep approaches and defend positions where a small garrison can hold off a much larger force. The Hill Fortress network of our territory is both our shield and the school in which our military tradition is trained.

URB.name: The Ideal Court
URB.desc: Our court has been called the most perfectly ordered in all of Italy, and men of learning and artistic ambition travel great distances to take part in its life. The conversations, performances, and works of art we foster here have inspired accounts of what a Perfect Court might look like, and those accounts have spread our reputation far beyond our borders. This refinement of governance and culture is the greatest thing we have built.

URB.name: The Mathematical School
URB.desc: We have nurtured a tradition of mathematical and philosophical inquiry that has made our city known throughout Europe for the precision of its thinkers. The Mathematical School of our court has produced translations, commentaries, and original works that advance the sciences and win us admiration from the finest universities. A commitment to learning opens our citizens' minds and sharpens our ability to understand and shape the world.

URB.name: The Montefeltro Seignory
URB.desc: We rule these hilltop towns and valleys as lords whose authority is ancient and whose right to govern has never been successfully challenged. Our people know that the Montefeltro have always defended their lands and their customs, and that loyalty has built a bond between lord and subject stronger than any decree. This seignory is not merely power over a territory but a compact that both sides have chosen to honor.

URI.name: Eternal Alliance of the Forest Cantons
URI.desc: We have forged an eternal alliance with our friends in the neighboring Cantons. Had it not been for this treaty, we would have surely succumbed to the Habsburg invaders and fallen under the rule of foreign tyrants yet again. These alliances will ensure our survival for centuries to come.

UTR.name: A Blessed Land
UTR.desc: The Pope himself influences the election of our Prince-Bishop, challenging the traditional five-chapter election format that we had before. This is clear proof that our land has been divinely blessed!

UTR.name: Skilled Diplomats
UTR.desc: Given the growing influence of our neighbors, our nation's survival depends on our ability to find loyal, powerful allies who will support us in our times of need.

UTR.name: The City of Churches
UTR.desc: Utrecht, often called the City of Churches, is home to the iconic Dom Tower. The spiritual center of the Netherlands and the seat of the Bishopric of Utrecht, it has been a beacon of faith since antiquity.

VEN.name: Magistrato alla Sanità
VEN.desc: No city in Europe has confronted the threat of epidemic with more rigor than Venice, and the permanent Magistrato alla Sanità we have established is the most sophisticated public health institution in the world — staffed by physicians, notaries, and inspectors all bound to report the first signs of contagion to a central authority. When plague appears at our borders, the Magistracy holds the power to quarantine arriving ships in the lagoon for forty days, a measure we call quarantina, and impose penalties on anyone who conceals sickness. This system has spared Venice from catastrophes that have emptied rival cities, and it keeps our workforce, our merchants, and our fleet healthy enough to sustain trade even as disease sweeps across the peninsula.

VEN.name: Monte Nuovo
VEN.desc: The original lending system in Italy was a joint stock fund called Monte Vecchio, in which each citizen was required to lend a certain amount of money in exchange for interest. But with this updated iteration, our bankers have introduced a guaranteed minimum interest payment to lenders, which has increased the amount of money people are willing to invest. This 'Monte Nuovo' has been extremely successful, and should prove extremely lucrative over time.

VEN.name: Promissione Ducale
VEN.desc: The Promissione Ducale serves as the formal oath of office and contractual agreement that each newly elected Doge of Venice must swear to uphold.

VEN.name: Provveditori ai Beni Inculti
VEN.desc: The mainland territories of the terraferma hold agricultural potential that poor drainage, neglect, and feudal indifference have left unrealized — marshes that could be grain fields, river banks that flood each spring and wash away the labor of the season before. We have established the Provveditori ai Beni Inculti with the authority to commission drainage canals, enforce irrigation schemes, and compensate landowners whose cooperation the works require. This systematic land improvement has extended the productive capacity of our wealthiest agricultural regions, giving Venice a food surplus that keeps the city fed even when sea trade is disrupted by war or blockade.

VEN.name: Standardized Relazioni
VEN.desc: The 'Relazioni' are the reports our ambassadors send to the government, detailing the political, financial, and social state of the countries they serve in.

VEN.name: Galleys
VEN.desc: Galleys form the backbone of our national and commercial security. As such, a great focus of our naval and military tactics revolve around how to use our finest galleys to best any kind of naval foe.

VEN.name: Gotico Fiorito
VEN.desc: The great palaces rising along our canals embody an architecture wholly our own, borrowing the pointed arch of the Gothic north, the open loggia of the Byzantine east, and the delicate tracery of Islamic craftsmen, fused into the style we call Gotico Fiorito. Nowhere else in Italy does a merchant's wealth announce itself so confidently in stone and carved marble, and the Palazzo Ducale and the Ca' d'Oro stand as proof that our republic can raise monuments as magnificent as any king's. This architectural tradition reinforces the standing of our patrician class, making the physical face of Venice inseparable from the prosperity and civic pride that sustains it.

VEN.name: Il Ridotto
VEN.desc: In 1638 the Great Council of Venice took the unprecedented step of licensing a permanent public gambling house in the Palazzo Dandolo, creating the Ridotto, the first state-supervised casino in Europe. Admission required a mask and a patrician's hat, which gave the establishment the appearance of equality while ensuring that the proceeds flowed reliably to the treasury and the behavior of the nobility remained visible to the state. This managed institution transformed a vice the Republic could not suppress into a dependable source of revenue and a mechanism for keeping the city's most powerful men where they could be watched.

VEN.name: La Fenice
VEN.desc: The Teatro La Fenice (the Phoenix) opened its doors in 1792 as the grandest opera house in Italy, built to replace a theater lost to fire and named for the bird that rises from its own ashes, a symbol that would prove grimly prophetic more than once. Its gilded interior, its boxes arranged by rank, and its season of premieres turned opera from aristocratic private entertainment into the defining cultural event of a city that had run out of military victories but not beauty. Every night the theater displays the Republic's taste, wealth, and ambition to an audience of nobles, travelers, and critics whose admiration travels further than any diplomatic dispatch.

VEN.name: Printing Industry
VEN.desc: When Aldo Manuzio established the Aldine Press in Venice in 1494, we became the printing capital of the world almost overnight; our merchants had the gold to finance it, our scholars the Greek and Latin to edit it, and our trade routes to carry the finished books to every court in Europe. The italic typeface, the affordable pocket octavo, and the authoritative editions of Plato, Aristotle, and Virgil that Aldo produced set a standard that no press on the continent has since matched. Mastery of the book trade extends the reach of Venice far beyond what our galleys can carry, and the ideas that flow from our presses become as valuable as the spices in our warehouses.

VEN.name: Stato da Mar
VEN.desc: From the days of the earliest Doge, Venice has built its power on the mastery of the sea; our merchants carry the riches of the East through the Adriatic while the Stato da Mar, our network of overseas ports and islands, secures the routes that sustain it all. At the heart of this maritime order stands the Arsenale, the greatest industrial complex of the medieval world, capable of launching a fully fitted galley in a single day when the Republic demands it. This combination of merchant dominance, state shipyard, and overseas empire makes Venice unlike any landlocked rival, transforming the sea itself into an extension of our state.

VEN.name: Venetian School of Music
VEN.desc: The twin choir lofts of San Marco, facing each other across the golden nave, gave birth to the Cori Spesâi (Cori Spezzati in standard Italian: Divided Choirs) technique, two ensembles answering and overlapping in a controlled interplay of sound that only the basilica's extraordinary acoustics can fully realize. Adrian Willaert, the Gabrielis, and Claudio Monteverdi all worked within this tradition, and the musicians they trained carried the Venetian polyphonic style to courts from Madrid to Vienna. This school of music makes Venice the acknowledged capital of European sound, and the stream of composers and singers our city produces carries Venetian prestige to places our galleys never reach.

VEN.name: Establish the Signoria of Venice
VEN.desc: The old Commune of Venice serves its purpose and has its long tradition within our state. However, its administrative efficiency is showing its age. We might want to rework the supreme body of government and replace it with a new system which leads solves the domestic problems of the nation.

VER.name: Court of Great Refugees
VER.desc: Dante Alighieri spent years of his exile walking our streets, and his presence drew others: poets, scholars, and master builders who found in Verona's Roman ruins and abundant stone a city still worth adding to. We extend this tradition of welcome into deliberate policy, offering patronage to displaced talent and drawing the finest craftsmen to the ancient workshops of the Marmorina, where the stonecutting skills of generations meet the fresh techniques that newcomers bring from across Italy. Our reputation for hospitality draws artists of unusual quality and gives our ambitious construction projects a depth of skilled labor, with stone and talent both close at hand.

VER.name: Gateway of the Alps
VER.desc: Verona sits at the point where the road from the Brenner Pass descends into the Po plain, making whoever holds our city the keeper of the most traveled route between Italy and the German lands. We have rebuilt our walls with the full depth of bastioned fortification and maintained the largest permanent garrison in northern Italy. This position means that any army moving south must either take Verona first or leave a hostile city at its back, and we intend to make both choices expensive.

VER.name: Perpetual General Captain of the People
VER.desc: The Scaligeri have claimed the title of Capitano del Popolo not as a temporary office but as a permanent grant rooted in commune law, framing every military campaign as the defense of civic rights rather than dynastic ambition and making it far harder for rivals to cast our wars as mere aggression. Cangrande della Scala built his reputation on exactly this legitimacy (riding out against Milan, Venice, and Padua while presenting each conflict as a just cause) and we formalize his example by keeping the city's councils engaged in decisions that other lords make alone. This combination of legal standing and public mandate makes rivals reluctant to antagonize us openly, since any attack on Verona reads as an attack on the commune itself.

VER.name: Spettacoli dell'Arena
VER.desc: Verona's amphitheater is one of the finest surviving Roman monuments in Italy, and we have made it the stage for the greatest public Spettacoli in the north, bullfights, pageants, and civic competitions that draw crowds from Venice and the Terraferma for days at a time. No other city can offer this scale of spectacle inside ancient Roman stone, and the tradition has become inseparable from how Verona understands itself, a republic that still performs its identity before thousands of witnesses in a space built two thousand years ago. This reputation for public magnificence spreads our name across northern Italy and draws visitors whose spending and whose letters home do more for our standing than any envoy we could send.

VER.name: The Adige
VER.desc: The Adige runs from the Alps through the center of our city and down to the Adriatic, carrying grain, timber, and finished goods along a route that has been profitable since Roman times. We invest in improving the river landings, clearing the shallower stretches, and negotiating passage rights with the communes downstream, turning a natural advantage into a managed commercial system. The river trade fills our markets with goods from the mountains and brings our city a steady prosperity that rivals cannot easily cut off.

VER.name: The Grand Tour
VER.desc: Verona has become a destination that the educated aristocracy of Europe cannot complete their travels without visiting: English lords, French scholars, and German princes make their way to the Arena, the Roman theater, and the Gothic tombs of the Scaligeri, spending freely and writing the city into the correspondence of every court on the continent. Their accounts turn Verona into a byword for Italy's layered heritage, a city where Roman, medieval, and Renaissance civilization can be read in a single afternoon's walk through streets that belong to no single century. This steady stream of wealthy and influential visitors enriches our treasury, opens diplomatic conversations that our size alone would never invite, and builds a reputation for civilization that travels far ahead of our armies.

VIJ.name: Rajya
VIJ.desc: The Rajyas are the main provinces of the. These territories are each jointly governed by a military commander and a member of the ruling dynasty. Administration is carried out in the region's native language, which allows these laws to be implemented more effectively.

VIJ.name: Adroit Diplomacy
VIJ.desc: The numerous invaders of our Hindu people have shown time and time again the same weakness: the tendency to fight amongst themselves. We must be ready at all times to exploit this to our own ends.

VIJ.name: An Army for the City of Victory
VIJ.desc: For the City of Victory to be worthy of its name, we must have an army that can bring about these namesake triumphs. We will ensure our troops are well-trained and take great pride in their service.

VIJ.name: Arabian Horses
VIJ.desc: Horses from Arabia are far superior to our local breeds. We will use our trade connections to ensure that we have a steady supply for our military.

VIJ.name: Carnatic Music
VIJ.desc: We must resist the Muslim invasion on all fronts. The musical traditions of the Northern States are already showing signs of foreign influence. This is blasphemy, because we all know that music is a divine art form that originated with the Devas and Devis themselves. We will show the Hindu people that we are committed to defending this holy art form.

VIJ.name: City of Victory
VIJ.desc: Vijayanagar — the 'City of Victory' — is the heart of our state, and will one day become the heart of the entire Hindu. Let it shine as a beacon of culture and tradition even as it fends off the Muslim invaders!

VIJ.name: Cultural Integration
VIJ.desc: The cultural diversity of India is one of our defining traits. By allowing our various settlements to rule by their own customs, we will assure their loyalty and integration into our society.

VIJ.name: Decentralized Rule
VIJ.desc: As our state grows, so do our administrative burdens on the government and the risk of revolt. To counteract this, we shall establish a system of decentralized rule, where settlements can manage their own minor issues, only seeking intervention from the central court for severe matters.

VIJ.name: First Indian Artillery
VIJ.desc: The military application of gunpowder is not yet widespread, but it has the potential to mold the future of warfare. We must explore the utility and benefits of gunpowder.

VIJ.name: Harsh Penal Code
VIJ.desc: Harsh punishments — including being put to death — are how we uphold law and order in this society. By establishing and strictly enforcing a harsh penal code, we ensure criminals fear the consequences of their actions, creating stability through the certainty of punishment.

VIJ.name: Indian Throne
VIJ.desc: India has been subject to Muslim threats for far too long. Heathen empires claim their rule from Delhi in the north, yet their beliefs and government are in direct opposition to what our people want. No, a new seat of power must be established — and Vijayanagar shall be the new Throne of India!

VIJ.name: Promotion of Trade
VIJ.desc: Our territory is situated on one of the key trade routes from East to West. We must ensure that our ports are safe and secure so that visiting captains will land there... giving us the opportunity to tax them.

VIJ.name: Rule According to Dharma
VIJ.desc: Dharma is a major pillar of our religious and social values. Our state can only be just and virtuous if our rulers themselves embody and live in accord with dharma.

VIJ.name: The Bunds
VIJ.desc: Our society is built on agriculture in the rather arid Karnakassala area. The bunds, also called anecut, provide our cities and fields alike with much-needed fresh water.

WBG.name: Fürspang Society
WBG.desc: The Gesellschaft mit dem Fürspang is an order of knights formed to defend their interests and provide assistance to those who sponsor them. Providing them with extensive funds will grant us significantly more political prowess within our region and within the Holy Roman Empire.

WBG.name: Fürspang Society
WBG.desc: The Gesellschaft mit dem Fürspang is an order of knights formed to defend their interests and provide assistance to those who sponsor them. Providing them with extensive funds will grant us significantly more political prowess within our region and within the Holy Roman Empire.

WLS.name: The Iron Ring
WLS.desc: Our entire administration is organized around maintaining the sheer number of castles that control our hills and valleys, making us one of the most fortified countries in the world.

YEM.name: Arabia Felix
YEM.desc: Ever since antiquity, Yemen has been known as 'Arabia Felix', the Fortunate Arabia. Blessed with a temperate highland climate and fertile soil in a sea of desert, it remains one of the most naturally prosperous regions of the peninsula. Let us nurture that prosperity and use it as the foundation of a thriving realm.

YEM.name: Coffea Arabica
YEM.desc: Though others have attempted to transplant our beloved bean, the Coffee of Arabia remains unmatched in flavor and fame. From the bustling port of Mocha to the courts of faraway rulers, the world's desire for our drink is insatiable.

YEM.name: Port of Aden
YEM.desc: The port of Aden has been a nexus of trade for millennia — its natural harbor welcoming ships from India, Egypt, and East Africa. If properly supported, it can once again become the cornerstone of our maritime economy and the pride of the Red Sea.

YEM.name: Rasulid Bureaucracy
YEM.desc: The Rasulid dynasty brought unprecedented administrative order to our lands. With census records, tax systems, and a robust cabinet structure, they transformed Yemen into one of the most efficiently governed realms in the region.

YEM.name: Red Sea Control
YEM.desc: Any and all trade from India and Africa must pass through the strait called Gate of Grief. Let us enforce our dominion over this maritime chokepoint and turn every passing ship into an opportunity.

YEM.name: Unite the Yemeni Tribes
YEM.desc: From the Tihāmah coast to the Ḥarāz mountains, our realm is home to countless fiercely independent tribes. While they have long resisted centralized authority, they are also our strength. By uniting them under a single cause, we can better utilize them as a workforce.

YEM.name: Zaydī Scholarly Traditions
YEM.desc: The highlands of Yemen have long been home to the Zaydī imamate, a center of learning and piety. Rooted in Islamic jurisprudence, theology, and rationalism, our scholars have ensured the rule of law and the moral integrity of our governance for centuries.

ZAB.name: Biskra Fair
ZAB.desc: The annual Biskra autumn fair, convening Saharan caravans from Touat, Sahel merchants from Constantine, sub-Saharan slave traders from the Niger bend, and Bedouin pastoralists from the steppe fringe, turns our oasis capital into a regional commercial hub for the autumn weeks. Pavilions host the negotiations. The customs house weighs and registers every transaction, and the merchant guild posts standard scales and assay weights to which all participants must conform. The Biskra fair draws the caravans together at set times and turns their natural meeting point into a market the state manages and taxes.

ZAB.name: Foggara Irrigation
ZAB.desc: The foggāra underground channel system, qanats dug under the desert sand to bring water from upland water tables to the oasis gardens, gets extended and renewed under our oasis council coordination, freeing new cultivable land from the older surface irrigation perimeter. Our guild of foggara diggers passes the channel construction technique through hereditary apprenticeship, our resident villages contribute corvée-labor for the cleaning rotations, and our oasis chamber arbitrates the share water disputes that the new channels inevitably generate. As the foggara spread, our oasis gains more cultivable land and more people than the rival oases that rely on surface irrigation.

ZAB.name: Raḥmāniyya Expansion
ZAB.desc: The Raḥmāniyya tariqa, founded by Sīdī Muḥammad ibn 'Abd ar-Raḥmān al-Azharī in the central Kabyle region and expanding southward through the Aurès foothills, establishes branch zawiyas across our oasis belt over the course of generations. Our resident shayḵs accept Raḥmāniyya initiation, our scholar families take students from the Kabyle and Algerian centers, and our merchant pilgrims maintain the correspondence across regions that binds the order's scattered lodges into one religious network. Through the Raḥmāniyya lodges, students and shayḵs pass freely between our oasis and the central Algerian highlands.

ZAB.name: Saharan Terminus
ZAB.desc: Our oasis sits at the northern terminus of the western Saharan caravan corridor. Caravans from Touat, Touggourt, and the central Sahara converge on Biskra before continuing north to Constantine and Tunis or east into Hafsid territory, while our merchant houses provision the southbound legs with grain, cloth, salt, and pottery from the Tell. Our caravanserais host sub-Saharan, Berber, and Maghrebi traders side by side; our customs officers tax through traffic at modest rates that keep the corridor profitable; and our diplomatic letters bind the caravan route's contributing tribes to our chamber arbitration. This place at the end of the desert road makes our oasis a city of merchants and envoys, as no purely agricultural oasis could be.

ZAB.name: Sidi Okba Shrine
ZAB.desc: The tomb of 'Uqba ibn Nāfi' (founder of Kairouan, who led the first Arab armies into the Maghreb and is buried at our southern village of Sidi Okba) anchors a sacred pilgrimage site whose religious authority predates every dynasty of the Maghreb. Our resident shrine keepers maintain the tomb, our annual pilgrimage draws zawaya scholars and notables from across the western Islamic world, and our ulema invoke the founder's authority in legal opinions that bind clients far beyond our actual political reach. The founding shrine gives our state a sacred claim to legitimacy, ancient and tied to the prophetic conqueror himself.

ZAB.name: Zibane Palmery
ZAB.desc: Our oasis belt, the Zībān palm gardens stretching from Biskra and Tolga through Sidi Okba and Bou Saada to Ouled Djellal, produces the dates that the Maghrebi and trans-Saharan markets specifically commission for their size, sweetness, and keeping qualities. Our orchard owners hold hereditary leases on individual palm plots, our irrigation guildsmen apportion well-water by ancient share tables, and our caravan masters price each consignment by origin grove and harvest year. The Zibane palm country supplies a luxury trade in dates that no broader fruit-growing region of the Maghreb can displace from the elite markets.

ZAN.name: Control of the Mahdali Coinage
ZAN.desc: The might of our dynasty is imprinted upon the coins that circulate the markets from the Italy coast, to India, and beyond. This trimetallic coin is primarily made of Copper, Silver, and Gold, and is the first of its kind to exert such influence on a multiregional scale. Control of its circulation is synonymous with continued prosperity!

ZAN.name: Kilwan Trade Communities
ZAN.desc: A series of loose confederations, often led by a governor that strengthens the power of local merchants, these communities push for local autonomy and urbanization. Their trading skills provide a steady stream of revenue for our treasuries.

ZAN.name: Kilwan Merchant Navy
ZAN.desc: Centuries of maritime wisdom and access to high quality cotton and lumber have given way to a most formidable merchant fleet. Equipped with cutting edge designs and new sail compositions, these vessels are the pride of our people.

ZAN.name: Kilwan Dhow
ZAN.desc: Known for their slender and elongated hull design, the Kilwan Dhow is famous for being the backbone of our maritime trade that connects our ports to faraway lands. The ship itself is a manifestation of our mastery of shipwright, as our workers utilize palm trees for a sturdy body as well as locally-grown cotton for the sails.

ZAN.name: Kilwan Zambuc
ZAN.desc: The Kilwan Zambuc is a smaller variation of the Kilwan Dhow, and it is primarily used for local trade, transportation of goods and pottery between the various city-states across the Swahili Coast, as well as serving as trustworthy faring vessels for short distances.

ZAN.name: Mtepe
ZAN.desc: One of the most common ship types and a predecessor to the standard Kilwan Dhow, the Mtepe is connected to Swahili as a steadfast cornerstone of their maritime prowess. Unlike the Kilwan Dhow, the Mtepe has a square stern and its core construction does not use nails. Instead, a sewn-plank construction is utilized, bonding the hull together. The primary role of the Mtepe is to navigate the shallow local waters and establish maritime trade across the coast of Africa.

ZAN.name: Bantu and Perso-Arabian
ZAN.desc: Ever since our descent from Arabia and Persia, we have established communities across the Swahili Coast that integrate the local Bantu in an effort to maintain social order and make way for the rise of new architectural and cultural advances.

ZAN.name: Diplomacy Through Trade
ZAN.desc: We are uniquely positioned at the confluence of wealth coming from China, India, and Europe. This not only benefits us financially, but it gives us great influence in the diplomatic game between Empires and foreign powers...

ZAN.name: Food Imports
ZAN.desc: The dawn of a new age in seafaring has given us new opportunities to seek sustenance for our people. Whereas once we would only trade with the interior of Africa to procure crucial supplies of Sturdy Grains, Livestock, and Rice, we can now access new ports where food may be cheaper and more readily available.

ZAN.name: Gold Trade of Africa
ZAN.desc: Our abundant reserve of Gold from many sources across East Africa is the cornerstone of our economy. We must take full advantage of our reserves, and use our wealth to support and disseminate a strong currency. This will help us develop as a trading hub.

ZAN.name: Kilwan Dhow
ZAN.desc: Known for their slender and elongated hull design, the Kilwan Dhow is famous for being the backbone of our maritime trade that connects our ports to faraway lands. The ship itself is a manifestation of our mastery of shipwright, as our workers utilize palm trees for a sturdy body as well as locally-grown cotton for the sails.

ZAN.name: Kilwan Trade Networks
ZAN.desc: Attracting merchants from as far away as Persia and Arabia, our capital has become a bustling commercial hub, facilitating business from the horn of Africa all the way to the shores of China.

ZAN.name: Kilwan Zambuc
ZAN.desc: The Kilwan Zambuc is a smaller variation of the Kilwan Dhow, and it is primarily used for local trade, transportation of goods and pottery between the various city-states across the Swahili Coast, as well as serving as trustworthy faring vessels for short distances.

ZAN.name: Latitude Staves
ZAN.desc: Our superior ship technology allows us to sail further and for longer than any of our competitors, giving us a significant edge in any seafaring activity.

ZAN.name: Palm Tree Masters
ZAN.desc: We may not have a very robust manufacturing industry, but one thing we do have in abundance are palm trees. Sturdy enough to support construction and shipwrighting, but flexible enough to be shaped by our artisans, mastering the use of this unique lumber will help us expand our seafaring activities, improve production, and ultimately line our pockets.

ZAN.name: Shirazi's Legacy
ZAN.desc: Our ancestral founder came from Širâz, son of the 'Amīr of Persia, which makes our right to rule undeniable.

ZAN.name: Zanj Taxation
ZAN.desc: Originally a term to describe the inhabitants of inner Africa, particularly those of Bantu origin, these folk make up a substantial portion of our demographics. While they have many liberties and responsibilities, they are taxed accordingly in order to preserve these privileges. Their peaceful, relatively autonomous place within our legal framework has led to the organic development of linguistic phenomena and new cultural traditions.

ZMW.name: Council of Senior Wives
ZMW.desc: This Council will offer us excellent advice, and involve the most skilled wives of our ruling class in the administration of our country.

ZMW.name: Royal Ownership of Cattle
ZMW.desc: The ownership of Livestock gives us much power, and controlling our country's cattle will help entrench our rule.

ZMW.name: Cow-Horn Formations
ZMW.desc: Adapting to the ever-changing tactics of war is no easy task. Against potentially superior enemies, we should rely on our own mobility over everything else. If we are able to pin our foes into a melee fight and send a regiment to flank and encircle their troops, we will be able to inflict devastating casualties.

ZMW.name: Empowering the Rozwi
ZMW.desc: Our lands are home to many skilled warriors. Among them are the Rozwi, disciplined fighters who stand ready to defend our people against any who would dare try to take our rightful lands from us.
